Non-zero while the player is in a transition between modes: player_fire does nothing, player_mode1_step goes straight to mode1_collide, and player_animate plays the frames at $04E8 and the boxes at $04EC for it, rewriting it as it steps ($9AE8, $9AEF). player_down_enter_mode1 sets $44, mode1_up_end sets 2, and the code at $9AF3 and $9B3D sets $80. mode1_collide clears a negative value; round_start, ground_floor_check, air_mode1_check and $9B8A also clear it.

Flag from the player's animation tables: non-zero puts the second body sprite 24 pixels to the right of the first, zero puts it 21 lines below (player_sprite_coords); player_pose also uses it to pick the mode 1 records in mode 0. Cleared by player_down_enter_mode1, and by player_animate while the player is hit.

Hold counter of the player's animation (with $0296 and $0903): player_animate counts it up while the action and facing stay the same and $0903 is 0, and does not count while bit 7 of move_dir $0D is set. It is reset to 0 when the state or facing changes, when $0903 is non-zero, and when it reaches its limit (3, 4 or 6 in the three animation routines, so it cycles). init_round_state clears it; the fire path ($B1E6) sets it to $FF.

Index of the current frame in the player's animation table: player_animate steps it by 2 and wraps it at the table length; player_pose uses it to pick the third sprite's offsets. player_fire sets $FE when a shot starts on the ground in mode 0 or in mode 1 with $0B non-zero, and 0 or 2 in mode 1 with $0B zero; player_land, init_round_state and $9B8D also set $FE. A negative value takes the first entry.

Restart request for the player's animation (with $0296 and $0901): while it is non-zero, player_animate restarts the animation, clearing $0901, and clears it. Set by player_fire ($80 on the ground in mode 0, $FE in mode 1 with $0B non-zero), the mode 1 fire code ($FF at $9039), jump_start_state, the code at $8DB3, mode1_up_end (1) and reserve_player_object_slots_loop (8).

Top of the saved-background stack cell_save_stack: the index where the next record goes, 0 when the stack is empty. The save routines add 5, 6 or 8; restore_saved_cells pops until it is 0; init_round_state clears it.

The action number of the player, which player_animate ($98F3) reads together with the facing flag $18. The movement code writes 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7: 4 by player_stop; 5 by mode 1's horizontal movement and by mode 0 code for pressing down, slopes and floors; 6 by mode 1's vertical movement and on entering mode 1; 7 in mode 2; and 3 for jumps and falls.
Right edge of the follow zone (16 bits, high byte $0907), in the sprite coordinates of player_screen_x. Loaded from bytes 2 and 3 of the section record.
High byte of zone_right ($0906).

Left edge of the zone in which the player can stand without the view following (16 bits, high byte $0909), in the sprite coordinates of player_screen_x. Loaded from bytes 0 and 1 of the section record by load_section_record.
High byte of zone_left ($0908).
Top edge of the follow zone, in the sprite coordinates of player_screen_y. Loaded from byte 4 of the section record.
Bottom edge of the follow zone, in the sprite coordinates of player_screen_y. Loaded from byte 5 of the section record.
The A register saved by irq_panel, which it restores before the RTI.
The X register saved by irq_panel.
The Y register saved by irq_panel.
The X register saved by irq_panel_on, which loads it back at the end of the interrupt.
Number of objects in platform_list ($74): update_objects clears it and counts the objects with bits 3 and 4 of obj_state set; platform_scan_next walks that many entries.
Set to $FF by init_round_state ($4F21); no code in the listing reads it.
Set to $FF by init_round_state ($4F24), next to $0911; no code in the listing reads it.
Non-zero when place_third_sprite shows the third sprite. Written in several places by the player routines.
Colour of the player's first body sprite; reserve_player_object_slots_loop sets 8 at the start of a round and place_player_sprites puts it in the logical sprite table.
Colour of the player's second body sprite (8 at the start of a round).
Colour of the player's third sprite: 8 at the start of a round; player_pose sets $0E while the effect flash is on. place_third_sprite writes it to hardware sprite slot 0.

Frame records read by player_pose, $0917-$0A4A. A record begins with the shape number of the third sprite, which is also the index into the hit box tables at $03F7-$0415, followed by four-byte entries: a signed 16-bit X offset and a signed 16-bit Y offset of the third sprite from the player, one entry for each animation frame (picked by anim_frame). The records for mode 1 also hold the body sprite shape numbers at bytes 9 and 10. The pointer tables at $0A4B-$0A9A point into these records. Fixed records are used without a table: $095D (facing right) and $0962 (left) for a player in the air in mode 0, and $0A29 (right) and $0A3A (left) in mode 2.

Table of 10 bytes indexed by aim_dir ($0297): low bytes of the addresses of the frame records for a standing player in mode 0 ($0299 = 0, $0900 = 0). player_pose reads the pair of tables and puts the address in $E1/$E2.
Table of 10 bytes indexed by aim_dir ($0297): high bytes for the standing player (all $09; see pose_still_lo, $0A4B). player_pose reads the pair of tables and puts the address in $E1/$E2.

Table of 10 bytes indexed by aim_dir ($0297): low bytes of the frame record addresses for the player in mode 0 when stance ($0299) is non-zero ($FF after player_stop or a step with down held, 1 after the mode 1 exit); a 0 entry would make player_pose fall back to a fixed record, but none is 0 (entries 0, 4, 5 and 9 hold $01, with high byte $00). player_pose reads the pair of tables and puts the address in $E1/$E2.

Table of 10 bytes indexed by aim_dir ($0297): high bytes for mode 0 with stance ($0299) non-zero (see pose_stance_lo, $0A5F); entries 0, 4, 5 and 9 are $00. player_pose reads the pair of tables and puts the address in $E1/$E2.

Table of 10 bytes indexed by aim_dir ($0297): low bytes of the frame record addresses in mode 1 when the player moves vertically ($0B = 0). player_pose reads the pair of tables and puts the address in $E1/$E2.
Table of 10 bytes indexed by aim_dir ($0297): high bytes for mode 1 vertical movement (see pose_vert_lo, $0A73). player_pose reads the pair of tables and puts the address in $E1/$E2.

Table of 10 bytes indexed by aim_dir ($0297): low bytes of the frame record addresses in mode 1 when the player moves horizontally ($0B non-zero), and in mode 0 when $0900 is non-zero. player_pose reads the pair of tables and puts the address in $E1/$E2.
Table of 10 bytes indexed by aim_dir ($0297): high bytes for mode 1 horizontal movement (see pose_horiz_lo, $0A87). player_pose reads the pair of tables and puts the address in $E1/$E2.

Load a set from the cartridge directory: copy entry X, then X+8, X+16 and on, until an entry whose flag bit 5 marks it packed; that one is unpacked in place by bank 0's unpacker at $8DA2, which returns to the caller (an entry with flag bit 7 would end the routine without unpacking; none has it). stage_start passes X from the per-stage table in bank 0 at $8127 ($88, $A0, $B8, $D0, $E8); game_init calls it with $80 and $60.

Start a stage: bring the cartridge into view ($01 = $37, bank 0), load the stage's set with stage_load, load directory entries 6 and 7, copy a page of bank 13 to $FD00, read the stage's record in bank 5 into $08E3-$08E6, point $3A and $3C at the tables named in the unpacked block's header ($0C1C, $0C1E), then hide the cartridge again.
Queue sound effect number A: unless $DF is non-zero, and while fewer than three effects are waiting, store it at $91 + $90 and add one to $90. Y is preserved (via $8F). sound_frame plays the queue.
Once a frame, from irq_panel: unless $DF is set, play each sound effect queued in $91 onward ($90 counts them) through $6633, then run the sound driver at $6787.
Fills sprite_y_buckets ($7CBD-$7D2C, 112 bytes) with $FF, which marks every position empty. finish_round_setup calls it.

Byte 1 of the stage block, which is loaded from $0C01 (saved value $38). game_init stores 7 here at $5245 at power-on, when $0C01 onward still holds the start-up stream (directory entries 12-15) it has just unpacked, before it calls the routine at $0C05; the stage block replaces it later. Nothing reads it in play.

Background colour 0 of the stage ($D021): stage_setup_tables copies this byte to bg_colour0. At power-on game_init also stores $8C here ($524A), into the start-up stream that the stage block later replaces.

Background colour 1 of the stage ($D022): copied to bg_colour1 by stage_setup_tables. At power-on game_init stores the value of zero-page $E0 here ($524F), into the start-up stream that the stage block later replaces.

Background colour 2 of the stage ($D023): copied to bg_colour2 by stage_setup_tables. At power-on, before any stage block is loaded, game_init calls a routine of the start-up stream that starts here ($5254).

Number of the last section of the stage: track_stage_section stops looking for the next section at this index. init_round_state reads the record of this last section to get its byte $18 into temp_first ($16).
Low byte of a pointer (high byte at $0C08) into the cartridge bank 0 to the 64 bytes of stream records that load_stage_bank_records copies to $0100.
High byte of the pointer at $0C07.
Low byte of a pointer (high byte at $0C0A) to the list of animation ids of the stage that the helper at $06E6 searches. The list's last index is in $0C0B.
High byte of the pointer at $0C09.
Index of the last entry of the list at ($0C09), used as the start of the backward search in the helper at $06E6.

The 22 bytes $0C0C-$0C21 are the stage's eleven table pointers; stage_setup_tables copies them to $2A-$3F (map_row_lo_ptr, map_row_hi_ptr, block_chars_ptr, block_props_ptr, path_table_ptr, $34, script_ptr_a, script_ptr_b, anim_lo_ptr, anim_hi_ptr and $3E). The values of the saved state are $190E, $1946, $0D32, $197E, $1FD1, $1FD6, $1B34, $1B71, $1AE3, $1AA1 and $1B25.
Low byte of the word that stage_start copies to anim_lo_ptr ($3A). It is also part of the table at $0C0C that stage_setup_tables copies.
High byte of the word at $0C1C (anim_lo_ptr).
Low byte of the word that stage_start copies to anim_hi_ptr ($3C).
High byte of the word at $0C1E (anim_hi_ptr). The bytes $0C20 and $0C21 hold the last pointer, copied to $3E.

Colour of each character code, 256 bytes, indexed by the character (screen code) found in the screen buffers. recolour_screen copies the entry for every one of the 840 playfield characters into colour RAM. Only the low nibble reaches colour RAM, and a value of 8 or more turns on multicolour for that character, since the playfield runs in multicolour text mode ($D016 bit 4).

Table of section record addresses: one word for each section of the stage (eight words, $0D22-$0D31, in the saved state: $19D9, $19F2, $1A0B and on, each 25 bytes on). store_section_index indexes it with section_index times 2, track_stage_section with the next and the previous section's index times 2, and init_round_state with the last section's ($0C06); stage_setup_tables reads the first word through $24. The low byte is here, the high byte at $0D23.
The high byte of the first section address, then the rest of the table (see section_table). From $0D32 on come the map blocks, four characters each, which block_chars_ptr points to.

The map block table: four screen characters for each block number (upper left, upper right, lower left, lower right), pointed to by block_chars_ptr ($2E). The first three blocks are blank; most later ones hold runs of consecutive character numbers, but many repeat character $16 or one character or pair, and blocks at $0E66-$0E77 are blank again. The table's length depends on the stage.

Map row address table, high bytes: 56 entries $1946-$197D, one for each row of the stage map. map_row_hi_ptr ($2C) points here in the saved state and stage_setup_tables copies the pointer from $0C0E. The low bytes are the 56 bytes at $190E; a row starts at hi:lo, so the first rows are $0E9E, $0ECD, $0EFC, 47 bytes (one row of 47 blocks) apart (later rows are 19, 25 or 59 bytes apart: rows differ in length), and the last high byte is $18. Only the first 56 bytes belong to this table; the bytes that follow are block_props_table.

Map block properties, one byte for each block number: 91 bytes $197E-$19D8 in the saved state, matching the 91 four-character blocks of block_chars ($0D32-$0E9D). block_props_ptr ($30) points here. Bit 0 solid, bit 1 harmful, bits 2 and 3 slopes, bit 5 enter mode 1, as block_property_at and the terrain probes test them. The saved state holds only the values $00, $01, $03, $04, $05, $10, $11, $20 and $30.

The eight section records of the stage, 25 bytes each, $19D9-$1AA0: section_table ($0D22) holds their addresses ($19D9, $19F2, $1A0B and on, 25 bytes apart). Each record begins with the follow zone (zone_left, zone_right, zone_top, zone_bottom) and the view limits that update_view_scroll reads through section_ptr ($26), and holds the flags byte at offset $16 (section_scroll_flags); the rest of the 25 bytes is not decoded here.

High bytes of the addresses of the stage's animation data blocks, 66 entries $1AA1-$1AE2 indexed by animation number; anim_hi_ptr ($3C) points here in the saved state. The low bytes are the 66 bytes of anim_lo_table at $1AE3. In the saved state the blocks lie at $20E0-$2876 (high bytes $20 to $28).

Entry 47 of anim_hi_table in the saved state ($22: animation 47 is at $220A). stage3_patch writes $C0 here and the type-8 object handler at $A82A writes $60, and each also writes the next byte (entry 48, $1AD1) with $00 or $01, so the pair is a 16-bit value ($00C0 or $0160) rather than two table entries. What reads it is not established.

Second byte of the pair written with $1AD0: stage3_patch stores $00 here and the object handler at $A82A stores $01 (so the pair is $00C0 or $0160, little-endian). In the saved state it is entry 48 of anim_hi_table ($22).

Low bytes of the addresses of the stage's animation data blocks, 66 entries $1AE3-$1B24, indexed by animation number; anim_lo_ptr ($3A) points here. The partner of anim_hi_table. stage3_patch overwrites entries 2 and 3 (at $1AE5 and $1AE6).
Entry 2 of anim_lo_table (saved state $F0, giving animation 2 the address $21F0). stage3_patch stores $10 here and $04 in the next byte, $1AE6.
Entry 3 of anim_lo_table (saved state $FD, animation 3 at $21FD). stage3_patch stores $04 here after $10 in $1AE5. Nothing else in the listing writes or reads it by address.

Fifteen bytes $1B25-$1B33, the stage's eleventh table, which $3E points to (stored by stage_setup_tables from $0C20): the hit reactions 0 and 1 ($A8FA, $A8D8) replace an object's obj_anim_num with the entry at that index, so it maps an animation number to the animation the object switches to when hit. The saved values are $22 to $37.

Low bytes of the addresses of the object movement scripts: 61 entries $1B34-$1B70, the table that script_ptr_a ($36) points to. object_script_step loads the pair (script_ptr_a, script_ptr_b) into $E3/$E4 and then reads the script byte at ($E3) + obj_script_pos ($379C,x). The high bytes are script_addr_hi.

High bytes of the addresses of the object movement scripts: 61 entries $1B71-$1BAD, the table that script_ptr_b ($38) points to; the low bytes are script_addr_lo. In the saved state the scripts lie between $1BAE and $1FD0 (high bytes $1B to $1F).

Object movement script bytes, first part, $1BAE-$1FAD (1024 bytes in the saved state). A byte below $80 is a command number: object_script_step looks it up in script_cmd_lo/hi at $B33C/$B35F and runs it; a byte with bit 7 set is a move (low four bits the direction, next byte the repeat count). Three words inside this area are rewritten by the stage patches: $1D08 and $1D0A (stage2_patch, then the handler at $A7F3) and $1D6A (stage2_common).

Low byte of a 16-bit word (high byte $1D09) in an object script, probably an X position in pixels. The saved stage 0 bytes are $0B and $FD. stage2_patch stores $00A0 (160) here when section_index is below 2; the type-7 object handler at $A7F3 later stores $0140 (320), at the same moment it clears two map blocks (row pointer entry $13, columns 40 and 41) that stage2_patch had filled with block $36. It reads as a gate that opens; that is inferred.
High byte of script_word_a: stage2_patch stores $00, the type-7 object handler at $A7F3 stores $01.
Low byte of a second 16-bit word in the same script (high byte $1D0B), written together with script_word_a: stage2_patch stores $00A0, the type-7 object handler at $A7F3 stores $01F0 (496).
High byte of script_word_b ($00 from stage2_patch, $01 from the handler at $A7F3). The script bytes after it, up to $1D69, are not decoded.

Low byte of a 16-bit word inside another script command (saved value $8724). stage2_patch (through stage2_common) stores $00 here and in $1D6B, for every section of stage 2. What the word controls is not established.
High byte of script_word_c ($87 in the saved state); stage2_common stores $00. The script bytes that follow, up to $1FAD, are not decoded.
Object movement script bytes, second part, $1FAE-$1FD0 (35 bytes); see script_data_a for the byte format.

Table of path data addresses that path_table_ptr ($32) points to, indexed by obj_arc_state: the bytes $1FD2-$1FDD hold six words, $1FDE, $201F, $2040, $2070, $20B0 and $2098. $1FD1 itself is $07 in the saved state. The pointer at $34 (copy of $0C16) is $1FD6, so the last four words are also the table that script command 22 ($B722) reads through ($34) at $B72D to find the record of an object it sets up; whether those four are also paths is not established.

Path data read by path_advance, from $1FDE: signed 16-bit words (low byte first) that are added to an object's X or Y position, step by step; a low byte of $80 sends the path back to its start. The first path ($1FDE-$201E) steps -2 four times, -1 three times, 0 twice, 1 three times, 2 eight times, then the same back down, an arc. From $2040 the area also holds the object records that script command 22 finds through ($34) ($2040, $2070, $2098, $20B0), so where the path data ends is not established. The saved state is the first stage; stage1_patch rewrites bytes $2018-$201A.

Low byte of a path data word ($2018-$2019). stage1_patch stores $00 here and in $201A and copies the byte at $202E into $2019, so in stage 1 the word at $2018 reads zero when $202E holds 0, as it does in the saved state. The saved stage 0 holds $FE, $FF, which is a step of -2.
High byte of the word at $2018. stage1_patch first loads it from $202E (saved value $00) and then, in the same routine, stores $00 at $2018 and $201A.
Byte $201A of the path data: stage1_patch stores $00 here (saved value $FE, the low byte of a -2 step).
Byte of the path data read by stage1_patch and copied to $2E87 (saved value $FF). It is the high byte of a -2 step in the saved state.
Byte of the path data read by stage1_patch and copied to $2019 (saved value $00).

Thirty-two bytes, the pixel rows of four characters (eight bytes each). When the stage is 0, patch_stage_code copies them to $C780-$C79F, which are the shapes of characters $F0 to $F3 in the character set at $C000, unless bit 5 of $35A8 is set, in which case it fills $C780-$C79F with $00 instead. Other stages leave $C780 as loaded.

Last (ninth) byte of the nine-byte frame record at $2136, the first frame of animation 13 ($2117): the saved state holds $BC, which patch_stage_code writes for stage 0 (it also writes $C1 to $2150). The same byte of the neighbouring records ($212D, $213F) holds $54 and $53, so it looks like a shape number (inferred).

Last (ninth) byte of the frame record at $2148, which animation 12 ($2122) uses for its second and third frames; set to $C1 by patch_stage_code for stage 0 (with $BC at $213E). Looks like a shape number (inferred).
One byte in the data block at $2D00-$2D4F, which looks like pairs of nibbles. stage1_patch stores $08 here (saved value $EB, the stage 0 byte). No routine in the listing reads it by address.
One byte inside a run of $55/$AA patterned bytes. stage1_patch copies the byte at $201B into it (saved value $55). No routine in the listing reads it by address.

A byte of a patterned data area at $30C0 that falls into 8-byte groups. stage2_tail stores $B7 here, $BC at $30D6 and $BD at $30DA (saved values $55, $02 and $55). No routine in the listing reads them by address; what they are is not established.
Byte patched to $BC by stage2_tail (saved value $02); see stage_data_30CA.
Byte patched to $BD by stage2_tail (saved value $55); see stage_data_30CA.

Hit points in the low five bits; the top three bits are kept when hit points are taken off, and the byte goes to add_score_points, whose top two bits choose the award class. Player shots take 1 hit point off (2 at weapon_level 1, $A707-$A71A), and the player landing on the object from a jump takes 2 off ($A5F9-$A60B, when bit 4 of obj_kind is set); see object_sprites_and_hits. track_stage_section shows the low five bits of object $08CC in gauge_value.

Motion byte of each stage object, chosen in update_objects ($A283). $00-$7F: number of a movement script (index into the script address tables at $36/$38), run by object_script_step ($B207) with the position in obj_script_pos; unless that leaves bit 1 or 5 of obj_state set, the $B1F7 table handlers then run as below. $FF: update_objects clears obj_flags (sets it to 1 on landing) and skips the table handlers. Any other negative value (for example $FE): no script; the $B1F7 table handlers run when bit 5 of obj_flags is set and bit 3 of obj_state is clear. object_arc_step runs first for any object whose arc state is non-zero. Written by the phase handlers ($A9B9 copies obj_off_y, $A9FA and $AA45 write 2 and 1, $AB2B $FE), the hit handlers $A8E8 and $A904, script commands ($B87F, $BCF7 storing $FE, $BD2C swapping it with $3322), object_walk_land_stop ($B4BD, 0) and the swap at $4C9D; initial values come from the stage data (not traced).

Second motion byte. The trigger code at $4C9D swaps it with obj_motion and also saves the script position and repeat count in $3844 and $3898, so the object switches to the other motion when the player comes near (table handlers 0, 2 and 13 jump there, and script command 13 calls it); script command 14 ($BD22) swaps the two as well. Phase 5 objects ($A9EC) instead read it as a saved Y position, low byte, and copy it into obj_y_lo, and destroy routine 1 ($A841) copies it into weapon_level; the uses suit different kinds of object. Initial value comes from the stage data (not traced).

Motion byte that replaces obj_motion when the object is hit by the type 1 or 2 reaction ($A8E5) or when a movement script reaches the command at $B86F, which also sets bit 7 of obj_kind and obj_move_bits to $FF. Phase 5 objects ($A9F2) read it as a saved Y position, high byte, and copy it into obj_y_hi. Initial value comes from the stage data (not traced).

Animation number of each object: the index into the tables that the pointers $3A and $3C (low and high bytes) point to, which give the address of its animation block; obj_anim_index picks the frame within the block. The hit reactions 0 and 1 replace it through anim_swap_table ($3E), and script command 22 sets it from an object record.

Behaviour phase of each object, a small number dispatched by object_phase_dispatch ($A990): 0 and 6 or more apply obj_dir and obj_speed, 1 nudges Y, 2 counts a flag down, 3 starts an arc, 4 waits for bit 7 of obj_flags then returns to 0, 5 runs sub-states in obj_off_x. It is also the contact class in object_sprites_and_hits ($A731, $A56A): 0 runs the destroy routine at $A7A1, 1 goes to $A5B2, 2 or more go to $A74E; below 2 the object is tested against the player's second hit box first. The pool setup at $5066 gives every temporary object phase 1. Initial values of stage objects come from the stage data (not traced).
Bit mask of the frames in which the object moves: an object moves when it shares a bit with move_mask.

Step size of each object in pixels (low byte, unsigned). apply_object_direction/step_object_by_script and the move_object_* routines add or subtract it on the object's X or Y per step, and diagonal moves move X twice as far. The walking handlers ($B5D5) use it as the sideways step, and phase handlers copy it into $0295 so a rider is carried the same distance. Set by the script command at $B85D (next script byte), by phase2_wiggle_y (1) and the stage data.

Animation delay reload value. advance_object_animation ($B57A) counts obj_anim_timer down and, when it passes zero, reloads it from here and steps obj_anim_index. Set to 1 when a pool object turns into its short animation ($8508) and, for spawned pool objects, to the same value as the timer ($B77C, from the spawn record).

State bits of each object (stage objects and the temporary pool share the tables). Bit 7 ($80): off screen, not drawn. Bit 6 ($40): set when the object is in the view, but update_objects also sets it, with bit 7, for an object above or below the view. Bit 5 ($20): retired. Bit 1 ($02) makes update_objects skip an object on frames it does not move. Bit 3 ($08) and bit 2 ($04) are tested in update_temp_objects; $FF marks an unused slot.

Object kind and flag bits. Low four bits: reaction type used by $A88E when a player shot or the player destroys the object (0-9, table at $A87A). Bit 7: for a pool object, makes it blink (see update_temp_objects); for a stage object, set by the trigger at $4C9D, by script command 6 ($B86F) and by the hit handlers, which also clear bits 4 and 5 at $A91D; script command 14 ($BD1A) clears it. Bit 6: object not drawn and not hit (object_sprites_and_hits tests it; the blink sets it on alternate frames; phase 5 clears and sets it, $A124 does so for object $08CC, script command 20 toggles it). Bit 5: the object can be hit by the player's shots (the six shot slots at $06DD). Bit 4: the player can land on it from a jump and take 2 hit points off ($A5BB); when it is clear, that contact hits the player ($A630).

Not an array of its own: this is one byte before obj_flags ($364C), so $364B,x is obj_flags of slot x-1. For an object whose obj_motion is $FF, update_objects clears its obj_flags ($A28E); when it is falling (bit 6 of obj_arc_state) and lands level with slot x-1 ($39A5,x is obj_y_lo of slot x-1), it sets the flags of slot x to 1, clears its arc state and the flags of slot x-1 ($A2AF), and toggles bit 0 of obj_anim_index of slot x-1 ($3EBB,x). Reads as a pair of linked slots (a child object at x and its parent at x-1); that reading is inferred.

Flags of each object. Bit 7: a parent whose position followers take. Bit 6: a follower. Bit 4: retire when leaving the view. Bit 5 is tested before calling $B1F7. When an object is destroyed (code at $A7A1), the low four bits choose a routine from the tables at $A868 and $A871.

Not an array of its own: one byte after obj_flags ($364C), so $364D,x is obj_flags of slot x+1. The contact code at $A74E tests it. When non-zero it queues sound $10, sets stance ($0299) to 0, jump_state ($08FA) to $FF, jump_counter ($08FB) to $A0 plus jump_start_count and player_action ($0905) to 3, and clears $364D,x again ($A796) (inferred: the player bounces). When zero, and only if jump_state is positive and non-zero, bit 1 of move_dir ($0D) is clear and obj_flags of slot x is zero, it sets obj_flags,x to 1, toggles bit 0 of obj_anim_index,x and starts a rise in slot x+1 (see $3F1A). That the slots x and x+1 are a linked pair is inferred.

Direction of each object in the low four bits, in the joystick pattern: $0B left, $07 right, $0E up, $0D down, $06 up-right, $05 down-right, $09 down-left, $0A up-left. Written by apply_object_direction (step_object_by_script) from the script byte, by the phase 2 handlers ($0E, $0D) and by the walking code at $B5FE. Read by apply_dir_and_speed, which hands it to the player as $19 when the object carries the player, and by the walking code at $B5D5: bit 2 clear is a left direction; bit 2 and bit 3 both set (up or down) make it return without moving; otherwise bit 3 set moves left (speed subtracted at $B616) and clear moves right. XOR $0C turns the object round at a ledge or wall.

For a follower (bit 6 of obj_flags set), its X offset from the leader (signed byte): position minus leader_x_lo, stored at $8935 and $B24C, added back to leader_x at $A1E0. Other objects reuse the byte: object_run_script_handler ($B1F7) takes it as the index of its handler in script_cmd2, the phase 5 and phase 3 handlers ($A9C2, $AA61) keep a sub-state in it (counted up with inc, reset at $AA15), and phase1_pull_back_y ($AB69) compares obj_y_lo with it as a lower limit.

For a follower (bit 6 of obj_flags set), its Y offset from the leader (signed byte): position minus leader_y_lo, stored at $893E and $B255, added back to leader_y at $A200. Other objects reuse the byte: the phase 5 handlers count it down as a timer ($A9CF, $A9FE, $AA23; reloaded with $0E, $07 and $4B), phase4_wait_flag7 ($A9B6) copies it to obj_motion, and phase3_land_check ($AA93) compares it with obj_y divided by 16.

Position of each object in its movement script (offset into the script bytes found through the pointers $36/$38 and obj_motion). object_script_step ($B207) reads the byte there: below $80 a command, run through $88AF; $80 and above a move. It is advanced when a command or move finishes ($B22A, $B236) and by script command 13 ($B6F1) just before that command calls the trigger at $4C9D, which saves it in $3844 and clears it; $BD40 puts the saved value back and resumes the script. Set to 0 when an object is spawned ($4D09, $B69D) and by the hit handlers at $A91D ($A934).

Repeat counter of the current move in the object's movement script. step_object_by_script ($B259) loads it from the byte after the direction byte, with bit 7 set to mark it loaded, counts it down once per step and moves on to the next script byte when it underflows. Script command 5 ($0BA0) keeps its own count in it the same way. Zeroed when a command or move finishes ($B22F), when an object is spawned ($4D0C, $B6A0) and by the hit handlers at $A91D; the trigger at $4C9D saves it in $3898 and zeroes it, and $BD3A puts it back.
X position in the stage of each object, low byte (high byte in obj_x_hi).

Entry 40 of obj_x_lo (X low byte of object 40; the arrays hold 93 objects, $38EC-$3948). stage2_common stores $54 here when section_index is 6 or more (saved value $CC); object 41's entry, $3915, gets $34.
Entry 41 of obj_x_lo, the X low byte of object 41: $34 from stage2_common for stage 2 from section 6 on (saved value $D8). It is the first of the entries up to $3948, the end of obj_x_lo.
X position in the stage of each object, high byte.
Not an array of its own: one byte before obj_y_lo ($39A6), so $39A5,x is obj_y_lo of slot x-1. Compared with $E9 in the landing test at $A29A.
Y position in the stage of each object, low byte (high byte in obj_y_hi).
Y position in the stage of each object, high byte.

Frame countdown of each object's animation. advance_object_animation ($B57A) decrements it while bit 0 of obj_state is set; when it goes below zero it is reloaded from obj_anim_delay and obj_anim_index goes up. Set to $FF when an object is spawned ($4D11, $B6A8) and by the type 2 hit handler ($A8F5); set to obj_anim_delay by the spawner at $B77F and to obj_anim_delay plus 1 by script command 12 ($B833); cleared when a pool object becomes a short animation ($8510).

Smallest screen Y at which a sprite part of the object may be drawn: object_sprites_and_hits ($A4A8) skips parts below it, and also parts at $D5 or beyond. Set by $B5CD to $38 minus byte 4 of the animation data block (carry not set explicitly, so the value may be one lower; its meaning as a height is inferred).

Pointer to the data of the object's current animation step, low byte (high byte obj_frame_ptr_hi), set by $B5BC from the animation block at offset 5 plus twice obj_anim_index. The data starts with the hit box offsets that set_object_hitbox adds to the position (left, top, right, bottom), then byte 4 is the part count and the sprite parts follow; object_sprites_and_hits walks the parts.
High byte of the pointer to the data of the object's current animation step (low byte obj_frame_ptr_lo).
Left edge of each object's hit box, low byte (high byte at $3C31). Right $3C8E/$3CEB, top $3D48/$3DA5, bottom $3E02/$3E5F; set by set_object_hitbox.

Left edge of each object's hit box, high byte (low byte obj_hit_left_lo). Set by set_object_hitbox, and to $3E by the spawner at $B801 (with obj_hit_top_hi), which keeps a new object's box out of reach until set_object_hitbox runs (inferred). Read by the shot and player contact tests.
Right edge of each object's hit box, low byte (high byte at $3CEB).
Right edge of each object's hit box, high byte (low byte obj_hit_right_lo). Set by set_object_hitbox.
Top edge of each object's hit box, low byte (high byte at $3DA5).
Top edge of each object's hit box, high byte (low byte obj_hit_top_lo). Set by set_object_hitbox, and to $3E by the spawner at $B804 (with obj_hit_left_hi at $B801).
Bottom edge of each object's hit box, low byte (high byte at $3E5F).
Bottom edge of each object's hit box, high byte (low byte obj_hit_bottom_lo). Set by set_object_hitbox.

Not an array of its own: one byte before obj_anim_index ($3EBC), so $3EBB,x is obj_anim_index of slot x-1. $A2A4 toggles its bit 0 when the object in slot x lands (inferred: flips the facing or frame of a linked parent).

Index of the object's current step in its animation (frame sequence of the animation block selected by obj_frame). advance_object_animation ($B57A) adds 1 each time obj_anim_timer runs out and wraps to 0 at the count in byte 0 of the block; script command 9 ($B838) steps it the same way and stores it at $B853. $B5B5 stores it and loads obj_frame_ptr and obj_draw_min_y for it. Cleared by script command 12 ($B824) when it selects a new animation, by the hit handlers at $A91D ($A93A), by the spawners at $B6A3 and $B7A5 and when a pool object becomes a short animation ($850D); bit 0 is toggled at $A76D and $A2A4 (the latter through $3EBB, the entry of slot x-1).

Motion state of each object for object_arc_step: 0 is none; with bit 7 set it jumps (bit 6 clear) or falls (bit 6 set); any other non-zero value is an offset into the path data at the pointer $32, and the path move clears it when the path ends.

Not an array of its own: one byte after obj_arc_state ($3F19), so $3F1A,x is obj_arc_state of slot x+1. $A772 sets it to $80 (start a rise) for slot x+1, with that slot's obj_arc_counter ($3F77) set to $2A, when the contact code at $A74E finds $364D,x zero, jump_state positive and non-zero, bit 1 of move_dir clear and obj_flags of slot x zero (inferred: launches the linked child of the object in slot x).

Counter that object_arc_step uses: in a rise or fall (obj_arc_state bit 7 set) it steps through the speed tables jump_rise_steps ($02CE) and jump_fall_steps ($02DF); in a path move it is instead the number of the path, the index path_advance ($894C) uses into the path state at $5C, $60 and $64.

Not an array of its own: one byte after obj_arc_counter ($3F76), so $3F77,x is obj_arc_counter of slot x+1. $A777 sets it to $2A together with obj_arc_state of slot x+1 ($3F1A), the rise that the contact code at $A74E starts.

Pool object X velocity, low byte; one byte for each of the nine temporary objects, indexed by the pool number (slot minus temp_first), not by slot. update_temp_objects adds temp_vel_x (this and the next table) to obj_x each frame the object moves. Filled from the spawn record by the spawner at $B7CF, cleared when the object turns into its short animation ($8516).
Pool object X velocity, high byte (sign extension of temp_vel_x_lo); added to obj_x_hi with the carry by update_temp_objects. Indexed by pool number. Set at $B7D5, cleared at $8519.
Pool object Y velocity, low byte; added to obj_y_lo each frame the object moves. Indexed by pool number. Set at $B7DB, cleared at $851C.
Pool object Y velocity, high byte; added with the carry to obj_y_hi. Indexed by pool number. Set at $B7E1, cleared at $851F.
Life of each pool object, counted down by one by update_temp_objects on each frame the object moves (set to $18 when one turns into its short animation).

Entry reached by jump from round_start ($8078) after store_score_digits when the lives have run out; round_start's comment calls the target the title. Sets the CPU port to $37 (cartridge ROM visible at $8000) and jumps to $8C68. The code at $4007 (also with the port restored to $35) counts $089C down: if it stays non-negative it jumps to $802B inside game_start, otherwise to game_start at $8000. Whether $8C68 returns to $4007 is not traced here.

Start of the between-stage screen. Clears the page at $FE00, runs the routine at $8C07 with $01 set to $37 (ROM visible; probably unpacks data from $8B27 into $FE00, inferred), then looks at $0294: negative goes to the loop at $4095, positive skips to $407C. When it is zero: if the stage number $08E7 is 5 or more, it switches off the CIA2 timer A interrupt and the screen ($D011), calls $BD5D and restarts the game at game_start. Otherwise it sets $D018 to $31, calls $8E9A and polls read_joystick_ports while bit 4 reads 0, that is until fire is released (at once if it is not held), blanks the screen, bumps $0294, then increments $089D and continues into stage_begin. The $0294 branch and $089D meaning are not established here.

Reads both joystick ports: writes $7F to $DC00 and $DC01 (CIA 1 ports A/B), reads $DC00 and, if no direction/fire pressed there ($7F), reads $DC01 instead. Returns the port value in A (fire is bit 4, active low). Its one caller is the loop at $4069 in stage_intro_start, which repeats while bit 4 is 0 (AND #$10): it waits for fire to be released.

Per-frame loop of the pre-round/intro screen. Points the IRQ vector ($FFFE/$FFFF) to irq_panel $837E and the raster line $D012 to $D5, sets sprite X positions in $D000-$D00E (sprites 0 and 2 from player_screen_x $029B with high bit $029C, sprites 1 and 3 at +24, sprites 4-7 at fixed $8C/$A4/$BC/$D4, high bits into $D010), waits for frame_flag $08F7 to change, then increments frame_count $08F6. At $80 frames it enables all sprites ($D015=$FF) and calls $6ED8 with A=$19 (caller of $6ED8); when the count wraps to 0 it increments $0294, turns the display off ($D011=0), sets $08B0=$FF and jumps back to $4044. Entered from $403D when $0294 is negative, and loops back to $4095 each frame otherwise.

Moves the sort-list entries left over after the eight-sprite limit into a queue at $7E. Returns at once if sprite_more ($6B) is zero. Otherwise it walks the sprite sort list $7CBD from position $6B, skipping empty entries (bit 7 set); each real entry is copied to $7E,Y and the list slot is set to $FF. An entry of $7F ends the walk: the queue gets a closing $FF, that slot and $0807 are set to $FF. Purpose is inferred from the names of the data it touches.

Choose the player's current animation frame and place the extra parts that depend on it. Depending on player_mode ($09), the facing bit 3 of $18, the animation number $0297, and state flags ($08FA, $0900, $0299, $0B), it finds a frame record (through the pointer tables at $0A4B-$0A91, or the fixed records at $0A29, $0A3A, $095D, and $0962) and then: sets the shape number player_shape_3 ($08EC) from the record's first byte (plus 20 and colour $0E in $0916 while bit 7 of $08B2 is set, otherwise plus 10 while the countdown $08DF is not negative, which it decrements); sets the third sprite's position ($08B3/$08B4 and $08B5/$08B6) to player_x and player_y plus an X and a Y offset from the record (chosen by $0902) and $0322/$0323; and loads the extents $031E-$0321 from the tables at $03F7, $040B, $0401, and $0415 indexed by the record's first byte. In mode 1, with $0B zero and bit 7 of $08C6 set, it also loads player_shape_1 and player_shape_2 ($08EA, $08EB) from bytes 9 and 10 of the record.
Put the player back at the position saved by save_player_x and save_player_y: Y first (restore_player_y), then X.
Copy player_try_x ($08BB/$08BC) back to player_x ($08B7/$08B8).
Copy player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE) back to player_y ($08B9/$08BA).
Save the player's X position ($08B7/$08B8) in player_try_x ($08BB/$08BC).
Save the player's Y position ($08B9/$08BA) in player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE).

Work out the visible part of the stage in pixels from the scroll position. $40/$41 (view_left) = scroll_x ($1C/$1D, in 8-pixel columns) times 8 plus 7 minus scroll_fine_x ($06); $42/$43 (view_top) = scroll_y ($1E/$1F, in 8-pixel rows) times 8 plus 7 minus scroll_fine_y ($07) (the subtraction at $429F starts with the carry clear, so its 8 acts as 7); $44/$45 (view_right) = view_left + $12F; $46/$47 (view_bottom) = view_top + $9F. Every routine that compares a position with the screen (the object updates, the sprite placement, the hit tests) reads these.
Moves player_try_x ($08BB/$08BC) left by move_step ($0A), with borrow into the high byte, unless bit 7 of fire_flags ($08C6) is set, in which case it does nothing. Mirror of move_prev_x_right.

Moves player_prev_x ($08BB/$08BC) right by move_step ($0A), with carry into the high byte, unless bit 7 of fire_flags ($08C6) is set, in which case it does nothing. Called for a step to the right by player_jump_right and walk_right_move (mode 0), by mode2_step_right, mode2_up_right and mode2_down_right, and by mode1_right.

Subtracts move_step ($0A) from player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE), with borrow into the high byte, unless bit 7 of fire_flags ($08C6) is set. A smaller Y is taken as up (inferred from the scroll direction table, where direction 0 is up).
Adds move_step ($0A) to player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE), with carry into the high byte, unless bit 7 of fire_flags ($08C6) is set. Mirror of move_prev_y_up.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 0 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 1 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 2 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 3 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Mark the scroll idle: $0F and scroll_phase $0E both become $FF.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 4 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 5 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 6 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.
Set the scroll direction $0F to 7 and scroll_phase $0E to 0, so that the next call of the matching scroll routine starts moving.

Adds a score award to the five-byte score at $08D0-$08D4. The top two bits of A pick the award class 0-2 (class 3 returns with nothing added). Pointer $4A/$4B comes from the tables at $042E and $0431, and its five bytes are added digit by digit from the last place with carry. A digit reaching $CB wraps by subtracting $0A, leaving the carry set for the next place, so the digits are stored as $C1 plus the digit value (the snapshot's score is five $C1 bytes). The three awards ($02BB, $02C0, $02C5) are 10, 50 and 100. Role as the score is inferred from this arithmetic.

Copies the 16-bit scroll_y ($1E/$1F) to $22/$23 and stores its low bit in $08C8, then jumps to $43FB. Part of the scroll engine's row setup; the exact use of $22/$23 is not shown in this range (inferred).
Same as copy_scroll_y_row but for the row above: stores scroll_y minus 1 (16-bit) in $22/$23, its low bit in $08C8, and jumps to $43FB when no borrow happened.
Starts the same setup for the row below: loads scroll_y and adds 1. The routine continues past this range, so the rest is not described here.

Redraws the playfield column just left of the view (map x = scroll_x minus 1, map y low byte = scroll_y plus 1; the carry into the high byte is added to $1F, not to $23, so $23 keeps its old value) into the screen buffer pointed to by $08C1/$08C2, one character column down the screen (21 rows, counter in $E9). Bit 0 of the map x and y positions go to $08C7 and $08C8 and select which half of each 2x2-character block is copied. Map blocks are found through the row pointer tables at ($2A)/($2C) indexed by y/2, then the block number times 4 plus $2E gives the block's characters. Odd-row starts are handed to draw_column_odd_start. Used while the screen scrolls; role inferred from the code.

Address inside the instruction at $44DE: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction.

Variant of draw_column_left_of_view for a column that starts on the lower half of a map block ($08C8 non-zero). It copies one character of the first block to the top screen row, and one from the block ten rows further down to the row twenty rows below ($E5 plus $320), then sets the remaining row counter $E9 to 18 and rejoins the normal column loop at $448D. The $320 offset is the bottom row of the 21-row playfield; role inferred.

Entry that sets up a map-row copy at map position ($1C/$1D plus 1, $1E/$1F minus 1): $20/$21 get scroll_x plus 1 with the carry carried into the high byte, $08C7 gets bit 0 of $20, then it sets carry and joins the shared code at $45A6, which derives $22 and $08C8 from scroll_y minus 1. Sibling of draw_row_x_minus1_y_minus1 ($4593), which subtracts instead of adding.

Entry that sets up a map-row copy at map position ($1C/$1D minus 1, $1E/$1F minus 1): stores the results in $20/$21 and $22/$23, the odd-column and odd-row flags in $08C7 and $08C8, and the destination pointer from $08C1/$08C2 into $E5/$E6, then jumps to map_row_copy_start.

Entry that sets up a map-row copy at column $1C/$1D and row $1E/$1F plus $15 (21): column flag goes to $08C7, row flag to $08C8, and destination is $08C1/$08C2 plus $0320 in $E5/$E6. Falls through to map_row_copy_start.
Same as draw_bottom_row_x_plus0 but the column is $1C/$1D plus 1. Reached only from outside this range; the preceding clc and bcc skip past it.
Same as draw_bottom_row_x_plus0 but the column is $1C/$1D minus 1.
Common tail of the three bottom-row entries: row = $1E/$1F + $15 into $22/$23 with its low bit in $08C8, and destination = $08C1/$08C2 + $0320 into $E5/$E6.

Finds the map cell: loads row ($22/$23) shifted right once, uses it as an index into the pointer tables at ($2A) and ($2C) for the row's address, and adds column ($20/$21) shifted right once to get the cell pointer in $E1/$E2. Sets $E9 to $13, then chooses the even path when $08C7 is 0 or the odd path otherwise.

Even-column path loop: multiplies the cell value by 4, adds the block table base $2E/$2F, adds 2 when $08C8 is set (picks the lower pair of the 4-byte block), then copies two characters to ($E5), advancing $E1/$E2 by 1 and $E5/$E6 by 2 until $E9 underflows after 20 passes (40 characters).
Return from the even path.

Odd-column path: copies only the right-hand character of the first block, then copies the left-hand character of the block 20 cells further on ($14 offset) to destination offset $27, sets $E9 to $12, and jumps into the even loop. Locates the block the same way (cell value times 4 plus $2E/$2F, plus 2 for odd rows).

Move the view by one step toward where it should be; called from track_stage_section each frame that $08CB is zero and the player is not hit. First it sets scroll_step to 2. Bits 7 and 6 of section_scroll_flags then choose the mode. Bit 7 clear: auto_scroll_horizontal, which scrolls right (bit 5 set) or left (bit 5 clear) until the section limit, then follows the player vertically. Bit 7 set and bit 6 clear: auto_scroll_vertical, down (bit 5 set) or up, then follows the player horizontally. Both set: follow_player_both. Following means that a player_screen_x or player_screen_y outside the zone makes the view scroll toward that side; inside the zone the scroll goes idle through stop_scroll. A straight follow move that meets a limit stores it in view_pinned_edges and also goes idle; the auto modes store it and go on to follow, and a diagonal move pins an edge without storing it.

Section that scrolls sideways by itself. With bit 5 of section_scroll_flags set, room_to_scroll_right is asked and the view scrolls right while there is room; otherwise room_to_scroll_left and a scroll left. At the limit the view is pinned (pin_view_right or pin_view_left), view_pinned_edges gets $08 or $04, and the code falls into follow_player_y.
Follow the player vertically: player_screen_y below zone_top ($090A) scrolls up (try_scroll_up), at or beyond zone_bottom ($090B) scrolls down (try_scroll_down), and inside the zone the scroll stops.

Bit 7 of section_scroll_flags is set. With bit 6 also set the view follows the player in both axes (follow_player_both). Otherwise the section scrolls vertically by itself: bit 5 set asks room_to_scroll_down and scrolls down while there is room, bit 5 clear asks room_to_scroll_up and scrolls up. At the limit the view is pinned (pin_view_bottom or pin_view_top), view_pinned_edges gets 2 or 1, and the code falls into follow_player_x.

Follow the player horizontally: player_screen_x beyond zone_right ($0906) scrolls right (try_scroll_right), below zone_left ($0908) scrolls left (try_scroll_left), and inside the zone the scroll stops.

Follow the player in both axes. The horizontal position is tested first (beyond zone_right, below zone_left, or inside) and then the vertical one (above zone_top, below zone_bottom, or inside). Outside on one axis only gives a straight scroll; outside on both gives a diagonal one through try_up_right, try_up_left, try_down_right, or try_down_left. Inside on both axes stops the scroll.
Scroll up if room_to_scroll_up allows; otherwise pin the view at the top (pin_view_top), store 1 in view_pinned_edges, and stop the scroll.
Scroll down if room_to_scroll_down allows; otherwise pin the view at the bottom (pin_view_bottom), store 2 in view_pinned_edges, and stop the scroll.
Scroll right if room_to_scroll_right allows; otherwise pin the view at the right edge (pin_view_right), store 8 in view_pinned_edges, and stop the scroll.
Scroll left if room_to_scroll_left allows; otherwise pin the view at the left edge (pin_view_left), store 4 in view_pinned_edges, and stop the scroll.

The player is above and to the right of the zone. With no room to scroll up the view is pinned at the top and scrolls right only; with no room to scroll right it is pinned at the right edge and scrolls up only; with room on both sides it takes the diagonal scroll_up_right.

The player is above and to the left of the zone. With no room up the view is pinned at the top and scrolls left only; with no room left it is pinned at the left edge and scrolls up only; with room on both sides it takes scroll_up_left.

The player is below and to the right of the zone. With no room down the view is pinned at the bottom and scrolls right only; with no room right it is pinned at the right edge and scrolls down only; with room on both sides it takes scroll_down_right.

The player is below and to the left of the zone. With no room down the view is pinned at the bottom and scrolls left only; with no room left it is pinned at the left edge and scrolls down only; with room on both sides it takes scroll_down_left.

One step of the view to the right. If the scroll direction $0F is not 2 yet, set_dir_right makes it 2 and the step waits for the next call. The step is skipped while the previous tile's redraw is still too recent: scroll_fine_x scaled by scroll_step (fine_x_steps) has to be above scroll_phase. The step clears the left bit of view_pinned_edges and subtracts scroll_step from scroll_fine_x ($06). When that goes below 0 the value wraps into 0 to 7, scroll_x ($1C) grows by 1, and tile_scroll_done starts the redraw.

One step of the view to the left, the mirror of scroll_right (direction 6, set_dir_left). It clears the right bit of view_pinned_edges and adds scroll_step to scroll_fine_x ($06); when scroll_fine_x is 7 it first prepares scroll_x minus 1 in $20/$21, and a result of 8 or more wraps into 0 to 7 and stores that value into scroll_x before tile_scroll_done.

One step of the view up (direction 0, set_dir_up). It waits like scroll_left, sets scroll_step to 4 when the player is $2C or more pixels above zone_top, clears the bottom bit of view_pinned_edges, and adds scroll_step to scroll_fine_y ($07). When scroll_fine_y is 7 it first prepares scroll_y minus 1 in $22/$23, and a result of 8 or more wraps into 0 to 7 and stores that value into scroll_y ($1E) before tile_scroll_done.

One step of the view down (direction 4, set_dir_down). It waits like scroll_right, sets scroll_step to 4 when the player is $2C or more pixels below zone_bottom, prepares scroll_y plus 1 in $22/$23, clears the top bit of view_pinned_edges, and subtracts scroll_step from scroll_fine_y ($07). Going below 0 wraps the value into 0 to 7 and stores scroll_y plus 1 before tile_scroll_done.

Diagonal step up and to the right (direction 1). A diagonal only runs when the fine positions are in step, 8 minus scroll_fine_y equal to scroll_fine_x. When they are not, the view scrolls right by itself (scroll_right) until they are. The first instructions work out scroll_x plus $26 and throw the result away.
The jump at $4A04 to scroll_up; no branch or jump in the code reaches it.
Jump stub: continues at scroll_right ($489D).

The move of the diagonal up and to the right. It keeps only the top and right bits of view_pinned_edges, subtracts scroll_step from scroll_fine_x and adds it to scroll_fine_y. When scroll_fine_x goes below 0 both wrap into 0 to 7, scroll_x grows by 1, scroll_y shrinks by 1 (a subtract with the carry left clear), and tile_scroll_done runs.
Diagonal step down and to the right (direction 3), allowed when scroll_fine_y equals scroll_fine_x. Otherwise the view scrolls right by itself (scroll_right) until they are equal.
The jump at $4A68 to scroll_down; no branch or jump in the code reaches it.
Jump stub: continues at scroll_right ($489D). This is the byte at $4A6B.

The move of the diagonal down and to the right. It keeps the bottom and right bits of view_pinned_edges, subtracts scroll_step from both fine positions (they stay equal), and when they go below 0 wraps them and adds 1 to both scroll_x and scroll_y before tile_scroll_done.
Diagonal step down and to the left (direction 5), allowed when 8 minus scroll_fine_y equals scroll_fine_x. Otherwise the view scrolls left by itself (scroll_left) until they are.
The jump at $4AC7 to scroll_down; no branch or jump in the code reaches it.
Jump stub: continues at scroll_left ($48E0).

The move of the diagonal down and to the left. It keeps the bottom and left bits of view_pinned_edges, subtracts scroll_step from scroll_fine_y and adds it to scroll_fine_x. When scroll_fine_y goes below 0 both wrap into 0 to 7, scroll_x shrinks by 1, scroll_y grows by 1, and tile_scroll_done runs.

Diagonal step up and to the left (direction 7), allowed when scroll_fine_x equals scroll_fine_y. Otherwise the view scrolls left by itself (scroll_left) until they are equal. The first six instructions are two compares whose branches lead to the next instruction.
The jump at $4B3E to scroll_up; no branch or jump in the code reaches it.
Jump stub: continues at scroll_left ($48E0). This is the byte at $4B41.

The move of the diagonal up and to the left. It keeps the top and left bits of view_pinned_edges and adds scroll_step to both fine positions. When they reach 8 or more both wrap into 0 to 7 and scroll_x and scroll_y shrink by 1 before tile_scroll_done.

The view has moved by one whole tile. Flip the displayed screen buffer $10 (the old value goes to $11), swap the bytes at $08C0 and $08C2, and set scroll_phase to 1 so that the redraw of the new edge starts (see scroll_phase).
Return with the N flag clear when the view can still move right: the largest view_left in the section record (bytes 8 and 9 at ($26)) is above view_left.
Return with the N flag clear when the view can still move left: view_left is above the smallest view_left in the section record (bytes 6 and 7).
Return with the N flag clear when the view can still move down: the largest view_top in the section record (bytes 12 and 13) is above view_top.
Return with the N flag clear when the view can move up by a whole scroll_step: view_top minus scroll_step is not below the smallest view_top in the section record (bytes 10 and 11).
Return scroll_fine_y ($07) divided by 1, 2, or 4 for a scroll_step of 1, 2, or more. The scroll routines compare the value with scroll_phase to decide whether the redraw has got far enough.
Return scroll_fine_x ($06) divided by 1, 2, or 4 for a scroll_step of 1, 2, or more, for comparison with scroll_phase.
Pin the view at the top limit: scroll_fine_y becomes 7 and view_top is rounded down to a multiple of 8.
Pin the view at the bottom limit: scroll_fine_y becomes 7 and view_top is rounded down to a multiple of 8 (the same code as pin_view_top).
Pin the view at the left limit: scroll_fine_x becomes 7 and view_left is rounded down to a multiple of 8.
Pin the view at the right limit: scroll_fine_x becomes 7 and view_left is rounded down to a multiple of 8 (the same code as pin_view_left).

NMI/IRQ frame handler (nmi_frame). Saves A and the CPU port ($01), maps I/O in with $01=$35, then reads CIA2 $DD0D: if bit 7 is clear (not an NMI) it jumps to frame_exit $4D42. Otherwise it reads state byte $08B0: negative leaves, 0 goes to blank_screen_exit $4D3D, non-zero saves X and Y in $7C/$7D. A value of 1 skips the sprite copy and goes to wait_and_set_vic $4D9A. A value of 2 or more falls into copy_sprite_shadows $4D47.
Branch target after the CIA2 check shows an NMI. Loads $08B0 and picks between exit (negative), blank_screen_exit (zero) or the frame update (positive).
When $08B0 is 0, writes $57 to VIC $D011 (screen control, ECM on) and falls into frame_exit. No sprite or colour work is done for this frame.
Common exit of nmi_frame: pulls the saved $01 value and A from the stack and returns with RTI.

Full frame update, taken when $08B0 is 2 or more. Disables interrupts, then loops X from 7 to 0 copying shadow buffers: $07E7,x to the sprite pointers $CBF8,x and $CFF8,x (both screens), $07EF,x to zero page $6C,x, $07F7,x to $D000,x and $07FF,x to $D008,x (the sprite position registers $D000-$D00F, X and Y alternating) and $07BF,x to sprite colours $D027,x. Then writes the enable mask $07BD to $D015, the X high bits $07BC to $D010 and the expand flags $07BE to both $D017 and $D01D. Sets the next interrupt: $07AB/$07AC (raster_vector) go to $FFFE/$FFFF, line $07AD goes to $D012, and the raster flag in $D019 is acknowledged.

Reached from nmi_frame when $08B0 is 1, or by falling through from the sprite copy. If $D011 bit 7 (raster line high bit) is clear, it waits in a loop until the raster passes line $FB, so the VIC register writes below happen in the lower border.

Writes $00 to CIA2 $DD00 (VIC bank 3, $C000-$FFFF), then applies the shadow registers: shadow_d018 $07B0 to $D018, bg_colour0-2 $08C3-$08C5 to $D021-$D023, shadow_d016 $07AF to $D016 and shadow_d011 $07AE to $D011. Increments frame_flag $08F7 so the main loop sees a new frame, restores X and Y from $7C/$7D, restores $01 and A, and returns with RTI.

Patches game code and data for the current stage ($08E7); called once from round_start at $80A8, after the raster vector is set. Stage 0: sets bytes $213E=$BC and $2150=$C1, sets pointer $48/$49 to $000A, then copies 32 bytes from $20C0 to $C780 unless bit 5 of $35A8 is set, in which case the buffer is cleared. Other stages are handled by the branches below. Returns with RTS.
Stage 0 with $35A8 bit 5 set: fills the 32 bytes at $C780-$C79F with $00 (Y from $1F down to 0), then returns.
Stage is not 0: compares it with 1 and goes to stage_not1 $4E34 if different.
Stage 1: stores $08 at $2D32, sets pointer $48/$49 to $1FC8, copies $201B to $2E87 and $202E to $2019, clears $201A and $2018, then returns.
Stage is not 1: compares it with 2 and goes to stage_not2 $4EB3 if different.

Stage 2. When section_index ($0298) is below 2, reads a pointer into $E1/$E2, its low byte from ($2A),$13 and its high byte from ($2C),$13, writes $36 at offsets $28 and $29 of that target, and sets $1D08/$1D0A to $A0 and $1D09/$1D0B to $00. Falls into stage2_common.
Stage 2 common part: clears bytes $1D6A and $1D6B. If section_index ($0298) is 6 or more, also sets $3914=$54 and $3915=$34.
Stage 2 end: stores $BD, $B7 and $BC at $30DA, $30CA and $30D6, then initialises a table at $BFFE-$C007 (values $FF, $00, $01, $06, $80 by byte) and returns with RTS.
Stage is not 2: compares it with 3 and goes to patch_stage_exit $4EDC if different.
Stage 3: stores $C0 at $1AD0, $00 at $1AD1, $10 at $1AE5, $04 at $1AE6, $19 at $BF22, $01 at $BF24 and $00 at $BF23/$BF25, then falls into the RTS.
Return point of patch_stage_code (RTS), also reached for stage 4 or higher where nothing is patched.

Resets per-round state: stores starting values (mostly 0 or $FF, also $19, 4, 3, $FE and 7) into about 30 game variables ($0898-$0913, zero page $06-$1A and $6B, player_effect $08B1, player_hit $0292, jump_state $08FA, view_pinned_edges $08FE), loads the record of the section numbered by $0C06 from table $0D22 to get byte $18 into $16, marks every obj_state $3592-$35E5 as $FF (free), then runs the start-position lookup, spawns objects, and ends by jumping to player_pose $413A.
Loop: writes $FF into obj_state $3592,x for x = $53 down to 0, freeing 84 object slots.
Loop: zeroes the six bytes $06DD-$06E2.

Start of the per-record test: record pointer is $E1/$E2 (from stage tables $8113/$8118, read with bank $80 selected; $85 is then written to the cartridge bank register $DE00 before the records are read). Compares player_hit_x $08E3/$08E4 and player_hit_y $08E5/$08E6 against the record's min and max x and y (bytes 0-7); any miss branches to skip_to_next_start_record.

Record did not contain the player position: scans forward from byte $11 (past the section byte $10) for a byte with bit 7 set, adds that byte's index plus 1 to $E1/$E2, and retests the next record at find_start_record_loop.
Loop: advances Y until the byte at ($E1),y has bit 7 set, marking the end of the current record.
A record matched: copies bytes 8-11 to $1C-$1F, bytes 12-15 to player_x $08B7, player_x_hi $08B8, player_y $08B9, and player_y_hi $08BA, then reads byte 16 as the section index.

Stores the section index (bit 7 stripped; if bit 7 was set, $09 is first set to 2) into section_index $0298, then loads the section record pointer from table $0D22 into $26/$27 and reads two bytes from ($E9) into $F0 and $08CC.
Reads the next object-range pair from the matched record (from Y = $11 on): a first byte with bit 7 set ends the list; otherwise X = first index and $E3 = end index, with Y saved in $E4.
Loop: calls $8000 once for each X from the range start up to (not including) $E3, then restores Y from $E4 and goes back to next_spawn_range.
After the object ranges: sets $01 to $35, calls load_section_record $936E, sets $28/$29 to $B9C9 and $08FC to $38, and calls $0BF6.
Loop: sets $17 = $16 + 9, then for nine slots counting down from $17-1 writes $FF to obj_state $3592 and obj_move_bits $3484, and 1 to $3427.

Runs with interrupts off and $01 = $37 while cartridge bank $8D is selected: copies a 63-byte sprite shape into $FF80 when player_shape_3 $08EC differs from the cached value $02CB (source from tables $9245/$9263), the same for $08EA into $FF00 (cache $02CC, tables $91BF/$9202), and $08EB into $FF40 (cache $02CD); the code then restores bank $80 and $01 = $35. Note a spin loop at $50BB when $08EA is zero, seen in the disassembly.

Background loader that copies cartridge data into RAM $C000+ in pieces of 63 bytes (the pointers step 64), one per call, so the game never stalls. If section_scroll_flags ($08FD) bits 2-3 are clear it returns. Bit 3 set starts a new stream: it clears the bit, takes the stream number from the low flag bits and begins at the destination. Otherwise it copies the next piece with ROM banked in ($DE00 selects the cartridge bank, $01 flips ROM/RAM), and when the count in $08A2 runs out it moves to the next entry of the stream table, the next segment of the same stream with its own count; a zero entry ends the stream and clears bit 2.
Sets the RAM destination for a new data stream: the stream's block number ($08AC,y) times 64 plus $C000 goes into pointer $04/$05, then falls into load_stream_source.

Reads the next stream entry from the table at $0773,x. The high byte gives the cartridge bank (top 3 bits, selects bank via $DE00 and $08A4) and the address in $8000-$9FFF; a zero high byte ends the list (clears flag bit 2 in $08FD and moves to the next entry). The first source byte is the number of pieces to copy (64 bytes apart, 63 copied from each) and is stored in $08A2.
Common exit of the stream loader: puts cartridge bank 0 back ($DE00 = $80) and restores the normal memory map ($01 = $35, I/O visible), then returns.

Switches in ROM and I/O ($01 = $37), selects cartridge bank 0 ($DE00 = $80) and calls $8194: with the cartridge in view that runs bank 0's routine there, not the RAM copy enable_frame_nmi (facts.md has stage_load use it to refresh the stack-page routines). It then runs cart_copy for the cartridge directory entries at offsets $40, $48 and $50 (entries 8-10) and restores the normal map ($01 = $35). Called once from $80AE before the per-frame calls in the main code; the entries' destinations are not read here, so what they hold is not claimed.

First code the game runs from RAM (the hand-over, entry.vsf): clears $C480-$C53F, copies 192 bytes from $FFBF-$FFFE to $44E1-$45A0 and selects bank 13 ($DE00 = $8D). With bank 13 in view it copies three 64-byte blocks into RAM (sprite shapes $3F, $40 and $41): $8000 to $CFC0 with ROM in view ($01 = $37), and $8300 to $D000 and $9282 to $D040 with $01 switched to $00 (all RAM) for each store under I/O and back to $37 for the next read. It then selects bank 0 again, runs stage_load ($0A9B) twice (X = $80, then $60), stores $07, $8C and the byte in $E0 at $0C02-$0C04, calls $0C05, sets $E0 to 9 and copies 59 bytes from $44E1 back to $FFBF-$FFF9.
Sets the CPU port ($01) to $37, ROM and I/O visible, and returns.
Sets the CPU port ($01) to $00 and returns. With the data-direction register in $00 this selects the all-RAM view (inferred).

Called by game_start ($8003). Disable interrupts, set $08B0 to $FF, point the NMI vector ($FFFA/$FFFB) at nmi_frame ($4D1D), switch the cartridge into view ($01 = $37), call $8194 (with the cartridge in view this runs the cartridge's code there, not the main loop's; facts.md has $0A9B use it to refresh the stack-page routines), copy six cartridge directory entries (0-5, per facts.md) into RAM with cart_copy_six, then hide the cartridge again ($01 = $35).
Keyboard matrix scan through CIA 1 ($DC00 rows, $DC01 columns), called from $80FC.

Draw the strip of the background that a one-tile scroll will bring into view. It does nothing unless scroll_phase ($0E) is zero. It then picks from scroll_dir ($0F: 0 is up, 2 right, 4 down, 6 left, and the odd numbers 1, 3, 5, and 7 are the diagonals between them) the row, the column, or both that are about to appear at the edge of the screen, and fills them into the off-screen character buffer whose address is in $08C1/$08C2. The stage map is read through the row pointer tables $2A and $2C (low and high bytes of each map row's address); each map byte is a tile, expanded to a 2 by 2 block of characters taken from the table at $2E/$2F, with $08C7 and $08C8 choosing which half of the tile the row or column starts in. A row is 40 characters (20 tiles) wide and a column 21 characters tall. The routines at $433D-$438B set $0F and clear $0E, except $4361, which sets both to $FF, as the reset at $4F1D does; $4B8A sets $0E to 1 once a tile step is made, and $888D then counts $0E down.

Refresh the colour RAM of the 21 playfield rows ($D800-$DB47, 840 characters) so it matches the screen buffer that is now on show. The screen buffer is swapped by the tile step at $4B8A, which flips $10 (0 shows the buffer at $C800, 1 shows $CC00; build_vic_shadows turns that into $D018 $21 or $31). Colour RAM exists only once, so it is rewritten rather than swapped: the tile step sets scroll_phase ($0E) to 1, and the countdown at $888D calls this routine when it sees the old value 1, one frame later. Each character's colour is taken from char_colour_table ($0C22). Reached by the jump at $889B and by the stub at $9517. The copy is unrolled with Y as the index, in four loops: three of 32 characters a pass, each covering a page of 256, and a last one of 72 (36 a pass for $C800, 24 for $CC00): recolour_c800_0 and the loops after it do the $C800 buffer, and recolour_cc00_0 and its loops do the $CC00 buffer.
Colour-RAM refresh from the screen buffer at $C800, used when $10 is zero. Clears carry for the additions in the loops and starts Y at 0.

First of 4 copy loops that read the screen buffer at $C800 one character at a time and write each character's colour to colour RAM. Each of the 32 unrolled steps takes the character code from $C800+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $D800+Y. Y then moves on by $20 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 256 characters, from $D800 to $D8FF. When Y wraps it falls into the next page's loop at $5CF6.

Copy loop 2 of 4 for the screen buffer at $C800. Each of the 32 unrolled steps takes the character code from $C900+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $D900+Y. Y then moves on by $20 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 256 characters, from $D900 to $D9FF. When Y wraps it falls into the next page's loop at $5E20.

Copy loop 3 of 4 for the screen buffer at $C800. Each of the 32 unrolled steps takes the character code from $CA00+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $DA00+Y. Y then moves on by $20 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 256 characters, from $DA00 to $DAFF. When Y wraps it falls into the next page's loop at $5F4C.

Copy loop 4 of 4 for the screen buffer at $C800. Each of the 36 unrolled steps takes the character code from $CA48+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $DA48+Y. Y then moves on by $24 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 72 characters, from $DB00 to $DB47 (the Y offsets are shifted so the unrolled steps end exactly at the last playfield character). That ends the 21 playfield rows (840 characters, $D800-$DB47); the routine then returns.

Colour-RAM refresh from the screen buffer at $CC00, used when $10 is non-zero (jumped to from $5BC6). The same four loops as recolour_c800 with the source moved up by $0400, except that the last one is unrolled 24 steps a pass (Y moving on by $18) rather than 36 ($24); clears carry and starts Y at 0.

First of 4 copy loops that read the screen buffer at $CC00 one character at a time and write each character's colour to colour RAM. Each of the 32 unrolled steps takes the character code from $CC00+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $D800+Y. Y then moves on by $20 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 256 characters, from $D800 to $D8FF. When Y wraps it falls into the next page's loop at $61C7.

Copy loop 2 of 4 for the screen buffer at $CC00. Each of the 32 unrolled steps takes the character code from $CD00+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $D900+Y. Y then moves on by $20 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 256 characters, from $D900 to $D9FF. When Y wraps it falls into the next page's loop at $62F1.

Copy loop 3 of 4 for the screen buffer at $CC00. Each of the 32 unrolled steps takes the character code from $CE00+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $DA00+Y. Y then moves on by $20 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 256 characters, from $DA00 to $DAFF. When Y wraps it falls into the next page's loop at $641D.

Copy loop 4 of 4 for the screen buffer at $CC00. Each of the 24 unrolled steps takes the character code from $CE48+Y, looks its colour up in char_colour_table ($0C22), and stores it at $DA48+Y. Y then moves on by $18 and the loop repeats until Y wraps past $FF, so it copies 72 characters, from $DB00 to $DB47 (the Y offsets are shifted so the unrolled steps end exactly at the last playfield character). That ends the 21 playfield rows (840 characters, $D800-$DB47); the routine then returns.

End of the fourth unrolled colour-RAM loop of the screen recolour: adds $18 to Y; when Y wraps to zero it returns, otherwise it jumps back into the loop at recolour_cc00_3 ($641D). Role inferred from the jump target.
Jumps back to recolour_cc00_3 ($641D) for the next pass of the loop.

Mode flag. sound_init sets it to $1F (nonzero); sid_player_init clears it. While it is nonzero, sid_load_song_voices works, update_filter_sweep is held off, and sid_voice_change_check silences a voice whose one-shot sound has run out. While it is zero, sid_load_song_voices does nothing and update_filter_sweep passes this test (it still returns when the voice it finds owning the filter has a one-shot sound active). Which of the two the game means (sound effects against a music player) is inferred from the callers.

Busy flag. sid_player_init increments it on entry and sid_init_finish clears it at the end; sid_player_update returns at once while it is nonzero, so the per-frame update never runs half way through a re-initialisation.
Scratch byte. sid_voice_start_change saves the voice number here; script command $81 (the pattern select at $6B52) also uses it as a temporary for the pattern index doubled.
Scratch byte. sid_voice_start_change saves the one-shot step counter here.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Frames left in the current note of the voice's script. tick_voice_script counts it down and reads the next script event at zero; the duration byte of each note (voice_store_duration) is stored here. Bytes $6505-$6507. Pattern command 4 also reads it, scheduling the next pattern step that many frames before the note ends (taken to be a gate-off; not proven).

Voice 1's byte of voice_script_timer ($6505-$6507). It is not cleared: right after sid_clear_registers_loop, sid_player_init stores 2 here (voice 0 gets 1 and voice 2 gets 3), so the voices' timers run out on different frames. sid_reset_voice_state also stores 2 here (Y + 1) for voice 1. The code that indexes voice_script_timer by voice number reads and writes it.

Voice 2's byte of voice_script_timer ($6505-$6507). It is not cleared: right after sid_clear_registers_loop, sid_player_init stores 3 here (voices 0 and 1 get 1 and 2), so the voices' timers run out on different frames. sid_reset_voice_state also stores 3 here (Y + 1) for voice 2. The code that indexes voice_script_timer by voice number reads and writes it.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Saved duration used while the repeat flag voice_repeat_flag is set (script command $87 stores it, $88 clears the flag). Bytes $6508-$650A.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Frames until the voice's pattern stream (the SID control and envelope writes, read by music_voice_step) is read again. Set to 1 at each new note unless restart-mask bit 2 is set, and loaded by the pattern wait commands. Bytes $650B-$650D.

Voice 1's byte of voice_pattern_timer ($650B-$650D). It is not cleared: right after sid_clear_registers_loop, sid_player_init stores 2 here (voice 0 gets 1 and voice 2 gets 3), so the voices' timers run out on different frames. The code that indexes voice_pattern_timer by voice number reads and writes it.

Voice 2's byte of voice_pattern_timer ($650B-$650D). It is not cleared: right after sid_clear_registers_loop, sid_player_init stores 3 here (voices 0 and 1 get 1 and 2), so the voices' timers run out on different frames. The code that indexes voice_pattern_timer by voice number reads and writes it.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Frames left in the current step of the voice's pulse-width program (music_voice_pulse_sweep). Bytes $650E-$6510.

Voice 1's byte of voice_pulse_timer ($650E-$6510). It is not cleared: right after sid_clear_registers_loop, sid_player_init stores 2 here (voice 0 gets 1 and voice 2 gets 3), so the voices' timers run out on different frames. The code that indexes voice_pulse_timer by voice number reads and writes it.

Voice 2's byte of voice_pulse_timer ($650E-$6510). It is not cleared: right after sid_clear_registers_loop, sid_player_init stores 3 here (voices 0 and 1 get 1 and 2), so the voices' timers run out on different frames. The code that indexes voice_pulse_timer by voice number reads and writes it.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Frames left in the current event of the voice's pitch program (music_voice_advance). Bytes $6511-$6513.

Voice 1's byte of voice_pitch_timer ($6511-$6513). It is not cleared: right after sid_clear_registers_loop, sid_player_init stores 2 here (voice 0 gets 1 and voice 2 gets 3), so the voices' timers run out on different frames. The code that indexes voice_pitch_timer by voice number reads and writes it.

Voice 2's byte of voice_pitch_timer ($6511-$6513). It is not cleared: right after sid_clear_registers_loop, sid_player_init stores 3 here (voices 0 and 1 get 1 and 2), so the voices' timers run out on different frames. The code that indexes voice_pitch_timer by voice number reads and writes it.

Single byte, not per voice. Frames left in the current step of the filter-cutoff program read from filter_sweep_table by update_filter_sweep. sid_player_init sets it to 1, and a note start resets it to 1 when the voice owns the filter (voice_filter_ctrl nonzero) and restart-mask bit 3 is clear.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Read position in the voice's top-level sequence script (the one pointed to by seq_script_ptr_lo and seq_script_ptr_hi, copied to $F7/$F8 by advance_voice_sequence). Bytes $6515-$6517; $6518-$651A are not used by the code.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Low bytes of the three sequence script addresses. sid_player_init fills $651B-$6520 from sid_seq_start_sets. Bytes $651B-$651D; the high bytes are seq_script_ptr_hi.

Byte written by sid_player_init when a song starts (it copies six bytes to $651B-$6520). Low byte of voice 1's sequence script address (seq_script_ptr_lo), which advance_voice_sequence loads indexed by the voice number.

Byte written by sid_player_init when a song starts (it copies six bytes to $651B-$6520). Low byte of voice 2's sequence script address (seq_script_ptr_lo), which advance_voice_sequence loads indexed by the voice number.
