Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. High bytes of the three sequence script addresses (low bytes in seq_script_ptr_lo). Bytes $651E-$6520.

Byte written by sid_player_init when a song starts (it copies six bytes to $651B-$6520). High byte of voice 1's sequence script address (seq_script_ptr_hi), which advance_voice_sequence loads indexed by the voice number.

Byte written by sid_player_init when a song starts (it copies six bytes to $651B-$6520). High byte of voice 2's sequence script address (seq_script_ptr_hi, $651E-$6520), which advance_voice_sequence loads with lda $651E,x, X = 2.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Low byte of the voice's current position in its pattern stream (music_voice_step). Bytes $6521-$6523. Both halves are set to $6602, an idle pattern, at a reset; script command $81 (at $6B52) sets voice_pattern_start to a real pattern, which the next note copies here unless restart-mask bit 2 is set.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Low byte of the address the pattern stream is restarted from at each new note (copied into voice_pattern_ptr_lo unless restart-mask bit 2 is set). Bytes $6524-$6526.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. High byte of the current pattern stream position (low byte in voice_pattern_ptr_lo). Bytes $6527-$6529.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. High byte of the pattern restart address (low byte in voice_pattern_start_lo). Bytes $652A-$652C.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Current byte index into pulse_program_table for the voice's pulse-width program. Bytes $652D-$652F.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Index into pulse_program_table where the pulse-width program starts; script command $82 sets it, and each new note copies it into voice_pulse_index. Cleared to 0 at voice reset. Bytes $6530-$6532.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Chooses the pitch-program table: 0 reads pitch_program_a ($7184), nonzero reads pitch_program_b ($7277). Script commands $83 (sets 0) and $8D (sets nonzero) write it, and pattern command 6 ($6B23) sets it to 0. Bytes $6533-$6535.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Current byte index into the chosen pitch-program table. Bytes $6536-$6538.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Index where the pitch program starts, set by script commands $83 and $8D; each new note copies it to voice_pitch_pos when voice_pitch_enabled is nonzero and restart-mask bit 0 is clear. Bytes $6539-$653B.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Low byte of the address of the arpeggio note offsets the voice steps through (script command $84; points just after the two-byte header in arp_ptr_table's records). Bytes $653C-$653E; $653F-$6541 are not used.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. High byte of the arpeggio offsets address (low byte in voice_arp_ptr_lo). Bytes $6542-$6544.

Single byte. Start index into filter_sweep_table, set by script command $85 (first operand); copied to filter_index at a note start. sid_player_init's voice loop also stores 0 at $6548,x for X = 2 to 0, so it zeroes this byte, filter_index ($6549) and filter_step_lo ($654A); nothing else clears those two.
Single byte. Current byte index into filter_sweep_table.
Single byte. Low byte of the 16-bit amount added to the filter accumulator each frame (high byte in $654B). Loaded from filter_sweep_table.
Single byte. High byte of the filter step; see filter_step_lo.

Single byte. High byte of the filter accumulator's starting value, set by script command $85 (second operand, stored straight into filter_acc_hi too); copied into filter_acc_hi ($654E) at a note start.
Single byte. Low byte of the filter accumulator's starting value, set by script command $85 (third operand, stored straight into filter_acc_lo too); copied into filter_acc_lo ($654F) at a note start.

Single byte. High byte of the filter-cutoff accumulator; only its low three bits reach the SID. update_filter_sweep adds filter_step_hi to it, with the carry from $654F, each time it runs, and writes the value shifted right three times to $D416: bits 0-2 of $654E become the top three bits of $D416, above the top five bits of $654F, whose low three bits go to $D415.
Single byte. Low byte of the filter-cutoff accumulator (the byte added to first, with carry into $654E).

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Low byte of the address of the waveform bytes for the voice's one-shot sound, taken from the first two bytes of a record in sid_oneshot_defs. sid_voice_start_change patches it into the operand of its lda at $6E96. Bytes $6550-$6552.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Low byte of the address of the frequency bytes: waveform address plus the length. Patched into the operand of the lda at $6E88. Bytes $6553-$6555.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. High byte of the waveform address (low byte in voice_oneshot_wave_lo). Bytes $6556-$6558. dispatch_voice_command's lda $6557,x has $6557 as its base, but its X is the command byte ($80 up), so it reads voice_cmd_table_hi at $65D7, not these bytes.

Voice 1's and 2's bytes of voice_oneshot_wave_hi ($6556-$6558): script command $86 writes them and sid_voice_start_change reads them, indexed by the voice. dispatch_voice_command's lda $6557,x only uses $6557 as its base: X is the command byte, $80 or more, so it reads voice_cmd_table_hi at $65D7 onward.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. High byte of the frequency-bytes address (low byte in voice_oneshot_freq_lo). Bytes $6559-$655B.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Low byte of the address of the voice's note script, loaded from the song-script table at $7C3D by sid_load_song_voices (or $F5 after reset). tick_voice_script copies it to $F5. Bytes $655C-$655E; the high bytes are voice_script_ptr_hi.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. High byte of the voice's note script address. Bytes $655F-$6561.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Low byte of the voice's current SID frequency. It is loaded from note_freq_lo, changed by the pitch program, and written to $D400 by sid_write_frequency. Bytes $6562-$6564.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. High byte of the voice's current SID frequency (from note_freq_hi), written to $D401. Bytes $6565-$6567.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. The voice's current note: the byte read from the note script, an index into note_freq_lo and note_freq_hi. Bytes $6568-$656A.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Sequence script repeat counter. advance_voice_sequence keeps the same phrase playing while it counts down, then moves on; sequence command $F1 sets it. Bytes $656B-$656D.
Single byte. Offset in the pattern stream (relative to $F5/$F6) while music_voice_step reads one step; added to the stream pointer when the step ends (code at $6B3E).

Single byte. SID register offset of the voice being processed: 0, 7 or 14, copied from sid_voice_offsets by sid_update_voice_loop. The per-voice update code adds it to $D400 for its SID writes; sid_load_song_voices and sid_voice_change_check take the offset from sid_voice_offsets directly instead.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Attack/decay value of the voice, set by pattern command 2 and written to $D405. Bytes $6570-$6572 (no symbol existed; $6573 is voice_sustain_release).
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Sustain/release value of the voice, set by pattern command 2 and written to $D406. Bytes $6573-$6575.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Nonzero while the voice has a pitch program running. Script commands $83 and $8D, and pattern command 6, set it; music_voice_advance does nothing while it is zero. Bytes $6576-$6578.

Three bytes, one per voice ($6579-$657B). Only sid_init_voice_loop and sid_reset_voice_state write them, both storing zero, and no instruction reads them (no base reaches them with an index of 0 to 2), so the array is unused.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Nonzero while the voice plays an arpeggio (script command $84). While it is set, sid_voice_run skips the plain frequency lookup because the arpeggio writes the frequency itself. Bytes $657C-$657E. The neighbouring array $6579-$657B is only ever cleared.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Nonzero for the voice that owns the SID filter: it holds the value script command $85 wrote to $D417 (resonance and filter routing). The command clears all three before setting its own. Bytes $657F-$6581; update_filter_sweep only runs when no filtered voice is playing a one-shot sound.
Written by script_cmd_set_filter; the routines that index this array from its first byte read it (the references list which).
Written by script_cmd_set_filter; the routines that index this array from its first byte read it (the references list which). This is the byte at $6581.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Nonzero while a one-shot SID sound (script command $86) is playing on the voice: set from the record's sustain/release byte, cleared at each new note. While nonzero, sid_voice_run skips the pattern, pulse and arpeggio steps, and sid_voice_change_check steps the sound. Bytes $6582-$6584.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Set to 1 at each new note, so that sid_voice_run looks the note up in the frequency tables and refreshes voice_freq_lo/hi. Bytes $6585-$6587.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Nonzero makes voice_store_duration reuse voice_repeat_duration instead of reading a duration byte (script command $87 sets it, $88 clears it). Bytes $6588-$658A.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Set only by pattern command 5 (the handler at $6AE2): to its third operand when that is nonzero, or to 1 when it is zero (after the frequency is set to $FFFF). While nonzero it is also a note offset: sid_voice_run and the arpeggio step at $6D81 add it to voice_note and voice_transpose when they index note_freq_lo/hi. At the voice's next pattern step music_voice_step clears it and reloads voice_freq_lo/hi from voice_note plus voice_transpose, without the offset. Bytes $658B-$658D.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Transposition in semitones added to voice_note before every frequency lookup. Set by sequence command $F3 and cleared by advance_voice_sequence once the repeat counter has run out. Bytes $658E-$6590.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Low byte of the voice's pulse width: music_voice_pulse_sweep adds voice_pulse_delta to it each frame and writes it to $D402. Bytes $6591-$6593.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Low byte of the pulse width a note starts from (third operand of script command $82); copied into voice_pulse_lo when a new note starts, unless bit 1 of voice_restart_mask is set. Bytes $6594-$6596.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. High byte of the pulse width, written to $D403. Bytes $6597-$6599.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. High byte of the starting pulse width (second operand of script command $82). Bytes $659A-$659C.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Low byte of the pulse-width change added every frame, loaded from pulse_program_table. Bytes $659D-$659F.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. High byte of the pulse-width change per frame. Bytes $65A0-$65A2.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Low byte of the change added to voice_freq every frame, loaded from the pitch program. Bytes $65A3-$65A5.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. High byte of the per-frame pitch change. Bytes $65A6-$65A8.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Read position (offset from $F5) in the voice's note script; saved at the end of every script step. Bytes $65A9-$65AB.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Frames left before the arpeggio moves to its next note offset. Bytes $65AC-$65AE.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Frames per arpeggio step: first byte of the record (arp_pattern_0, arp_pattern_1). Bytes $65AF-$65B1.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Current step of the arpeggio; wraps to 0 at voice_arp_length. Bytes $65B2-$65B4.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Number of steps in the arpeggio: second byte of the record. Bytes $65B5-$65B7.
Single byte. Working copy of the filter accumulator's low byte while update_filter_sweep shifts the cutoff into $D416.
Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Number of steps of the voice's one-shot sound: the third byte of its sid_oneshot_defs record. Bytes $65B9-$65BB.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Steps of the one-shot sound played so far; sid_voice_start_change increments it, and the sound ends when it equals voice_oneshot_length. Bytes $65BC-$65BE.

Single byte. Nonzero while the master volume fades down. Set (with $65C0 and $65C1) to the same value by sequence command $F4 and by sid_start_fade_out ($6ED8), which the game calls to start a fade-out; sid_check_fade does the stepping.
Single byte. Frames left before the next volume step of a fade; reloaded from $65C1.
Single byte. Frames per volume step of a fade, in both directions.
Single byte. Master volume and filter mode as written to $D418: $1F after init, then counted down or up by the fades. Zero in the low nibble ends a fade-out by calling sid_silence_all.
Single byte. Nonzero while the volume fades up (sequence command $F5 stores the rate here and starts $65C2 at $10); sid_fade_in_step clears it when the volume reaches sid_fade_in_target.
Single byte. Volume the fade-up stops at, the second operand of sequence command $F5.

Per-voice array: three bytes, one for each SID voice 0 to 2, indexed by X. Bits that stop a new note restarting parts of the voice's sound (script command $89 sets it; sid_silence_all sets $FF). Bit 0: pitch program, bit 1: pulse-width program, bit 2: pattern stream, bit 3: filter program, bit 4: arpeggio. Bytes $65C5-$65C7.

Voice 1's byte of voice_restart_mask ($65C5-$65C7). sid_silence_all sets it to $FF directly; sid_reset_voice_state, sid_init_voice_loop and script command $89 (the handler at $6C16) write it through $65C5 indexed by the voice, and advance_voice_script reads it as $65C5,x when a new note starts.

Voice 2's byte of voice_restart_mask ($65C5-$65C7). sid_silence_all sets it to $FF directly; sid_reset_voice_state, sid_init_voice_loop and script command $89 (the handler at $6C16) write it through $65C5 indexed by the voice, and advance_voice_script reads it as $65C5,x when a new note starts.

Single byte of scratch for sid_load_song_voices. It keeps the position in the song list at $7C15 (X) across the call to sid_reset_voice_state, then briefly holds the voice number (Y) while X indexes sid_voice_offsets, and gives Y back before the next entry.

Low bytes of the handler addresses for the voice-script commands $80 to $8D (14 entries, $65C9-$65D6). dispatch_voice_command reads it as $6549,x with X = the command byte, which is why the label has the filter variable's address. Handlers: $80 6939 (next phrase of the sequence), $81 6B52 (select pattern from pattern_ptr_table), $82 6B70 (pulse program), $83 6B8A (pitch program A), $84 6BBC (arpeggio), $85 6C88 (filter), $86 6C24 (one-shot sound), $87 6BFA (fix duration), $88 6C0B (end fixed duration), $89 6C16 (restart mask), $8A 6EE7 (stop voice), $8B 6EF2 (new script address), $8C 6F06 (not code: it points into note_freq_lo, so the command is not used), $8D 6BA3 (pitch program B).
High bytes of the voice-script command handlers, 14 entries at $65D7-$65E4; read as $6557,x. Pairs with voice_cmd_table_lo.

Low bytes of the sequence-script command handlers for bytes $F0 to $F5, $65E5-$65EA; seq_run_command reads them as $64F5,x. Handlers: $F0 6996 (jump to a position), $F1 699F (repeat count), $F2 69AE (stop the voice), $F3 69BF (transpose), $F4 69CE (start fade-out), $F5 69E3 (start fade-in).
High bytes of the sequence-script command handlers, $65EB-$65F0, all $69; read as $64FB,x.

Low bytes of the seven pattern-stream command handlers, $65F1-$65F7: 0 6A53 (wait), 1 6A5F (jump), 2 6A73 (envelope), 3 6A92 (control byte, wait), 4 6AB8 (control byte, wait for the note length minus an amount), 5 6AE2 (control byte, wait, frequency flag), 6 6B23 (start a pitch program). music_voice_step patches the one it needs into the jmp at $6A50.
High bytes of the pattern-stream command handlers, $65F8-$65FE; pairs with pattern_cmd_table_lo.
SID register offset of each voice: 0, 7, 14 ($65FF-$6601), added to $D400 for voice 0, 1 and 2.
Default pattern stream for every voice (voice_pattern_ptr points here after a reset): command 0 wait $FF frames, then command 1 jump back to $6602. Five bytes, $00 $FF $01 $02 $66.

Sound start-up: clears the fade flags sid_fade_in_active and sid_fade_out_active and the filter resonance ($D417), sets sid_volume, sid_effects_enabled ($6501) and $D418 to $1F (volume 15 with the low-pass filter), then zeroes SID registers $D400-$D416 and $6530-$6546. The sound code's SID writes run from $6615 to $6EEE; the last, $D404,y at $6EEE, is in the $8A stop-voice handler at $6EE7, which the listing has not reached.

Starts a set of up to three sound voices from a song list. Does nothing if sid_effects_enabled ($6501) is zero. X is the position of the first entry in the list at $7C15; voice Y = 0 to 2 takes the entry at X+Y. An entry with bit 7 set is skipped; otherwise it is doubled and used to fetch a two-byte script pointer from $7C3D/$7C3E into $655C/$655F for that voice. It then calls sid_reset_voice_state and writes 0 to a SID control register: $D404 plus sid_voice_offsets indexed by the list position X, not by the voice. Only for a list that starts at position 0 is that the voice's own register; for a later list it reads the bytes after the table ($6602 on) and clears some other SID register. Which song or effect a list means is inferred.

Resets the sound-engine state for one voice slot (Y = 0..2). Sets the voice flag $FC+Y to 1, stores Y+1 in voice_script_timer ($6505+Y), and zeroes nine per-voice tables at Y: voice_transpose, voice_script_pos, voice_repeat_flag, voice_restart_mask, voice_pitch_enabled, f_6579, voice_arp_enabled, voice_oneshot_active and voice_freq_pending. It points the voice's pattern stream at sid_idle_pattern ($6602: 2 into voice_pattern_ptr_lo and voice_pattern_start_lo, $66 into the high bytes $6527/$652A) and clears voice_pulse_start ($6530+Y). Its only caller is sid_load_song_voices, before a voice starts its script.

Sound driver setup: sets busy flag $6502 (incremented here, cleared at $6781), then copies six bytes from $70BA,x ($70BA-$70BF plus the caller's x) into $651B-$6520. Zeroes per-voice state for voices 2 to 0 in $6515-$65C5 and calls $693F for each. Clears SID registers $D400-$D417, sets the per-voice flags $FC-$FE to 1, and loads $650x-$651x counters with 1, 2, and 3. If $65C3 is zero, sets volume $65C2 and SID $D418 to $1F.

Loop over voices 2, 1, and 0 using counter $FF: zeroes the per-voice arrays ($6515, $658E, $656B, $6588, $65C5, $6576, $6579, $657C, $6582, $6585), calls $693F, then stores 2 and $66 in $6521-$652A, 0 in $6530 and $6548, and $F5/$F6 in $655C/$655F.
Writes $08 then $00 to each SID register $D400-$D417 counting x down from $17, leaving every register at zero.
Clears the busy flag $6502 and returns; reached directly when $65C3 is nonzero, skipping the volume setup.

Per-frame sound driver step: returns at once if busy flag $6502 is nonzero. Otherwise walks voices 2 to 0 (counter $FF), loading the SID register offset from $65FF,x into $656F, and skips voices whose flag $FC,x is zero. Per active voice: optional call to $6828 when $65C3 is set, volume fade via $65BF, then the step routines $684C, $6A09, $6CBE, $6D81, and the frequency write. Finishes with $6E3E and a jump to $6DCE.
Starts a pass: sets the voice counter $FF to 2.
Top of the per-voice loop: loads x from $FF, copies the voice's SID offset $65FF,x to $656F, and jumps to sid_next_voice if the voice flag $FC,x is zero.
Active voice: calls $6828 when $65C3 is nonzero.

If fade flag $65BF is nonzero, decrements delay $65C0; when it reaches zero, reloads it from $65C1, decrements volume $65C2, and writes it to SID $D418. Jumps to $6EB0 when the low nibble of the new volume is zero; otherwise continues.

Calls $684C, then skips to sid_next_voice if $FC,x is zero or $6582,x is nonzero. Otherwise calls $6A09, $6CBE, and $6D81, and skips to sid_next_voice if $657C,x is nonzero. When $6585,x is set, clears it and looks up the voice's frequency: y = $6568,x + $658B,x + $658E,x indexes the tables $6F06 (low byte, to $6562,x) and $6F64 (high byte, to $6565,x).
Calls $6D08, then writes the voice's frequency low byte $6562,x and high byte $6565,x to SID registers $D400,y and $D401,y, where y is the offset saved in $656F.
Decrements the voice counter $FF and loops back to $6791 until it goes negative.
After the last voice: calls $6E3E, then jumps to $6DCE.

Volume fade-up step, the counterpart of the fade-down code at $67A8. Decrements the delay $65C0; when it reaches zero, reloads it from $65C1, increments the volume byte $65C2 and writes it to SID $D418 (master volume and filter mode). When the low nibble (the volume) equals the target in $65C4, clears $65C3, which stops the fade (inferred to be the fade-in flag).

Per-frame step of one music voice (X selects the voice). Decrements the note duration $6505,x and returns unless it hits zero. Then loads the voice's script pointer from $655C,x/$655F,x into $F5/$F6, runs advance_voice_script to read the next event, advances the script position $65A9,x and saves the pointer back.

Reads the next event for one music voice (X selects the voice, script pointer $F5, position in $65A9,x). A negative byte is a command, handled by dispatch_voice_command; $60 is a rest: it takes a duration and the script goes on, with no new note; any other byte becomes the new note in $6568,x, restarts the voice counters and, unless the voice's mask in $65C5,x says otherwise, re-arms the pattern, pulse, pitch, arpeggio and filter slots for it. The next byte, or the repeated value, is stored as the duration in $6505,x and the position is saved.

Common end of advance_voice_script: takes the duration from the next script byte (or reuses the saved one in $6508,x if the repeat flag $6588,x is set), stores it in $6505,x, and saves the script position in $65A9,x.

Handles a command byte (bit 7 set) in a voice script: looks the handler address up in voice_cmd_table_lo/hi, read as $6549,x/$6557,x with X = the command byte ($80-$8D), patches it into the jmp at $6936 (operand $6937/$6938), restores X from $FF and takes the jmp. The $6C88 (script_cmd_set_filter) that the jmp shows is only the last handler patched in before the snapshot.

Address inside the instruction at $6936: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction.

Address inside the instruction at $6936: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction. This is the byte at $6938.

Steps one voice's sequence (order list), with X = voice number from $FF. The sequence pointer comes from $651B/$651E,x into $F7/$F8 and the position from voice_seq_pos ($6515,x). It clears voice_script_pos, and clears voice_transpose if it is set while the repeat count voice_repeat_count ($656B,x) is zero. A sequence byte of $F0 or more is a command (seq_run_command); any other byte is a phrase number, whose address from phrase_ptr_lo/hi ($70CC/$70F5) goes into $F5/$F6 as the voice's new note script. A nonzero repeat count is decremented and the position stays put while it is still nonzero, so the phrase plays again; otherwise the position moves on one byte. Called from sid_init_voice_loop and from the stub at $6939 (voice-script command $80), which then reads the new phrase with advance_voice_script.
Counter spent (or zero): step the voice's script position on by one byte and return.

Sequence byte of $F0 or more is a command: the handler address is taken from seq_cmd_table_lo/hi, read as $64F5,x and $64FB,x with X = the command byte, and written into the operand of the jmp at $6993 (the bytes $6994/$6995); then X is restored from $FF and the jmp runs. The $69BF it shows in the snapshot is only the last handler patched in, that of command $F3 (transpose). Patching a jmp operand is the same trick dispatch_voice_command uses at $6936.

Address inside the instruction at $6993: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction.

Address inside the instruction at $6993: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction. This is the byte at $6995.

Voice sequence command handler, reached by jump from the command loop at $695F: reads the byte after the command from ($F7),y and stores it in voice_transpose ($658E,x), adds 2 to voice_seq_pos ($6515,x) (command byte and operand), and jumps back to $695F. Name is inferred from the destination table's name.

Sound engine: steps one voice's pattern stream (X selects the voice). Counts down voice_pattern_timer ($650B,x) and returns until it hits zero. If voice_freq_lookup ($658B,x) is set, it clears it and reloads voice_freq_lo/hi ($6562,x/$6565,x) from note_freq_lo/hi ($6F06/$6F64) indexed by voice_note plus voice_transpose. Then the voice's pattern pointer ($6521,x low, $6527,x high) goes into $F5/$F6 and the pattern bytes are read: each command byte indexes pattern_cmd_table_lo/hi ($65F1/$65F8) and the handler is patched into the jmp at $6A50 (operand $6A51/$6A52). Commands 1, 2 and 6 go back to $6A3C for the next byte; 0, 3, 4 and 5 set a new wait and end at voice_save_pattern_ptr. The $6AB8 the jmp shows is only the last handler patched in (command 4).

Address inside the instruction at $6A50: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction.

Address inside the instruction at $6A50: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction. This is the byte at $6A52.

Pattern-stream command 3 (reached through the patched jmp at $6A50, ends by jumping to voice_save_pattern_ptr at $6B3E). Reads two operand bytes from the pattern at ($F5),y: the first goes to $FB, the second to voice_pattern_timer ($650B,x), the frames until the voice's next pattern step. Then writes $FB to the voice's SID control register ($D404 plus the offset in $656F) if bit 3 (test bit) is set, and always writes it again with bit 3 cleared. The extra write with the test bit set resets the oscillator before the real waveform/gate value goes in (inferred from the SID register layout).

Common end of the pattern commands that wait (0 at $6A5C, 3 at $6AB5, 4 at $6ADF, 5 at $6B0E): adds one to sid_pattern_pos ($656E), then stores the 16-bit pointer ($F5/$F6 plus that position) in voice_pattern_ptr_lo/hi ($6521,x / $6527,x) for voice X, so the next pattern step starts after the bytes just read. Then returns.

Sound script command handler (inferred to be the SID filter setup command). Reads four parameter bytes through the script pointer ($F5),Y: the first goes to $6548, the next two are stored twice each at $654C/$654E and $654D/$654F, and the fourth is held on the stack. It saves the new script position in $65A9,X, clears $657F-$6581, writes the fourth byte to the SID filter control register $D417 (and to $657F,X), then jumps to advance_voice_script.

Sound engine: per-voice sweep of the SID pulse width. Counts down the step timer $650E,x. At zero it reads the next entry of the table at $711E using index $652D,x: a zero duration means loop, with the next byte as the new index. Otherwise it loads the duration, then a 16-bit delta into $659D,x and $65A0,x. Every call adds the delta to the 16-bit value in $6591,x and $6597,x, and writes it to the voice's SID registers +2 and +3 (pulse width low and high) at offset $656F. A pulse-width sweep, which gives the voice its moving tone.

Music engine: advances one voice (X = 0 to 2) by one frame. If the voice is enabled ($6576,x), counts down its note timer $6511,x; when it reaches zero it reads the next 3-byte event (duration, two data bytes) from the stream at $7277 or, when $6533,x is zero, from $7184, using the voice's position $6536,x. A zero duration byte is a jump: the next byte becomes the new stream position. The two data bytes go to $65A3,x and $65A6,x. Every frame it then adds that pair to the 16-bit accumulator $6562,x/$6565,x, which looks like the voice's pitch (slide or vibrato step); that reading is inferred.

Arpeggio step for one voice (voice number in X). Does nothing unless the voice's arpeggio flag $657C,x is set (script command $84 sets it). Otherwise counts down $65AC,x; on zero it reloads the count from $65AF,x (frames per step), reads the next semitone offset from the arpeggio record (pointer $653C/$6542,x, index $65B2,x), adds voice_note ($6568,x) and the offsets $658B,x and $658E,x, looks the sum up in note_freq_lo/hi ($6F06/$6F64) and writes the result to the voice's SID frequency registers ($D400/$D401 plus the voice offset in $656F). It then advances the index, wrapping to 0 at the record's step count $65B5,x.

Per-frame SID filter-cutoff sweep. Returns at once if $6501 is non-zero or if the highest-numbered voice with $657F,x non-zero has $6582,x non-zero (the loop stops at the first active voice, counting down from voice 2). Otherwise counts down $6514; when it expires it reads the next (length, step low, step high) triple from the table at $72C5 (a zero length is a jump: the next byte is the new index). Each frame the 16-bit step in $654A/$654B is added to the accumulator $654F (low)/$654E (high); bits 0-2 of the low byte go to $D415 and the sum shifted right three to $D416, the 11-bit filter cutoff. Purpose (a sound effect sweep) inferred from the register writes.

Sound engine: checks the three SID voices, X = 2 down to 0. A voice with $6582,x zero is skipped. If $65BC,x differs from $65B9,x it goes to sid_voice_start_change. If they match and $6501 is non-zero, it writes 0 to that voice's SID registers +4, +5 and +6 (waveform/gate, attack-decay, sustain-release), silencing the voice; $65FF,x gives the voice's register offset. Exact meaning of the $65B9/$65BC tables is inferred.

Voice has a pending change: saves the voice number in $6503 and the step in A (voice_oneshot_step, $65BC,x) in $6504, then copies table bytes from $6550/$6553/$6556/$6559,x into operands of later instructions at $6E89/$6E8A and $6E97/$6E98 (self-modifying code). It then loads Y from $65FF,x and X from $6504, and writes the byte of the voice's frequency data at that step (the patched lda at $6E88; the $6FFD the listing shows is only the last value patched in) to SID registers +0 and +1. The routine continues past this range.

Writes the new voice's start values to the SID. The operand of the lda at $6E88 is self-modified: sid_voice_start_change copied the voice's bytes from $6553,x and $6559,x into $6E89 and $6E8A, so the table address is chosen per voice. X is reloaded from $6504 (the table index saved earlier), and the byte read is written to both the frequency registers at $D400,y and $D401,y, where Y is the voice's register offset ($65FF). Then $08 goes to the control register $D404,y.

Address inside the instruction at $6E88: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction.

Address inside the instruction at $6E88: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. This is the byte at $6E8A.

Second table read of the voice start: the operand of this lda is also self-modified (from $6550,x and $6556,x via $6E97 and $6E98, which is why those two addresses are labelled). The byte, indexed by $6504, goes to the control register $D404,y. Then X is reloaded with the voice number ($6503), voice_oneshot_step ($65BC,x) is increased, X counts down and, if still non-negative, control returns to the voice loop at $6E40; otherwise it returns.

Test: leaves Z set when the three voice flag bytes $FC, $FD and $FE are all zero (ORs them into A). Called from the main loop at $8127, which keeps waiting while any voice flag is set. Reading the flags as 'voice is sounding' is inferred; sid_silence_all clears them.

Silences the sound chip and clears the voice state. Zeroes the three voice flag bytes $FC-$FE, $65BF and $65C3, writes 0 to the SID volume register $D418, sets $65C5-$65C7 to $FF, and writes $08 (test bit set, gate off) to the control registers of all three voices ($D404, $D40B, $D412).

Starts a fade-out: stores A in sid_fade_out_active ($65BF), sid_fade_delay ($65C0) and sid_fade_rate ($65C1), clears sid_fade_in_active ($65C3), and returns. Called with A = $19 from $40FC and with A = $25 from $82DC, $8B92, $8E2C and $A64B. The sequence command at $69CE stores a script byte into the same three bytes. What each of the three does in the fade is not traced here.

SID frequency low bytes, 94 entries ($6F06-$6F63), indexed by note number. Entries 1 to 93 are the equal-tempered notes C#0 to A7 (entry 57, $1D60, is A4 at 441.6 Hz on a PAL clock, and entry 93, $EB00, is twice entry 81); only entry 0 is out of place: $0578 where C0 would be about $0117. The index is the note byte of a script plus the transposition and arpeggio offsets.
SID frequency high bytes for the same 94 notes ($6F64-$6FC1); pairs with note_freq_lo.

Ten five-byte records ($6FC2-$6FF3) for the one-shot SID sounds started by script command $86. The command's operand is the record's byte offset (0, 5, 10 ...). Bytes: address of the waveform bytes (2), number of steps (1), sustain/release for $D406 (1), pulse width high for $D403 (1). The step data is in sid_oneshot_0_wave and sid_oneshot_data, and records may share blocks. Records 3 and 8 have sustain/release 0, so voice_oneshot_active stays 0 and they do not play.

Waveform bytes of one-shot sound 0 (9 steps, $6FF4-$6FFC): one byte per frame written to $D404 after a write of $08 (test bit); bit 7 noise, bit 6 pulse, bit 5 sawtooth, bit 4 triangle, bit 0 gate. The step data of the ten sounds follows in $6FFD-$70B9; no record reaches $7068-$707D or $7096-$70A3.

Step data of the one-shot sounds ($6FFD-$70B9). Each sound is a block of waveform bytes followed by the same number of frequency bytes; the byte at step n is written to both $D400 and $D401. The records in sid_oneshot_defs point into it and several share blocks: record 0 uses $6FF4 (9 steps, so its frequency bytes are $6FFD-$7005), records 1, 2 and 4 all use $7006 (12, 3 and 12 steps), record 3 uses $702A (3), record 5 $7030 (19), record 6 $7056 (9), record 7 $701E (9), record 8 $707E (12) and record 9 $70A4 (11).

Three sets of six bytes ($70BA-$70CB). A set holds the start addresses of the three voices' sequence scripts as little-endian words: $76B7, $7691, $7668 (set 0), $7891, $7800, $784A (set 1), $7B54, $7B3A, $7B26 (set 2). sid_player_init copies the set that starts at $70BA plus X into $651B-$6520; both callers in the code pass X = 6, so set 1 is the one used. $70BA-$70BF are the first set, labelled byte by byte.
High byte of voice 0's start address in set 0 ($76B7).
Low byte of voice 1's start address in set 0 ($7691).
High byte of voice 1's start address in set 0.
Low byte of voice 2's start address in set 0 ($7668).
High byte of voice 2's start address in set 0; the bytes up to $70CB are sets 1 and 2 with the same layout.

Low bytes of 41 phrase addresses ($70CC-$70F4). A byte below $F0 in a sequence script is an index into this table and its high-byte pair phrase_ptr_hi; the address becomes the voice's note script ($F5/$F6) that advance_voice_script then plays. The addresses run from $76C9 to $7BEE.
High bytes of the 41 phrase addresses ($70F5-$711D); pairs with phrase_ptr_lo.

Pulse-width programs ($711E-$7183, 102 bytes): three-byte steps of frame count, delta low, delta high, where the 16-bit delta is added to the voice's pulse width every frame for that many frames. A frame count of 0 is followed by a step index to jump to. Programs are entered at the index script command $82 gives; for example index 8 is +$0028 for 8 frames, -$0028 for 8 frames, then a jump back to index 8, a repeating pulse-width wobble.

Pitch programs, table A ($7184-$7276). Same format as pulse_program_table: frame count, delta low, delta high, with 0 and an index to jump. The delta is added to the voice's SID frequency every frame (music_voice_advance); small alternating deltas give a vibrato, for example the program entered at index 5: delta 0 for 25 frames (a delay), then from index 8 +8 for 3 frames, -8 for 6, +8 for 3, and a jump back to index 8. Selected by script command $83. The boundary with table B is where the label $7277 starts; indexes are bytes, so it is inferred.
Pitch programs, table B ($7277-$72B6): same format as pitch_program_a, selected by script command $8D.

Two arpeggio record addresses ($72B7-$72BA): $72BB and $72C1. Script command $84 picks one by index; the routine reads the high byte of both from $72B8, which works because both are in page $72. A record is the frames per step, the number of steps, then that many semitone offsets added to the note: arp_pattern_0 and arp_pattern_1.
Arpeggio record 0: 1 frame per step, 4 steps, offsets 0, 3, 7, 3 semitones ($72BB-$72C0).
Arpeggio record 1: 3 frames per step, 2 steps, offsets 0 and 2 semitones ($72C1-$72C4).

Filter-cutoff programs ($72C5-$7383, 191 bytes): three-byte steps of frame count, step low, step high, where the 16-bit step is added to the cutoff accumulator every frame. A frame count of 0 is followed by a step index to jump to. Programs are entered at the index script command $85 gives; update_filter_sweep reads it only when sid_effects_enabled is zero.

49 pattern stream addresses as little-endian words ($7384-$73E5), from $73E6 to $765C. Script command $81 takes the pattern number, doubles it, and copies the word into voice_pattern_start_lo and voice_pattern_start_hi.

Pattern streams, from $73E6 to the sequence scripts at $7668: byte sequences interpreted by music_voice_step through pattern_cmd_table_lo/hi, with command numbers 0 to 6 and their operands (wait, jump, envelope, control byte). The first stream starts: command 2 (attack/decay $00, sustain/release $C9), command 5 (control byte $89, wait 1, frequency flag 0).

List read by sid_load_song_voices at $663A: the byte at $7C15+X+Y is voice Y's number into voice_script_table, or has bit 7 set ($80) when the slot is unused. The 40 bytes $7C15-$7C3C are ten groups of four, one per sound: every request queued through $0B8C is a multiple of 4 from 0 to $24, so all ten are used, and the fourth byte of each group (0) is never read, since only Y = 0 to 2 are taken.

Table of ten note script addresses, words low byte first, $7C3D-$7C50: $7C51, $7C5C, $7C67, $7C72, $7C7D, $7C88, $7C93, $7C9A, $7CA5 and $7CB2. sid_load_song_voices doubles the number from song_voice_list and copies the word's two bytes to voice_script_ptr_lo ($655C,y) and voice_script_ptr_hi ($655F,y), Y being the voice.
High byte of the first word of voice_script_table ($7C, giving $7C51); the other nine words follow at $7C3F-$7C50.

The ten note scripts that voice_script_table points to, $7C51-$7CBC (108 bytes). Command bytes $81, $82, $83, $84 and $8A, $8D are sound-engine commands run by tick_voice_script; $84 starts an arpeggio.

Sort list for the logical sprites: an entry is filed at position Y / 2 of its screen line, or at the next free position after it, so walking the list from the start gives top-to-bottom order. A position holding $00-$7E holds an entry number; $FF marks a free position, and $7F, written one past the highest position used, ends the list.

Entry 1 of sprite_y_buckets (position Y / 2 on the screen line, one byte for each); many routines write it through $7CBD,x. $FF marks an empty position; $7F is the end-of-list marker, which j_A43A stores at $7CBE plus sprite_bucket_max, so it reaches this entry only when that maximum is 0.

Status line cell: the stage number as a digit tile, written by draw_status_stage ($8353) as stage ($08E7) + $C2 (tile $C1 is digit 0, so stage 0 shows 1). Row 21, column 13 of the panel screen at $7C00.

Eleven status line cells $7F58-$7F62 (row 21, columns 16 to 26) drawn by draw_segment_gauge from the value in $08A1: cells left of value / 4 get tile $D7, cells right of it $D5 (the empty cell), and the edge cell a partial tile from gauge_tiles ($0434) by the value's low two bits. With $08A1 = 0 in the saved state all eleven show $D5; the saved state also shows $D4 at the left end of the row and $D6 at the right end.
Five status line cells $7F69-$7F6D (row 21, columns 33 to 37), the label written by draw_status_label from the 9-byte records at $FFC2 (each byte plus $A5).

Status line cell written with tile $C1 (digit 0) by draw_status_lives ($8347): the first digit of the lives pair. update_status_line calls it each frame unless player_hit ($0292) is set; $80BA and $A862 call it too. Row 23, column 1.

Status line cell for the lives counter: draw_status_lives ($8347) stores lives_tile ($089D) here, each frame through update_status_line unless player_hit ($0292) is set, and when called from $80BA and $A862. Row 23, column 2.
Status line cell, row 23 column 4: update_status_line copies $089E here each frame unless player_hit ($0292) is set (a digit tile, $C1 at the start).
Status line cell, row 23 column 5: update_status_line copies $089F here each frame unless player_hit ($0292) is set (digit tile).
Status line cell of the level clock's minute digit: draw_level_timer stores $0899 + $C1 here. Row 23, column 22.
Status line cell of the clock's tens of seconds: draw_level_timer stores $089A + $C1 here. Row 23, column 24.
Status line cell of the clock's units of seconds: draw_level_timer stores $089B + $C1 here. Row 23, column 25.
Five status line cells $7FB9-$7FBD (row 23, columns 33 to 37) that update_status_line fills with the score digits copied from $08D0-$08D4. The two blank cells after them ($B8) are not written.

Sixty-four bytes $7FC0-$7FFF made of the pattern $FF $FF $00 $00 $00 $00 $FF $FF repeated. It lies in the last 64 bytes of the panel screen at $7C00 (the last eight bytes at the place of the screen's sprite pointers). No routine in the listing reads or writes it.
Start of a game: initialise, set the CIA 2 timer for the per-frame NMI, wait for raster line $EE, blank the screen and enter the stage.

Address inside the instruction at $8000: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Calls nmi_and_first_copy ($5271), then loads the CIA 2 timer A latch with $4CC7 (19655; low byte $C7 at $DD04, high byte $4C at $DD05), the interval for the per-frame NMI. The timer runs latch + 1 = 19656 cycles, one PAL frame of 312 lines of 63 cycles.

This is the byte at $800A.
Loads $4C, the high byte of the per-frame timer interval $4CC7, for the CIA 2 timer A latch.

Stores the high byte $4C in the CIA 2 timer A latch ($DD05), completing the interval $4CC7 for the per-frame NMI.

Address inside the instruction at $800D: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. cart_copy reads it as the base of an indexed table (lda $800E,x at $0138, with ROM bank 0 selected), the destination high byte of a cartridge directory entry; it is not a patched operand of the RAM instruction.

Address inside the instruction at $800D: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction. This is the byte at $800F.

Begins a new game after the title. Waits for raster line $EE, writes $91 to CIA 2 control register A ($DD0E), blanks the screen by clearing $D011, sets the stage number $08E7 to 0 and $089C to 2, and calls new_game_defaults. Then it turns on the raster interrupt ($D01A = 1), clears $DD00 (selects the video bank), clears cheat_flag and $08C1, $08BF and $0294, and jumps to $403A in the stage intro. The meaning of $089C, $08C1 and $08BF is not established here.
A stage begins: stage_start loads it from the cartridge, then the round starts.

A round begins (at a stage's start and after losing a life): stop the interrupts, reset the frame state, count $089D down (below $C1 the game is over: $BD5D, then back to the title at $4000), start the sound, set the raster interrupt to irq_panel_on ($BCE1) at line $DE, set up the stage, then wait 20 frames.

The main loop, once a frame: count the frame, scan the keyboard ($5290) for as long as $02CA holds the game paused, run the game's updates ($A178 to $5B83), count down $0293 after a life is lost and restart the round at 0, then wait for the frame.

Address inside the instruction at $8107: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction.

Address inside the instruction at $810D: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction.

Main-loop call of place_player_sprites. The auto label f_8113 comes from two reads of the table of stage pointers in bank 0 at $8113 ($0B46 and $4F6C, with the cartridge bank 0 switched in by $DE00); nothing in RAM writes to this instruction, so the call is never patched.

Address inside the instruction at $8116: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction.

Address inside the instruction at $811C: the label sits on an operand byte, not on an instruction start. Other code refers to this address (an indexed table or buffer base, a patched operand, or a jump into the middle of the instruction; the references show which); the routine that contains it is commented at its first instruction.

Per-frame check of $0293 (death_countdown): if it is zero skips ahead to $8134; otherwise calls sid_any_voice_active ($6EA9) and, while no voice is sounding, counts $0293 down (inferred reading of the branch).

Death-countdown tail of the main loop, reached when death_countdown ($0293) is non-zero: calls sid_any_voice_active ($6EA9); if any voice flag is set, jumps to wait_nmi and waits. Otherwise decrements death_countdown and, when it reaches zero, jumps to round_start ($804F); if not, falls to wait_nmi ($8134). So the next round starts only after the sound has finished (inferred from the flag test).

Wait for the interrupt to set frame_flag ($08F7), then choose the next frame's raster interrupt: sprite_reuse_irq ($95A4) at the line spr_min_free_line returns when sprite_more ($6B) is non-zero, otherwise irq_panel ($837E) at line $D5. Then copy the sprite tables the game fills into the set the interrupts draw from: pointers, free lines and X/Y ($07C7-$07E6) to $07E7-$0806, colours ($07B4-$07BB) to $07BF-$07C6, and the enable, X high bit and expand images ($07B2, $07B1, $07B3) to $07BD, $07BC and $07BE. Then calls build_vic_shadows and falls into enable_frame_nmi.

Writes $81 to the CIA 2 interrupt control register ($DD0D), which enables the timer A interrupt (the per-frame NMI), loads X with 1 and falls into wait_frame. Reached only by fall-through from wait_nmi at $8191. The three jsr $8194 in the program (stage_load $0A9B, copy_three_cart_entries $51E4, nmi_and_first_copy $5285) run with $01 = $37, so they reach the cartridge's routine at $8194, not this RAM copy.

Wait for frame_flag to change from the value wait_nmi read (Y), clear it (X is 1 from enable_frame_nmi) and allow interrupts. Then test bit 5 (retired) of obj_state ($3592) of the stage's goal object, whose number is in $08CC, and store the result in all_move_flag ($94). When it is set the stage is cleared: increment stage, set up the sprites and go to stage_intro_start ($4016). Otherwise go on with the frame: copy the logical sprite lists to the interrupt's tables, stream data and run the per-frame routines.

Per-frame status line update. Returns at once if player_hit is non-zero, so the clock stops while the player is dying. Otherwise calls $8347 (stores $C1 at $7F99 and $089D at $7F9A), copies the five bytes $08D0-$08D4 to $7FB9-$7FBD and $089E/$089F to $7F9C/$7F9D, then falls into level_timer_tick. The copied values are probably score or counter digits already in tile form (inferred).

Level countdown timer. Called once by round_start ($80B7) and entered every main-loop pass from update_status_line, which skips it while player_hit is set. $0898 counts passes down from $19 (25); each wrap ticks the clock digits $089B (units, 9..0), $089A (tens, 5..0) and $0899 (minutes) down like a minutes:seconds display. When the minutes go below zero the time has run out: the digits are set to zero and the player is killed here (player_hit and jump_state $FF, see $82B8), sound $24 is queued with queue_sound ($0B8C), the music fades out through sid_start_fade_out when $DF is non-zero, and hit_save_pos ($8E2F) runs. Every path ends in draw_level_timer.
Time is up: zero the clock digits, clear player_mode, set jump_state and player_hit to $FF (the same flags a hit sets, so the player dies) and jump_counter to $10, then play sound $24.

If $DF (music_mode) is non-zero (queue_sound refuses new effects then), the music is faded out instead: sid_start_fade_out ($6ED8) is called with A = $25, which goes into sid_fade_out_active, sid_fade_delay and sid_fade_rate. Then hit_save_pos records where the player died.

Draws the clock: each digit ($0899, $089A, $089B) plus $C1 is stored in the status-line cells $7FAE, $7FB0 and $7FB1 (the cell between them, $7FAF, is skipped; the $C1 digit base is read from the code, the glyphs are not checked here). Carry is clear going in, so the adds do not chain.

Reached from draw_level_timer when the clock's minute digit $0899 is zero, so the last minute. Chooses colour $0E or $0A from bit 2 of frame_count, so it alternates every four frames, and writes it to the five colour RAM bytes $DBA8-$DBAC. The cells are probably the clock's label next to the digits, a time-running-out warning (inferred).

Draws an 11-cell bar gauge into the status line at $7F58-$7F62 from the value in gauge_value ($08A1). The value divided by 4 is the whole-cell count: cells above it get tile $D5, cells below it get tile $D7, and the boundary cell gets a partial tile fetched from $0434 indexed by the low two bits of the value (four fill steps). The value is the health of the stage's goal object: track_stage_section ($92EF) stores the low 5 bits of its obj_health in $08A1 and calls this routine while $08CB is non-zero; round_start calls it once at $80BD.

Writes the lives display on the status line: status_lives_tens ($7F99) gets $C1 (the digit 0 tile) and status_lives_digit ($7F9A) gets lives_tile ($089D). Called from update_status_line and from $80BA and $A862.
Writes the stage digit on the status line: stage ($08E7) plus $C2 goes to status_stage_digit ($7F55), so stage 0 shows as 1. Called once per round by round_start at $80B1.

Writes a five-character label into the status line cells $7F69-$7F6D. Scans 9-byte records starting at $FFC7 (X steps by 9, skipping records whose byte at $FFC7+X has bit 6 set), then copies five bytes from $FFC2+X, each plus $A5, as screen tile codes. What the text is (and what picks the record) is not established here, so the name is neutral; called once per round by round_start at $80B4.

Raster interrupt at line $D5, the top of the status panel. Waits for line $D6, then sets $D011 = $57: extended colour and multicolour together, a mode the VIC-II shows as black, which hides the switch to the panel's video bank ($DD00 = $02), screen and character set ($D018 = $FF) and colours. Moves all sprites to x = 0, out of sight, chains irq_panel_on for line $DE, and calls sound_frame.

New-game start values, called once by game_start ($802B). Puts $C6 (digit 5) in lives_tile ($089D), $C1 (digit 0) in $089E, $089F and the score digits $08D0-$08D4, $CC in shown_buf_hi ($08C0) and $C8 in back_buf_hi ($08C2). Sets player_facing ($18) to 7, clears $11, $08A0 and $D01B (so every sprite is drawn in front of the background), sets $10 to 1 and move_step ($0A) to 2. Writes $31 to $D018 (screen and character memory layout) and $10 to $D016 (multicolour on, 38 columns, no fine scroll).

Once a frame, update the pool of nine short-lived objects, temp_first ($16) to temp_first + 8 (stage 1: $4C-$54), from the last slot down. Y is the slot and indexes the velocities ($3FD3/$3FDC X, $3FE5/$3FEE Y) and life ($3FF7). For each slot not retired: bit 7 of $35EF makes it blink (bit 6 cleared on frames whose parity matches bit 0, set on the others); it moves only when $3484 shares a bit with move_mask. A move counts the life down (at zero it is retired with $A0), adds the velocity, and runs object_arc_step when $3F19 is non-zero. With bit 3 of obj_state set, $9400 (A = $0C, Y = $0A) is tested; if either low bit is set the object is retired or, with bit 2 set, becomes animation $37 (obj_anim_num) with life $18, motion cleared, and the routine returns. Then $B57A, and the view test ($40-$47): left, right or below retires; above retires only when $3F19 is zero. A survivor's position is stored and set_object_hitbox ($ABC7) run.

Once a frame, read the joystick and run the player. It writes $7F to both CIA 1 ports, reads port A (port B instead when A reads $7F), keeps the low four bits in joy_bits ($08), and copies the fire bit (bit 4) into bit 6 of $08C6 (1 means not pressed). Before that it tests a hidden combination: when port A ($DC00, joystick 2) has bits 0 and 4 low (up and fire) and port B ($DC01, joystick 1) has bits 1 and 4 low (down and fire), it increments cheat_flag ($08F9) and the background colour ($D021), once for each frame they are held. With port A at $7F the keys left arrow and space also pull port B bits 1 and 4 low. It then decrements $08DE unless its bit 7 is set, saves the previous position with save_player_x and save_player_y, runs player_mode_step ($85DC), sets $19 to $FF, calls $AF34 (skipped while bit 6 of $08C6 is set), $98F3, and $9F05 (skipped while bit 7 of $08C6 is set), picks the animation frame with player_pose ($413A), and ends in $92DF.

Run the player's movement for the current player_mode ($09). Mode 1 goes to $9025, and modes other than 0 and 1 go to $8E88. Mode 0 first rewrites $08C6: $40 when fire is not pressed (bit 6 set), otherwise $00 while $08FA is non-zero and $80 when it is zero; then it runs $8603, which reads joy_bits, and goes on to $89A9.

Mode 0 movement for one frame, called from player_mode_step. Reads joy_bits ($08), fire_flags ($08C6), and jump_state ($08FA). While player_hit ($0292) is non-zero it goes to player_hit_step. Calls $8D67 unless $1A is negative. On the ground: down ($0D) goes to player_down_enter_mode1, right ($07) to player_walk_right, left ($0B) to player_walk_left, down-right ($05) and down-left ($09) to player_down_right and player_down_left when $0C is zero (when $0C is non-zero they go to player_stop_facing if bit 7 of $08C6 is set, otherwise they walk right or left), up-right ($06) and up-left ($0A) to the jump routines (walks instead while bit 7 of $08C6 is set), and up ($0E) to player_jump_up only while bit 7 of $08C6 is clear (with it set, up is idle). In the air only right and left count. Anything else sets move_dir ($0D) to $FF and $0299 to 0, then runs player_jump_motion when airborne or sets $0905 to 1 when on the ground.

Start a jump to the right (joy_bits $06). When jump_state ($08FA) is non-zero it goes to walk_right_dir instead. Otherwise it calls $42F8 (adds move_step to player_try_x, skipped while bit 7 of $08C6 is set), loads A with 6, and falls into player_jump_start.

Shared tail of the jumps: stores A in move_dir ($0D), calls $0B8C with A at 0, and clears bit 7 of obj_flags ($364C) for the object whose index is in $1A when $1A is not negative. Then sets $1A and jump_state ($08FA) to $FF, $0299 and $0C to 0, $0903 to 1, and $0905 to 3, and copies $08FC into jump_counter ($08FB). player_jump_motion then lifts the player by $02CE steps until jump_counter runs out.

Start a jump to the left (joy_bits $0A). When jump_state ($08FA) is non-zero it goes to walk_left_dir instead. Otherwise it calls $42E1 (subtracts move_step from player_try_x, skipped while bit 7 of $08C6 is set), loads A with $0A, and goes to player_jump_start.

Down-left on the ground, entered with A at $09. Stores A in move_dir ($0D) and $18, sets $0B to 1 and $0905 to 5, and loads A with $FF, then joins player_walk_left at walk_left_move, so $0299 becomes $FF and the player steps left.

Down-right on the ground, entered with A at $05. Stores A in move_dir ($0D) and $18, sets $0B to 1 and $0905 to 5, and loads A with $FF, then joins player_walk_right at walk_right_move, so $0299 becomes $FF and the player steps right.

Step right. On the ground ($08FA zero) it sets $0905 to 1. Sets move_dir ($0D) to $07 and $0299 to 0, then calls $42F8, which adds move_step ($0A) to player_try_x unless bit 7 of $08C6 is set. When $0C is non-zero it goes to player_slope_step. Otherwise it sets move_step to 2 and, when jump_state is non-zero, goes on to player_jump_motion.

Step left. On the ground ($08FA zero) it sets $0905 to 1. Sets move_dir ($0D) to $0B and $0299 to 0, then calls $42E1, which subtracts move_step ($0A) from player_try_x unless bit 7 of $08C6 is set. When $0C is non-zero it goes to player_slope_step. Otherwise it sets move_step to 2 and, when jump_state is non-zero, goes on to player_jump_motion.

Vertical step that goes with a horizontal one when $0C is non-zero (A holds $0C). Ends in $430F (subtracts move_step from player_try_y) or $4326 (adds it), whichever the direction calls for, and the rts of that routine returns to the caller, so no jump motion follows. With $0C equal to 1 the player goes down when bit 3 of move_dir ($0D) is set (moving left) and up when it is clear (moving right). With any other value it goes up when moving left and down when moving right. $430F and $4326 do nothing while bit 7 of $08C6 is set.

Movement after a hit (player_hit non-zero). Does nothing while $0293 is non-zero. While jump_state ($08FA) is negative, or while $08ED plus $0F (added without clearing the carry first) is below $EB, it goes to player_jump_motion. Otherwise it sets $0293 to $19, the countdown that the main loop at $8122 uses to reach round_start.

Vertical motion of a jump, using jump_state ($08FA) and jump_counter ($08FB) on player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE). A jump_state of 0 does nothing. A negative one (rising) clears bit 0 of move_dir ($0D), subtracts $02CE[x] from player_try_y, where x is jump_counter limited to 16, and subtracts the same amount from jump_counter. When jump_counter would reach zero or below it sets jump_state to 1 and jump_counter to 0. A positive one (falling) clears bit 1 of move_dir, adds $02DF[x] with x as jump_counter, and raises jump_counter by one until it reaches 8.

Down pressed on the ground. Goes to player_stop when bit 7 of $08C6 is set. Otherwise it calls $9E69 and goes to player_stop when bit 4 of $08E9 is clear. Otherwise it sets $0322 to $12, adds $15 to player_y ($08B9/$08BA), adds $E1/$E2 to player_x ($08B7/$08B8), sets $08FF to $44, clears player_third_on ($0913), $0B, $0900, and $0323, sets player_mode ($09) to 1 and move_step ($0A) to 2, stores $0D in both $18 and move_dir ($0D), and sets $0905 to 6.
Stores A in $18, then runs player_stop. Reached from player_move with A at $05 or $09 when $0C is non-zero and bit 7 of $08C6 is set.
Stand still: sets move_dir ($0D) and $0299 to $FF and $0905 to 4. No position changes.
Start a straight-up jump (joy_bits $0E). When jump_state ($08FA) is non-zero it goes to player_jump_motion. Otherwise it loads A with $0E and goes to player_jump_start, with no horizontal step.

Set up the tables for a stage, called at $8049. Clears section_index ($0298), sets the sprite multicolour enable $D01C to $FF, and copies the 22 bytes at $0C0C-$0C21 to $2A-$3F. Points $24/$25 at $0D22 and loads $26/$27 from the word stored there. Copies $0C03, $0C04, and $0C05 to bg_colour0, bg_colour1, and bg_colour2 ($08C3-$08C5, written to the three VIC background colour registers $D021-$D023 by nmi_frame at $4DB1), and sets the sprite multicolours $D025 and $D026 to $0B and $0F.

Count scroll_phase ($0E) down once a frame (called from the main loop at $825F). Does nothing when scroll_phase is negative. Otherwise it decrements it. When the old value was 1 it jumps to $5BC2. When the old value was 0 (now $FF) and player_hit ($0292) is zero, it reads the address from the tables $0324 (low) and $032C (high) at the index scroll_dir ($0F), stores it in $E1/$E2, and jumps through it at jump_via_e1. Any other old value just returns.

Jump through the address in $E1/$E2 (jmp ($00E1)). scroll_phase_step runs into it, and a jsr to it (as at $B224, after loading $E1/$E2 from the tables at $B33C and $B35F) lets the target's rts return to the caller.

Build the copies of the VIC registers that nmi_frame writes out at $4DAB-$4DCC (apply_vic_shadows). shadow_d018 ($07B0, for $D018) gets $21 when $10 is zero and $31 otherwise. shadow_d016 ($07AF, for $D016) gets $10 combined with scroll_fine_x ($06). shadow_d011 ($07AE, for $D011) gets $10 combined with scroll_fine_y ($07). Called at $8191.

Apply one frame of vertical motion to an object's new position (E9/EA) according to obj_arc_state ($3F19 for the object in X, passed in the flags). With bit 7 and bit 6 set it falls: the position moves down by a value from $02DF indexed by obj_arc_counter ($3F76), which rises by one up to 8 (so it speeds up). With bit 7 set and bit 6 clear it rises by a value from $02CE indexed by the counter (at most 16), the counter falls by the same amount, and when it runs out obj_arc_state becomes $C0 (falling). With bit 7 clear it works out a move along a path through the data at the pointer $32 and, for a follower, stores the offset from its parent in $36F4 and $3748; that path is not decoded.

Path case of object_arc_step (obj_arc_state has bit 7 clear). Saves X (the object) in $EB and Y in $ED, calls path_advance with A as obj_arc_state, and restores X and Y. When bit 6 of obj_flags ($364C) is set it then stores $E7 minus $08DA in obj_off_x ($36F4) and $E9 minus $08DC in obj_off_y ($3748).

Advance an object one step along its path. A is obj_arc_state (an offset into the table of path addresses at the pointer $32) and X is the object. Loads $E3/$E4 with the word at $32 plus A, copies obj_arc_counter ($3F76) into $EC, and uses that as the slot in path_end ($5C), path_axes ($60), and path_pos ($64). When path_end is below path_pos the path is over (path_finish). Otherwise path_axes 0 adds one word of path data to the X position $E7/$E8, 1 adds one word to the Y position $E9/$EA, and 2 or more adds an X word then a Y word, reading at offset path_pos.

Add the next word of path data to the Y position $E9/$EA. The data is at $E3/$E4 plus Y; a low byte of $80 restarts at offset 0. Y is advanced by two and stored in path_pos ($64) at the slot in $EC. Entered by path_advance when path_axes is 1, and after path_add_x when it is 2 or more.

Add the next word of path data to the X position $E7/$E8. The data is at $E3/$E4 plus Y; a low byte of $80 restarts at offset 0. Y is advanced by two and stored in path_pos ($64) at the slot in $EC. Called by path_advance, which enters it directly when path_axes is 0.
End of a path: clears obj_arc_state ($3F19) for the object in $EB and returns.

Second half of mode 0 movement, reached from player_move. Checks the new position that player_move left in player_try_x and player_try_y against the blocks. While player_hit ($0292) is non-zero it goes to restore_player_pos ($4246). On the ground (jump_state $08FA zero) it looks at move_dir ($0D): with bit 3 clear it goes to collide_ground_right, with bit 3 set and bit 2 clear to collide_ground_left, and otherwise it returns. In the air it goes by move_dir: $05 to air_down_right_x, $09 to air_down_left_x, $0D to air_vertical, $0E to $8D10, $06 to $8CDF, and $0A to $8CF6. Any other value returns.

Ground check for a step to the left (move_dir with bit 3 set and bit 2 clear). When slope_kind ($0C) is non-zero it goes to $8C60. Otherwise it calls $9BF6, merges $E1, $E2, and $E3 into $E1, and tests bit 0 (solid). If it is set, save_player_x ($4263) copies player_x over player_try_x, so the step is dropped. If it is clear, restore_player_x ($4249) copies player_try_x into player_x, so the step stands. Either way it goes on to ground_floor_check.

Check what is under the player after a ground step. Returns at once when stand_obj ($1A) is not negative. Otherwise it calls $9D3C. If bit 5 is set in all three of $E1, $E2, and $E3, it clears $08FF, sets $0B, player_mode ($09), and move_step ($0A) to 1, 1, and 2, sets $0905 to 5, and returns (the player enters mode 1). Otherwise, if $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set, it stores those two bits shifted down in slope_kind ($0C) and returns. If not, and no block has bit 0 set and stand_obj is still negative (the probe found no platform), it starts a fall: jump_counter ($08FB) becomes 1, $0299 becomes 0, jump_state ($08FA) becomes 1, and $0905 becomes 3.

Ground check for a step to the right (move_dir with bit 3 clear). Same as collide_ground_left, but a non-zero slope_kind ($0C) goes to $8CAB and the block probe is $9C1E. A solid block drops the step through ground_x_blocked, and a free one commits it with restore_player_x ($4249) before going on to ground_floor_check.

Airborne step down and to the left (move_dir $09). Pushes $031D, subtracts the fall step $02DF[jump_counter] from it, calls $9BF6 with the smaller value, and puts $031D back. Then it merges $E1, $E2, and $E3 and tests bit 0. A solid block drops the step with save_player_x ($4263), and a free one commits it with restore_player_x ($4249). Both ways it ends in air_vertical.
Airborne step down and to the right (move_dir $05). Same as air_down_left_x, but the block probe is $9C1E instead of $9BF6. Both ways it ends in air_vertical.
Vertical check for an airborne player: calls air_floor_check, then goes on to $8D20.

Decide what the blocks under an airborne player do, then commit or adjust player_prev_y. It calls $9D3C. If bit 5 is set in all three of $E1, $E2, and $E3, it sets $0905 to 5, $0B and player_mode ($09) to 1, ORs 3 into $18, copies $18 to move_dir ($0D), and goes to land_and_snap (mode 1 is entered). Otherwise it merges the three: with bit 1 set it goes to air_hit_hazard. If $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set it goes to $8C0B. When stand_obj ($1A) is not negative it goes to air_on_object. Otherwise bit 0 (solid) goes to air_land_solid. With bit 0 clear and bit 6 set it sets player_mode to 2, jump_state to $FF, jump_counter to $30, and $0905 to 7. In both bit 0 clear cases it then commits the new Y with restore_player_y ($4256).

Land on a stage object: sets $0905 to 1, calls player_land, and sets player_try_y to obj_hit_top for the object stand_obj ($1A), minus $031C and $031D. Then it commits the Y with restore_player_y ($4256).

Harmful block under the player (bit 1 set): sets player_hit ($0292) to 1, jump_state ($08FA) to $FF, and jump_counter ($08FB) to $10. Sound $24 is queued with queue_sound ($0B8C); when $DF is non-zero (queue_sound refuses it then) the music is faded out instead through sid_start_fade_out ($6ED8, A = $25). Then it goes to hit_save_pos ($8E2F).

Landing on a solid block. When up is held (bit 0 of joy_bits $08 clear) and fire is not pressed (bit 6 of fire_flags $08C6 set), the player jumps again at once: jump_state ($08FA) becomes $FF, jump_counter ($08FB) is loaded from $08FC, sound 0 is queued, and $0905 becomes 3. Otherwise $0905 becomes 1 and player_land runs. Either way it continues in snap_player_to_block.

Snap the player's feet to a block boundary. Adds $031C and $031D to player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE), rounds the sum down to a multiple of $10, subtracts $031D and $031C again, and stores the result in player_try_y. Then it commits the Y with restore_player_y ($4256).
Mark the player as on the ground: jump_state ($08FA) and slope_kind ($0C) become 0, and $0902 and move_dir ($0D) become $FE.

Address inside the instruction at $8C05 (sta $0902 in player_land): the label sits on an operand byte. Its one reference is jsr $8C07 at $4033 in stage_intro_start, made with $01 = $37, so it runs the cartridge's code at $8C07 (in whichever bank $DE00 last selected), not these RAM bytes. What that cartridge routine does is not read here.

Slope check for an airborne player, entered from air_floor_check when $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set. When bit 0 of $0291 is set it goes straight to air_slope_land. Otherwise it takes (player_try_x $08BB plus $1F) AND $0F into $E2, and turns that into $0F minus itself when bit 3 of $0291 is clear. Then it compares ((player_try_y $08BD AND $0E) plus 1 plus $031C plus $031D) AND $0F with $E2. If that is smaller it goes to air_slope_commit, because the feet are still above the slope. If not, it falls into air_slope_land.

Land on a slope from the air: move_dir ($0D) becomes $FF, jump_state ($08FA) becomes 0, slope_kind ($0C) becomes 1 when bit 2 of $0291 is set and 2 otherwise, and $0905 becomes 1. Then player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE) is increased by 1 and it falls into air_slope_commit.
Commit the step: goes to restore_player_pos ($4246), which copies player_try_x and player_try_y into player_x and player_y.

Ground step to the left while slope_kind ($0C) is non-zero, entered from collide_ground_left. When slope_kind is 1 it goes to ground_slope_left_one. Otherwise it calls $9D3C and, if $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set (still on a slope), goes to ground_slope_commit. If not, it adds 6 to player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE) and goes to land_and_snap.

Ground step to the right with slope_kind ($0C) not equal to 1, reached from ground_slope_right. Calls $9D3C and, if $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set, goes to ground_slope_commit. Otherwise it goes to land_and_snap with player_try_y unchanged.

Ground step to the left with slope_kind ($0C) equal to 1, reached from ground_slope_left. Calls $9D3C and, if $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set, goes to ground_slope_commit. Otherwise, unless bit 1 of joy_bits ($08) is set, it sets $0905 and $0B to 5. Either way it ends in land_and_snap.

Ground step to the right while slope_kind ($0C) is non-zero, entered from collide_ground_right. When slope_kind is not 1 it goes to ground_slope_right_two. Otherwise it calls $9D3C and, if $0291 has bit 2 or bit 3 set, goes to ground_slope_commit. If not, it adds 6 to player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE) and, unless bit 1 of joy_bits ($08) is set, sets $0905 and $0B to 5. It ends in land_and_snap.
Commit the step: goes to restore_player_pos ($4246). Used by the ground slope routines when $0291 still has bit 2 or bit 3 set.

Airborne step up and to the right (move_dir $06). Calls $9C1E. When bit 0 is set in $E1, $E2, or $E3 the step is dropped with save_player_x ($4263); otherwise it is committed with restore_player_x ($4249). Both ways it ends in air_up_check.
Airborne step up and to the left (move_dir $0A). Same as air_up_right_x, but the block probe is $9BF6 instead of $9C1E. Both ways it ends in air_up_check.

Vertical check for an airborne player moving up. Calls $9D17 and merges $E1, $E2, and $E3. When bit 0 is set it goes to air_start_fall. Otherwise it commits the Y with restore_player_y ($4256), calls $9E69, and goes on to air_mode1_check. Also entered with move_dir $0E.

Calls $9E69, then tests bit 4 of $08E8 and $08E9; when either is clear it returns. When both are set it adds $E1/$E2 to player_x ($08B7/$08B8), sets $0B, $08FF, and jump_state ($08FA) to 0, player_mode ($09) to 1, move_step ($0A) to 2, $18 and move_dir ($0D) to $0E, and $0905 to 6 (the player enters mode 1). Entered from air_up_check, and from air_vertical.
Start a fall: jump_state ($08FA) becomes 1, jump_counter ($08FB) becomes 0, and it returns.

Carry the player along with the object it stands on; player_move calls it when stand_obj ($1A) is not negative (with X = stand_obj). It acts on ride_dir ($19): $0E goes to ride_up, $0D to ride_down, $0B to ride_left, $07 to ride_right, and any other value returns. ride_up places the player on the object and commits Y; ride_down does the same after a block test (a harmful block goes to ride_hit, a fast object to player_leave_object); ride_left and ride_right move player_prev_x by obj_speed and commit it unless a block is solid. Most paths end in ride_finish.
Case $0E of player_ride_object: calls place_player_on_object, commits the Y with restore_player_y ($4256), and goes to ride_finish.

Case $0D of player_ride_object. When $0295 is 7 or more it goes to player_leave_object. Otherwise it calls place_player_on_object and $9D3C and merges $E1, $E2, and $E3. With bit 1 set it goes to ride_hit; if not, it commits the Y with restore_player_y ($4256) and goes to ride_finish.
The player leaves the object: $0299 becomes 0, jump_state ($08FA) becomes 1, jump_counter ($08FB) becomes 8, and $0905 and $0903 become 3.

Case $0B of player_ride_object. Subtracts obj_speed ($34E1) for the object in X from player_try_x ($08BB/$08BC), calls $9BF6, and merges $E1, $E2, and $E3. With bit 0 set the step is not committed and it goes to ride_finish. Otherwise it commits with restore_player_x ($4249) and, when stand_obj ($1A) is not negative, goes to ride_finish; else it returns.
Case $07 of player_ride_object. Same as ride_left, but it adds obj_speed ($34E1) to player_try_x, and the block probe is $9C1E instead of $9BF6.
End of a ride step: clears bit 7 of obj_flags ($364C) for the object stand_obj ($1A) and calls $AC13. When stand_obj is still not negative it returns; otherwise it goes to player_leave_object.

Harmful block while riding an object (bit 1 set), reached from ride_down ($8D98): sets player_hit ($0292) to 1, jump_state ($08FA) to $FF, and jump_counter ($08FB) to $10. Sound $24 is queued with queue_sound ($0B8C), and when music_mode ($DF) is non-zero a fade-out is started with sid_start_fade_out ($6ED8, A = $25). It falls into hit_save_pos.

Remember where the player was hit: stores player_x ($08B7/$08B8) in player_hit_x ($08E3/$08E4) and player_y ($08B9/$08BA) in player_hit_y ($08E5/$08E6). A word whose high byte is negative is stored as 0. Reached by falling in from ride_hit, by a jump from air_hit_hazard ($8B95), and by jsr from level_timer_tick ($82DF, when time runs out) and the hit code at $A64E; each first queues sound $24 and, with music on, starts the fade-out.

Put the player on the object in X: stores the object's Y position (obj_y_lo $39A6 and obj_y_hi $3A03) minus $031D and then minus $031C in player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE). It loads Y from stand_obj ($1A) but does not use it. ride_up commits the Y with restore_player_y ($4256) straight after; ride_down does so only when the probe that follows finds no harmful block.

Mode 2 movement for one frame, jumped to from player_mode_step for any player_mode ($09) other than 0 and 1. Keeps only bit 6 of fire_flags ($08C6), so bit 7 is clear and the position steps are never skipped, sets player_action ($0905) to 7, runs mode2_move ($8E9B) to pick and apply the direction, and goes to mode2_collide ($8F73) to check the new position.

Address inside the instruction at $8E98 (jmp $8F73 in player_mode2_step): the label sits on an operand byte. Its one reference is jsr $8E9A at $4066 in j_403A, made with $01 = $37, so it runs the cartridge's code at $8E9A (in whichever bank $DE00 last selected), not these RAM bytes. What that cartridge routine does is not read here.

Choose the direction in mode 2 and step player_try_x or player_try_y. Sets move_dir ($0D) to $FF first. While jump_state ($08FA) is non-zero it runs mode2_jump_motion ($8F12) and then steps sideways by the facing flag $18: bit 3 clear steps right ($0D masked with $07, then $42F8), bit 3 set steps left ($0D masked with $0B, then $42E1). When jump_state is zero it follows joy_bits ($08): $07 is right, $0B left, $0E up ($430F), and $0D down ($4326), and the diagonals $06, $05, $09, and $0A do one vertical step and one horizontal step. The joy_bits value is stored in move_dir; any other value leaves $FF.

Vertical motion of the mode 2 jump, the reverse of player_jump_motion, using jump_state ($08FA) and jump_counter ($08FB) on player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE). A jump_state of 0 does nothing.
