A negative one clears bit 1 of move_dir ($0D), adds $02CE[x] to player_try_y, where x is jump_counter limited to 16, and subtracts the same amount from jump_counter; when jump_counter would reach zero or below, jump_state becomes 1 and jump_counter 0. A positive one clears bit 0 of move_dir, subtracts $02DF[x] with x as jump_counter, and then adds one to jump_counter, or sets jump_state to 0 when x is 8 or more. Entering mode 2 from the air ($8B37) sets $FF and $30, so the player first moves down the screen and then back up; the stage-start entry at $500A sets neither.

Second half of mode 2 movement (from player_mode2_step). While jump_state ($08FA) is non-zero it commits player_try_y with $4256 unchecked, then probes the sideways step ($9BF6 when bit 3 of move_dir ($0D) is set, otherwise $9C1E). When bit 0 is clear in $E1, $E2, and $E3 it commits X with $4249; otherwise it flips bits 2 and 3 of move_dir and stores the result in move_dir and $18, turning the player round. On the ground it returns while move_dir is negative; otherwise bit 2 clear probes left ($9BF6), else bit 3 clear probes right ($9C1E), and it commits X with $4249 or cancels it with save_player_x ($4263), cancelling without a probe when both bits are set. Then it handles up ($0D bit 0 clear, probe $9D17) and down (bit 1 clear, probe $9D3C). A block with bit 0 set stops the step; otherwise it commits Y with $4256. Going up with bit 6 clear in the probe results also sets player_mode ($09) to 0, jump_state to $FF, jump_counter ($08FB) to $08FC plus $10, and player_action ($0905) to 3.

Mode 1 movement for one frame, jumped to from player_mode_step when player_mode ($09) is 1. When $08FF is non-zero it goes straight to mode1_collide ($919E). Otherwise it rewrites fire_flags ($08C6), first setting $0903 to $FF when bits 7 and 6 are both set, then keeping bit 6 and setting bit 7 when bit 6 is clear. Then it runs mode1_move_vertical ($9055) when $0B is zero or mode1_move_horizontal ($917A) otherwise, and goes to mode1_collide.

Mode 1 movement when $0B is zero. Returns at once while bit 7 of fire_flags ($08C6) is set. Sets player_action ($0905) to 6, and sets jump_state ($08FA) to $FF when bits 2 and 3 of joy_bits ($08) are both set (neither left nor right). While jump_state is not negative only the vertical bits count: bit 1 clear steps down ($0D, $4326), else bit 0 clear steps up ($0E, $430F), and with neither move_dir ($0D) becomes $FF. With jump_state negative, exactly $0E and $0D step up and down, and otherwise left or right (diagonals included) sets move_dir to $0B or $07, moves player_try_x by 4 that way, and probes with $9BF6 or $9C1E. When bit 0 is clear in $E1, $E2, and $E3 it sets player_mode ($09) to 0, player_third_on ($0913) to 1, and queues sound 0 with queue_sound ($0B8C); otherwise mode1_step_blocked tries down, then up.

Tail of mode1_step_left, fallen into after its probe at $90B9 and the first two ORs: ORs in $E3, and if bit 0 of $E1/$E2/$E3 is set the step is blocked and it branches to mode1_step_blocked. Otherwise it clears $09, sets player_third_on to 1 and queues sound 0 through queue_sound. The label is here because stage_start ($0B25) reads $90C0,x with $01 = $37 and cartridge bank 13 selected, copying 256 bytes of the cartridge from $90C0 to $FD00; that read never touches this RAM.

The step was blocked. Reads the direction bits in joy_bits ($08, 0 = pressed): if bit 1 is clear (down) it goes to mode1_down_set, else if bit 0 is clear (up) it goes to mode1_up_set (try moving vertically instead). With neither, it stores $FF in move_dir ($0D, no move) and returns. Reached from mode1_step_left ($90C4) and mode1_step_right ($9104).

Walks the player right by 4 pixels in the 16-bit try X position (player_try_x, player_try_x_hi), after setting move_dir ($0D) to 7, the right direction code. Then probe_player_tiles checks the tiles there. If blocked it goes to mode1_step_blocked, else it clears $09, sets player_third_on to 1 and queues sound 0. Reached from mode1_move_vertical ($9085) when right is pressed.
Return in A the smallest of the eight bytes of spr_free_line ($07CF-$07D6), one per hardware sprite slot. Called from $8147. Each slot is compared with the running minimum, starting from slot 0.

Start an object on a path from the record at ($E3),Y. X is the object. The byte at Y is skipped; the bytes at Y+1 and Y+2 go to obj_arc_state ($3F19,X) and obj_arc_counter ($3F76,X, the slot in the path tables). The byte at Y+3 is kept in $ED and the one at Y+4 is stored in path_end ($5C), $ED in path_axes ($60), and 0 in path_pos ($64), all at that slot. Y is left at Y+4 (from $EB) and the routine returns with carry set. It is the handler for script command $15 (entry 21 of the tables at $B33C/$B35F), reached from the dispatch at $B217-$B224.

Mode 1 movement when $0B is non-zero. Sets player_action ($0905) to 5. Right in joy_bits ($08, bit 3 clear) sets move_dir ($0D) to $07 and steps right with $42F8; otherwise left (bit 2 clear) sets $0B and steps left with $42E1; otherwise move_dir becomes $FF.

Second half of mode 1 movement, reached from player_mode1_step. When $08FF is negative it is set to 0, and when it is positive nothing more happens. When $08FF is zero and $0B is non-zero, move_dir ($0D) of $07 goes to $9276 and $0B to $92AD. When $0B is zero, $0E goes to mode1_up_end ($91CF), $0D to $91EB, and left (bit 2 clear) or right (bit 3 clear) to $9207 or $921C, which move player_x by 8 and start a jump back in mode 0. mode1_up_end probes with $9D17; when $0291 is non-zero it commits Y with $4256, otherwise it sets player_third_on ($0913) to 0, $0903 to 1, and $08FF to 2.

Vertical half of mode 1 movement, entered when $0B is zero. Reads move_dir ($0D): $0E goes to mode1_up_end, $0D to mode1_down_end. Otherwise bit 2 clear (the left code $0B) goes to mode1_step_left_8, and bit 3 clear (the right code $07) to mode1_step_right_8; any other value returns.

Address inside the instruction at $91BE (beq $91CF in mode1_vertical_collide): the label sits on an operand byte. Its references are lda $91BF,x at $50C8 and $50E9 in copy_sprite_shapes, made with $01 = $37 and cartridge bank 13 selected: they read the low bytes of the shape addresses for player_shape_1 and player_shape_2 from the cartridge (high bytes at $9202), not these RAM bytes.

Continuation of mode1_vertical_collide (the run starts in the operand of the beq at $91BE): compares move_dir ($0D) with $0D and branches to mode1_down_end ($91EB) if equal. Otherwise bit 2 clear (the left code) goes to mode1_step_left_8; failing that, bit 3 clear (the right code) goes to mode1_step_right_8, and any other value returns.

Entry for move_dir $0E. Calls $9D17, then if $0291 is non-zero jumps to $91F5, which commits the Y position with restore_player_y. Otherwise clears player_third_on ($0913), sets $0903 to 1 and $08FF to 2, and returns.

Entry for move_dir $0D (the code the object path script uses for down; inferred to be down here too). Calls player_probe_tiles_and_platforms. If bit 4 of $0291 is set it jumps to $91F5 and commits the Y position with restore_player_y. Otherwise it falls into mode1_down_check.

Calls $9BF6, then ORs the tile attribute bytes $E1, $E2 and $E3 and tests bit 0. When it is set, control goes to mode1_set_dir_07; when clear, to mode1_set_dir_0B. The meaning of the bit is not established here.

Address inside the instruction at $9201 (and #$01 in mode1_down_check): the label sits on an operand byte. Its references are lda $9202,x at $50CD and $50EE in copy_sprite_shapes, made with $01 = $37 and cartridge bank 13 selected: they read the high bytes of the shape addresses for player_shape_1 and player_shape_2 from the cartridge (low bytes at $91BF), not these RAM bytes.
Moves player_x ($08B7/$08B8) left by 8 pixels, loads $0B (the left direction code) and joins mode1_start_jump. Reached from mode1_vertical_collide when move_dir has bit 2 clear.
Moves player_x ($08B7/$08B8) right by 8 pixels, loads $07 (the right direction code) and falls into mode1_start_jump. Reached from mode1_vertical_collide when move_dir has bit 3 clear.

Shared tail. Stores the direction code in $18, sets jump_state ($08FA) to $FF, clears $09 and $0C, sets move_step ($0A) to 2 and jump_counter ($08FB) to $10, sets player_action ($0905) to 3, and queues sound 0 through queue_sound. Mode 1 hands back to mode 0 here, as a jump (inferred from the jump_state and jump_counter names).

End of mode1_start_jump's shared tail ($922F): sets player_action ($0905) to 3 and queues sound 0 through queue_sound, which returns to the caller. The run listed at $9245 starts inside the operand of the lda at $9244.

Address inside the instruction at $9244 (lda #$03 in mode1_start_jump): the label sits on an operand byte. Its reference is lda $9245,x at $50A7 in copy_sprite_shapes, made with $01 = $37 and cartridge bank 13 selected: it reads the low bytes of the shape addresses for player_shape_3 from the cartridge (high bytes at $9263), not these RAM bytes.
Loads direction code $0B (left) and goes to mode1_set_dir_tail.
Loads direction code $07 (right) and falls into mode1_set_dir_tail.

Shared tail. Stores the direction code in $18, clears $09 and $0C, sets jump_state ($08FA) to 1, move_step ($0A) to 2, jump_counter ($08FB) to 1 and player_action ($0905) to 3, then queues sound 0 through queue_sound. Like mode1_start_jump but with jump_state and jump_counter set to 1, which looks like the start of a fall rather than a rise (inferred).

Last part of mode1_set_dir_tail: sets jump_counter ($08FB) to 1 and player_action ($0905) to 3, then queues sound 0 through queue_sound, which returns to the caller. The tail's first part ($9254) set the direction, jump_state and move_step.

Resolve a mode 1 sideways step to the right: reached only from mode1_horizontal_collide ($91E8) when move_dir is $07 ($92AD is the left-hand sibling, for $0B). Probes the tiles around the player (probe_player_tiles); if any of $E1-$E3 has bit 0 set the move is blocked and the routine ends at $92AC without committing. Otherwise it continues at $9283, which commits the new X with restore_player_x and probes again.

Address inside the instruction at $9281 (bne $92AC in player_step_check_first_dir): the label sits on an operand byte. Its reference is lda $9282,x at $5227 in game_init, made with $01 = $37 and cartridge bank 13 selected: it copies 64 bytes of the cartridge ($9282-$92C1) to the RAM under I/O at $D040, and never touches these RAM bytes.

Second half of player_step_check_first_dir, reached when none of $E1-$E3 has bit 0 set. Calls restore_player_x ($4249), which commits the new X (player_try_x to player_x), probes again with player_probe_tiles_and_platforms, and returns if bit 0 of $E1 is clear. Otherwise it picks a direction code from bit 1 of joy_bits ($08, 0 = pressed): set (down not pressed) gives $07 (jumps to $92CE), clear (down) gives $05, which is stored in $18 and move_dir ($0D) here; $09, jump_state ($08FA) and $0C are cleared and stance ($0299) set to 1. The run before this address ends in the operand of the bne at $9281, so the first real instruction is at $9283.

Second variant of the move-step check: probes with $9BF6 and returns if bit 0 of $E1, $E2 or $E3 is set; otherwise restores x (restore_player_x) and re-probes. If bit 0 of $E3 is then set: with joy_bits bit 1 set, $18 becomes $0B and player_action 1 (via $92CE); with it clear, $18 and move_dir become 9 and $0299 becomes 1 (via $9272). Both clear player_mode, jump_state and slope_kind. Direction meaning inferred.

Last step of update_player. First it updates the energy bar: when $08CB is non-zero it takes the low 5 bits of the health of object $08CC into $08A1 and draws the bar with $831B; when $08CB is zero and player_hit ($0292) is zero it calls update_view_scroll ($470C). Then, while the player is not hit, it takes a probe point (player_x plus $18, and player_y plus $031C, with their high bytes $08B8 and $08BA) and finds the stage section that holds it. The current section record is the one at ($26) and the section number is section_index ($0298); $93CD tests the point against the bounds in the record (offsets $0E to $15: x low and high, then y low and high, each as two bytes). When the point is outside, it tries the next section (up to the limit $0C06) and then the previous one, using the record addresses at $0D22, and on a match stores the new index and pointer and falls into $936E.

Copy the settings of the section record at ($26) into working variables: bytes 0 to 5 to zone_left ($0908/$0909), zone_right ($0906/$0907), zone_top ($090A) and zone_bottom ($090B), the edges of the zone in which the view does not follow the player; byte $16 to section_scroll_flags ($08FD); and bytes $17 and $18 to obj_first and obj_end. view_pinned_edges ($08FE) is cleared, and bit 2 of $08FD is cleared unless it is set and the low two bits of $08FD differ from stream_current ($08A7), in which case those bits are stored in $08A7 and bits 2 and 3 of $08FD are set (start a new background stream). Called when the player enters a new section (falling in from track_stage_section), and from $5048 (finish_round_setup) during stage setup.

Test whether the point at $E1/$E2 (x) and $E3/$E4 (y) lies inside the section record at ($E5): it compares each coordinate with the 16-bit minimum and maximum at offsets $0E to $15. Returns with the carry set when the point is inside and clear when it is outside.

Look up the block property at a position. The inputs are A (added to the x position $E7/$E8), Y (added to the y position $E9/$EA), and the 16-bit position itself. Both sums are divided by 16 to give a block column ($EB) and row ($EC); the row picks a row pointer from the tables at ($2A) and ($2C), the column picks a block number from that row, and the block number picks the property byte in the table at ($30), which comes back in A. A row above the top of the map (the high byte of Y plus $E9/$EA negative) returns 0. Used by the object code at $84B5 and $AA3C; the same lookup idea gives the tile bits that the player code tests (for example bit 0 solid and bit 1 harmful).

Redraws the whole playfield from the level map. Each map byte (found through row pointers $2A/$2C, starting at scroll_x/2 and scroll_y/2) selects a 2x2-character tile in the table at ($2E); its four characters are written to screen RAM (buffer pointed to by $08BF) and the matching colours from char_colour_table ($0C22) to colour RAM at $D800, 20 tiles per row pair. Finishes by tail-jumping to recolour_screen.

Copy the logical sprite list into the hardware sprite tables ($07B4-$07E6) in top-to-bottom order. It starts at slot 0, or slot 1 when place_third_sprite already used slot 0 (spr_enable $07B2 non-zero). It walks sprite_y_buckets ($7CBD) from the top: positions with bit 7 set are skipped, $7F ends the list, any other value is a logical sprite number, and each position it consumes (the $7F included) is reset to $FF. For each sprite it copies the pointer ($0838) to spr_pointer ($07C7), the colour ($0808) to spr_colour ($07B4), and the X low ($0850) and Y ($0880) to the X and Y pair at $07D7/$07D8 (two bytes per slot); it sets the slot's bit in spr_x_msb ($07B1) when the X high byte ($0868) is non-zero; and it sets spr_free_line ($07CF) to Y + $16, or Y + $2B when the colour's bit 7 is set, in which case the slot's bit is also set in spr_expand ($07B3). It stops after eight slots, leaving in sprite_more ($6B) the list position of the last sprite copied, or at the end of the list, leaving 0 there. Then it sets spr_enable from the table at $02A6 (one bit for each slot used). wait_nmi uses $6B to choose the raster interrupt at $95A4 when it is non-zero.

Raster interrupt that reuses the eight hardware sprites for the logical sprites left over after copy_sprites_to_tables ($951A) filled them. wait_nmi ($8134) puts this address in raster_vector ($07AB) for nmi_frame to install when $6B (sprite_more) is non-zero. It saves A, X, and Y in $68-$6A, acknowledges the raster flag ($D019), and takes Y from $0807 (the position of the last entry placed, $FF at the start of a frame). Each pass of the loop at $95B0 advances Y and loads X from the list at $007E,Y: a logical sprite number, or a negative value that ends the list. The entries are then dealt to hardware sprites 0 to 7 in turn: each takes the next sprite in that order whose free line in $6C-$73 has passed, and the walk wraps back to sprite 0 only after sprite 7. $0200-$0278 hold the logical sprite's colour with bit 7 for double size ($0200), height ($0218), pointer ($0230), X low ($0248), X high ($0260), and Y ($0278).

Take the next entry of the leftover list: Y is advanced and X loaded from $007E,Y. A negative entry ends the list and jumps to reuse_end_of_list ($98AA). Reached from the start of sprite_reuse_irq, from the last hardware sprite block, and when reuse_wait_free_sprite finds a free line already passed.

Try to use hardware sprite 0 for the logical sprite in X. The sprite is free when its free line $6C (minus one) is below the raster line in $D012; if it is not, the code goes on to reuse_hw_sprite_1 ($9615) with carry set. When free it copies Y ($0278,X) to $D001, X low ($0248,X) to $D000, and X high ($0260,X, non-zero sets the bit) into bit 0 of $D010; the colour ($0200,X) to $D027, with bit 7 setting bit 0 of both the double-width ($D01D) and double-height ($D017) registers; and the pointer ($0230,X) to $CBF8 and $CFF8 on both screens. It then stores Y plus the height ($0218,X) in $6C as the line where the sprite frees up; steps to the next entry and goes to the next hardware sprite, or to reuse_end_of_list when the list has ended.

Try to use hardware sprite 1 for the logical sprite in X. The sprite is free when its free line $6D (minus one) is below the raster line in $D012; if it is not, the code goes on to reuse_hw_sprite_2 ($9672) with carry set. When free it copies Y ($0278,X) to $D003, X low ($0248,X) to $D002, and X high ($0260,X, non-zero sets the bit) into bit 1 of $D010; the colour ($0200,X) to $D028, with bit 7 setting bit 1 of both the double-width ($D01D) and double-height ($D017) registers; and the pointer ($0230,X) to $CBF9 and $CFF9 on both screens. It then stores Y plus the height ($0218,X) in $6D as the line where the sprite frees up; steps to the next entry and goes to the next hardware sprite, or to reuse_end_of_list when the list has ended.

Try to use hardware sprite 2 for the logical sprite in X. The sprite is free when its free line $6E (minus one) is below the raster line in $D012; if it is not, the code goes on to reuse_hw_sprite_3 ($96CF) with carry set. When free it copies Y ($0278,X) to $D005, X low ($0248,X) to $D004, and X high ($0260,X, non-zero sets the bit) into bit 2 of $D010; the colour ($0200,X) to $D029, with bit 7 setting bit 2 of both the double-width ($D01D) and double-height ($D017) registers; and the pointer ($0230,X) to $CBFA and $CFFA on both screens. It then stores Y plus the height ($0218,X) in $6E as the line where the sprite frees up; steps to the next entry and goes to the next hardware sprite, or to reuse_end_of_list when the list has ended.

Try to use hardware sprite 3 for the logical sprite in X. The sprite is free when its free line $6F (minus one) is below the raster line in $D012; if it is not, the code goes on to reuse_hw_sprite_4 ($972C) with carry set. When free it copies Y ($0278,X) to $D007, X low ($0248,X) to $D006, and X high ($0260,X, non-zero sets the bit) into bit 3 of $D010; the colour ($0200,X) to $D02A, with bit 7 setting bit 3 of both the double-width ($D01D) and double-height ($D017) registers; and the pointer ($0230,X) to $CBFB and $CFFB on both screens. It then stores Y plus the height ($0218,X) in $6F as the line where the sprite frees up; steps to the next entry and goes to the next hardware sprite, or to reuse_end_of_list when the list has ended.

Try to use hardware sprite 4 for the logical sprite in X. The sprite is free when its free line $70 (minus one) is below the raster line in $D012; if it is not, the code goes on to reuse_hw_sprite_5 ($9789) with carry set. When free it copies Y ($0278,X) to $D009, X low ($0248,X) to $D008, and X high ($0260,X, non-zero sets the bit) into bit 4 of $D010; the colour ($0200,X) to $D02B, with bit 7 setting bit 4 of both the double-width ($D01D) and double-height ($D017) registers; and the pointer ($0230,X) to $CBFC and $CFFC on both screens. It then stores Y plus the height ($0218,X) in $70 as the line where the sprite frees up; steps to the next entry and goes to the next hardware sprite, or to reuse_end_of_list when the list has ended.

Try to use hardware sprite 5 for the logical sprite in X. The sprite is free when its free line $71 (minus one) is below the raster line in $D012; if it is not, the code goes on to reuse_hw_sprite_6 ($97E6) with carry set. When free it copies Y ($0278,X) to $D00B, X low ($0248,X) to $D00A, and X high ($0260,X, non-zero sets the bit) into bit 5 of $D010; the colour ($0200,X) to $D02C, with bit 7 setting bit 5 of both the double-width ($D01D) and double-height ($D017) registers; and the pointer ($0230,X) to $CBFD and $CFFD on both screens. It then stores Y plus the height ($0218,X) in $71 as the line where the sprite frees up; steps to the next entry and goes to the next hardware sprite, or to reuse_end_of_list when the list has ended.

Try to use hardware sprite 6 for the logical sprite in X. The sprite is free when its free line $72 (minus one) is below the raster line in $D012; if it is not, the code goes on to reuse_hw_sprite_7 ($9843) with carry set. When free it copies Y ($0278,X) to $D00D, X low ($0248,X) to $D00C, and X high ($0260,X, non-zero sets the bit) into bit 6 of $D010; the colour ($0200,X) to $D02D, with bit 7 setting bit 6 of both the double-width ($D01D) and double-height ($D017) registers; and the pointer ($0230,X) to $CBFE and $CFFE on both screens. It then stores Y plus the height ($0218,X) in $72 as the line where the sprite frees up; steps to the next entry and goes to the next hardware sprite, or to reuse_end_of_list when the list has ended.

Try to use hardware sprite 7 for the logical sprite in X. The sprite is free when its free line $73 (minus one) is below the raster line in $D012; if it is not, the code goes on to reuse_wait_free_sprite ($989B): the walk for this entry has reached the last sprite. When free it copies Y ($0278,X) to $D00F, X low ($0248,X) to $D00E, and X high ($0260,X, non-zero sets the bit) into bit 7 of $D010; the colour ($0200,X) to $D02E, with bit 7 setting bit 7 of both the double-width ($D01D) and double-height ($D017) registers; and the pointer ($0230,X) to $CBFF and $CFFF on both screens. It then stores Y plus the height ($0218,X) in $73 as the line where the sprite frees up and goes back to reuse_next_entry ($95B0), which starts again at sprite 0.

Reached when hardware sprite 7 is busy at the end of the walk for an entry (the sprites before the walk's starting point were not retested). Y is stepped back so the same entry is tried again, and lowest_free_line ($98C5) returns the earliest free line of all eight in A. When that line minus two is still ahead of the raster line, it jumps to reuse_set_next_irq ($98B8) to schedule the interrupt at that line; otherwise the line is about to pass and it retries at reuse_next_entry ($95B0), from sprite 0.

The leftover list is finished. It points the interrupt vector ($FFFE/$FFFF) back to irq_panel ($837E), sets X = $D5 for the next raster line and Y = $FF for $0807 (so the next frame starts at the first entry), and falls into reuse_set_next_irq.
Leave the interrupt: write X to the raster line register $D012 and Y to $0807, restore A, X, and Y from $68-$6A, and return with RTI. Entered with the next line in X and the list position in Y.
Return in A the smallest of the eight hardware-sprite free lines $6C-$73 (the first sprite to become free), with carry clear. Called once, by reuse_wait_free_sprite.

Choose the player's two body shapes and offsets each frame from the action number $0905 and the facing flag $18 (bit 3 set for left; $07 right, $0B left, and $05, $06, $09, $0A or $0E in some states). While player_hit ($0292) is non-zero it switches the third sprite off, clears $0900 and sets player_shape_1 and player_shape_2 to $28 and $34, or $29 and $35, by bit 2 of $18. Otherwise actions 0-2 use the table at $0458 or $046C by facing, 3 uses $04C0 or $04CA, 4 uses $04AC or $04B6; 5 and 6 go to $9A2A ($0480, $0490, $04A0) and 7 to $9BAB ($0438, $0448). Each table starts with its length; the frame index $0902 steps by 2 and wraps at it, the shape pair is read at offset 8 plus the index, and bytes 1 to 7 give $0322, $0323, $0900 and $031A-$031D. A step comes after a hold count in $0901, at once when $0903 is set or when the state-and-facing key in $0296 changes ($0902 is kept). While $08FF is non-zero ($9A2A) it plays a transition from $04E8 and $04EC and moves player_y.

Player terrain probe, one-column variant (sibling of probe_player_tiles at $9C1E, which also adds the second X offset $031B). If $029C is clear and player_screen_x is below $0C (player at the left screen edge), sets the probe results $E2, $E3 and $E4 to 3 and returns without reading the map; 3 is probably a solid attribute, inferred, so the edge acts as a wall. Otherwise falls to $9C0B.
Computes the probe X position: player_try_x ($08BB/$08BC) plus offset $031A, stored in $E5/$E6, then jumps to $9C50, the Y computation shared with probe_player_tiles.

Player terrain probe for the box's right-hand edge: looks up the map tile attribute values in the column at player_try_x ($08BB/$08BC) plus offsets $031A and $031B, and stores them in $E1 (top cell of that column), $E2 (the next cell below when the height $031D allows, otherwise the same as $E1) and $E3 (the cell at the lower edge). The top is player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE) plus $031C plus 2 (clamped to 0 if negative); positions are divided by 16 into tile columns and rows; it indexes the row pointer tables at ($2A)/($2C) with the row, then the block map row with the column ($E9), then the tile attribute table at ($30). If the player is on the right side of the screen ($029C set and player_screen_x $029B >= $25) it just sets $E2-$E4 = 3 and returns. probe_player_tiles_one_column ($9BF6) is the left-edge sibling.

Player terrain probe, one-row variant (sibling of player_probe_tiles_and_platforms at $9D3C, which also adds the second Y offset $031D). Sets $F0 to $FF, computes Y = player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE) plus offset $031C into $EA/$EB, and if the result is negative (above the top of the map) goes to $9D30. Otherwise jumps to probe_columns_from_y ($9D61) to work out the X columns.
Probe result for a position outside the map: clears the tile attribute results $E1, $E2 and $E3 and $0291 to zero and returns.

Probes the tile attribute bytes around the player's previous position (player_try_x $08BB/$08BC, player_try_y $08BD/$08BE plus offsets $031A-$031D) and then checks the object list. Y sum goes to $EA/$EB and $EE/$EF, X to $E5/$E6; a negative high byte jumps to $9D30 (outside this stretch, which zeroes $E1-$E3 and $0291). Tile row pointers come from ($2A) and ($2C) indexed by row, tile ids from the row, attribute bytes from table ($30): left column to $E1, second column to $E2 (only when $031B is above $10), column at prev_x+$1F to $0291, right edge column to $E3. Sets $F0 to 0 here; the sibling entry at $9D17 sets it to $FF and joins at $9D61. Callers are not shown.
Entry for the sibling code at $9D17 (jmp from $9D2D) and fall-in point of $9D3C: starts the x tile computation from player_try_x with offset $031A.

Runs on every pass of the probe: branched to when $031B is $10 or less (second column not read), and fallen into after the second column. Takes the tile at try X ($08BB/$08BC) plus $1F in the same row and stores its attribute in far_column_prop ($0291), then computes the right edge column (the left X in $E5/$E6 plus $031B, also kept in $EC/$ED) and stores its attribute in $E3.
If $F0 bit 7 is set (the $9D17 entry), returns at once. If $19 equals $0D, goes to $9E5E. If any of $E3, $E1, or $E2 is nonzero, goes to $9E59 (no platform).

Loops over the $0910 entries of the list at $74 (X counts down; negative ends the scan). For each object Y = list entry: needs $EE/$EF minus obj_hit_top $3D48/$3DA5 to be between 0 and 7, then horizontal overlap (obj_hit_right $3C8E/$3CEB at or past $E5/$E6, and $EC/$ED at or past obj_hit_left $3BD4/$3C31). On a match sets bit 7 of obj_flags $364C,y, stores Y in $1A, and returns.
Return.
Sets $1A to $FF (no object found) and returns.
Used when $19 is $0D: sets bit 7 of obj_flags $364C for the object already in $1A, then returns without scanning.

Looks up the two map tiles under the player's previous position and stores their property bytes. Takes the previous position ($08BB/$08BD plus offsets $22 across and $04 down for the head probe, $25 further down for the feet probe), turns them into tile column and row (divide by 16), reads the tile numbers from the level map through the row pointer tables at $2A/$2C, then looks each tile up in the property table at ($30) and puts the results in $08E8 (head) and $08E9 (feet). If the feet probe is above the top of the map it clears both and returns. Also leaves 8 minus the pixel offset within the tile in $E1/$E2. Used as the player's terrain check; the exact meaning of the property bits is inferred, not shown here.

Set aim_dir ($0297) when the player is not shooting; update_player skips it while bit 7 of fire_flags ($08C6) is set. In mode 1 with $0B equal to 0 it folds the direction to 0 (up, facing right) when it is below 5 and to 9 (up, facing left) otherwise. In mode 2 it always uses the facing: 7 when bit 3 of $18 is set (left), otherwise 2 (right). In mode 0, and in mode 1 with $0B non-zero, it uses slope_aim_dir ($AB74) when slope_kind ($0C) and stance ($0299) are both non-zero, which picks 3 or 8 for slope kind 2 and 1 or 6 for any other by the facing flag $18; otherwise the same 7 or 2 by facing. The result is the direction that player_fire ($AF34) uses for the next shot.

Put the player's first two sprites into the logical sprite list. player_sprite_coords ($9FC0) first turns the player's world position into screen coordinates. Then, if the shape number player_shape_1 ($08EA) is non-zero and its Y ($08ED) is between $1A and $D3, it fills entry 0 of the tables at $0808-$0880 (colour from $0914, X from $08F0/$08F3, Y from $08ED, height $15, pointer $FC, which is the shape block at $FF00) and files the entry in sprite_y_buckets ($7CBD) at Y / 2. The same is done for player_shape_2 ($08EB) with pointer $FD (the block at $FF40), colour $0915, and X and Y from $08F1/$08F4 and $08EE. If the bucket at Y / 2 is already taken by the first sprite, the second entry goes in the next bucket. It leaves the number of entries in sprite_count ($12) and the bucket position in sprite_bucket_max ($13), where object_sprites_and_hits carries on.

Turn the player's world position into sprite coordinates. X of the first sprite ($08F0 low, $08F3 high) is player_x minus view_left ($40/$41) plus $20 plus $0322; Y ($08ED) is player_y minus view_top ($42/$43) plus $37 plus $0323, checked by clamp_sprite_y. The third sprite's X ($08F2/$08F5) and Y ($08EF) are worked out the same way from $08B3 and $08B5, but without $0322 and $0323. The second sprite ($08F1/$08F4, $08EE) goes $18 pixels to the right of the first when $0900 is non-zero, otherwise $15 lines below it. It also leaves X before $0322 in $029B/$029C and a Y in $029D.

Check a screen Y value passed in A (high byte) and X (low byte): a negative value becomes 0 in both X and Y, a value of $D4 or more becomes $DE in both, and anything else is left as it is (Y unchanged). The callers treat Y values below $1A or from $D4 up as off-screen and do not draw the sprite.

Put the player's third sprite straight into slot 0 of the hardware sprite tables ($07B4-$07E6). It first clears spr_x_msb ($07B1) and spr_expand ($07B3). If player_third_on ($0913) is non-zero and the Y of the sprite ($08EF) is between $1A and $D3, it writes colour $0916, pointer $FE (the shape block at $FF80, whose shape number is $08EC), free-line Y + $15, X from $08F2, Y from $08EF, the X high bit from $08F5, and sets spr_enable ($07B2) to 1; otherwise spr_enable is 0. copy_sprites_to_tables then starts after slot 0 when spr_enable is 1.

Blink timer for the goal object whose number is in $08CC, called by wait_frame ($826C) only while the low six bits of $08CB are non-zero. $0290 is a two-phase countdown: while positive it counts down and sets bit 6 ($40, not drawn and not hit) of the object's obj_kind byte ($35EF); when it would go below 0 it becomes $81, and while bit 7 is set it counts down with that bit cleared, until $80 gives 0 again with the bit set. From 0 it cycles 0, $81, $80, so the object shows on two calls in three. Each pass through the clear phase also decrements the low six bits of $08CB (keeping its top two bits), setting it to $80 when it would underflow; $08CB is the time the gauge shows the object's health (track_stage_section), so the object blinks while the gauge is up.

Once a frame, update the stage's objects (enemies and the like) from obj_first ($14) up to obj_end ($15). First it sets move_mask ($029A) to $FF when bit 7 of $94 is set, otherwise to one bit chosen by the low three bits of frame_count from $029E, clears the count at $0910 (it counts the objects with bits 3 and 4 of obj_state set, whose numbers are listed from $74), and moves obj_first up by one when the first object is retired (bit 5, $20, of obj_state). Then for each object that is not retired: a follower (bit 6, $40, of obj_flags $364C) takes its position from the last object before it with bit 7 set plus its own offsets ($36F4 for X, $3748 for Y), any other object keeps the position in obj_x_lo/obj_x_hi/obj_y_lo/obj_y_hi ($38EC, $3949, $39A6, $3A03). An object whose bit mask in $3484 shares a bit with move_mask is moved this frame (bit 6 of obj_state cleared first): it is skipped if it lies far outside the view, otherwise given jumps and falls by object_arc_step ($88CE) and moved and animated through $B207, $B1F7, and $B57A according to its flags and its motion byte ($32CE); when those set bit 1 or bit 5 of obj_state, the object is marked not drawn and skipped. The new position is stored back. An object that does not move this frame and has bit 1 of obj_state set is skipped. The others are compared with the view window ($40-$47): outside it, bit 7 ($80) of obj_state is set (not drawn; with bit 6 as well when it is above or below the view) and, when bit 4 ($10) of obj_flags is set, bits 7 and 5 ($A0, retired for good); inside it, bit 6 ($40) is set and bit 7 cleared. An object that moved this frame, is inside the view horizontally, and has bit 4 ($10) of obj_state set gets its hit box from set_object_hitbox ($ABC7); one with bit 3 set calls $A990. The frame data it reads is reached through the stage-block pointers $3A and $3C, indexed by obj_anim_num ($33CA).

Per frame: draw the objects and test them against the player. Box 1 ($4C-$53: left, right, top, bottom): player_x + $031A, that + $031B, player_y + $031C, that + $031D. Box 2 ($54-$5B): player_third_x + $031E and + $031F, player_third_y + $0320 and + $0321. For obj_first to obj_end, then temp_first to temp_end ($F0 = $FF): unless obj_state bit 7 or obj_kind bit 6 is set, each on-screen part of the current frame ($3B1A/$3B77, count in byte 4) adds a sprite entry at $0808-$0880 (at most $16 in all), filed in sprite_y_buckets at Y/2 or the next free place; $7F goes after the highest. If $A54A's check passes, player_hit is 0 and obj_phase is not negative, phase 0-1 objects meet box 2 first (a miss tries box 1 unless the object is wholly above box 2), others box 1; contact goes by phase and group to $A7A1, $A5B2, $A616, $A741 or $A74E. Objects with obj_state bit 7 clear and obj_kind bit 5 set then meet the six shots: a hit clears the shot and kills a pool object or takes hit points ($A6F0).

Low bytes of nine handler addresses, indexed by the low four bits of obj_flags ($364C) at $A7A1: 0 $A7B9 collect item (sound $0C, counts up $089F), 1 $A83C pick up a weapon, 2 $0BBE, 3 $A85A, 4 to 6 none ($0000), 7 $A7F3 open the gate (see script_word_a), 8 $A82A. $A7A1 first stores $A0 in obj_state and jumps through the pair (high bytes in obj_flags_handler_hi).
High bytes of the nine handler addresses of obj_flags_handler_lo ($A7, $A8, $0B, $A8, then three zeros, $A7 and $A8).

Low bytes of the ten handlers that object_run_type_handler ($A88E) jumps to, indexed by the low four bits of obj_kind. With obj_kind_reaction_hi the addresses are: 0 $A8FA, 1 $A8D8, 2 $A8E0, 3 $A93D (nothing), 4 $A0E1 (in the resident code copied from bank 4), 5 $A93E, 6 $A8A6 (object_type_reset_group), 7 $A96D, 8 $A981, 9 $A902.
High bytes of the ten handler addresses of obj_kind_reaction_lo ($A884-$A88D).

Queue sound $14, then jump through a table indexed by the low four bits of obj_kind ($35EF,x): low bytes at $A87A, high bytes at $A884, ten entries. Called from $A61A (contact: after the jump-on health test at $A600, or from $A5AA when player_effect bit 7 is set), from $A72B (a shot takes the last hit point) and from $BD56 (script command 34, $BD54). By type, the handlers are $A8FA (0, launch up in an arc), $A8D8 (1), $A8E0 (2), $A93D (3, does nothing), $A0E1 (4, resident code from bank 4), $A93E (5), $A8A6 (6), $A96D (7), $A981 (8), and $A902 (9).

Handler for object type 6, run through object_run_type_handler ($A88E). Starting with object X, it handles each following object whose obj_flags ($364C) bit 6 is set (a follower) as well. For each object that has neither bit 4 of obj_flags nor bit 5 of obj_state ($3592) set, it calls $A8D8 and then sets bit 4 of obj_flags. X is left at the last object handled.

Handler for object type 1; also called from object_type_reset_group ($A8B4) and reached by a jump from $A96A. Replace obj_anim_num ($33CA) with the byte at the pointer ($3E) indexed by the old number, then carry on into object_reset_motion ($A8E0).

Handler for object type 2, and also reached by a jump from $A98D. Clear obj_arc_state ($3F19), copy the byte at $3376 to the motion byte at $32CE, clear bit 5 of obj_flags (the bit that makes $A2D9 call the table handlers of $B1F7), and set the animation countdown at $3A60 to $FF. Then continue at $A91D with A = $FF.

Handler for object type 0, and also reached by a jump from $B432. Replace obj_anim_num ($33CA) with the byte at the pointer ($3E) indexed by the old number, then carry on into object_start_rise_arc ($A902).

Handler for object type 9, and the second half of type 0. Set the motion byte ($32CE) to $FE, obj_arc_state ($3F19) to $80, and obj_arc_counter ($3F76) to $10, so that object_arc_step ($88CE) makes the object rise. Set bit 4 and clear bit 5 of obj_flags, then continue at $A91D with A = $FF.

Shared end of the handlers at $A8E0, $A8FA, and $A902. Store A (always $FF here) in obj_move_bits ($3484), clear bits 0, 4, and 6 of obj_state ($3592), clear bits 4 and 5 and set bit 7 of f_35EF, and zero the script position ($379C), the repeat count ($37F0), and the animation index ($3EBC). Bit 4 of obj_state gates the hit box in update_objects and bit 0 gates the animation step at $B585, so both are switched off.
Handler for object type 3: a bare rts, which is also the end of the code at $A91D.

Handler for object type 5. Set obj_flags ($364C) of objects 26 and 27 ($3666 and $3667) to $90, zero their obj_state, script position, and repeat count, set their obj_move_bits to $FF, and set their motion bytes ($32E8 and $32E9) to $36 and $37. Then reset the current object through $A8D8. This probably brings two linked objects into play.

Handler for object type 7. Store $09 in $2D32, $CD in $2D56, and $CE in $2D46 (in the data unpacked once at start-up from entries 12-15, above every stage block; what they hold is unknown), set obj_state of object 51 ($35C5) to $FF, and return.
Handler for object type 8. Set obj_state of object 51 ($35C5) to $FF, clear $48, and set $49 to $64 (the delay and count that the stage routine at $BD76 reads). Then continue at $A8E0.

Dispatches on the phase value in $3427,x: 0 and 6 or higher go to apply_dir_and_speed, 1 to phase1_nudge_y, 2 to phase2_flag_countdown, 3 to phase3_start_arc, 4 to phase4_wait_flag7, and 5 to phase5_substate_dispatch.
Jump stub to apply_dir_and_speed $AB38 for phase 0 and phases 6 or higher.
Jump stub to $AB49 for phase 1.
Jump stub to $AAAE for phase 2.
Jump stub to $AA61 for phase 3.
Phase 4: returns while bit 7 of obj_flags $364C is clear. When set, copies obj_off_y $3748 into $32CE,x and sets the phase $3427,x back to 0.

Phase 5: dispatches on obj_off_x $36F4. Value 0 goes to phase5_substate0_wait_flag7, 1 to phase5_substate1_block_check, 3 to phase5_substate3_countdown, and any other value falls into phase5_substate2_countdown.

Counts down obj_off_y $3748 and returns until it hits zero. Then advances obj_off_x, sets obj_off_y to $0E, masks obj_state $3592 to its low nibble, clears bit 7 of obj_flags $364C, copies $3322,x and $3376,x into obj_y_lo $39A6 and obj_y_hi $3A03, and sets $32CE,x to 2.
Shared RTS.
Counts down obj_off_y $3748 and returns until it hits zero. Then sets bit 4 of obj_state $3592, clears bit 6 of $35EF,x, resets obj_off_x to 0, and sets obj_off_y to 7.
Shared RTS.
Returns while bit 7 of obj_flags $364C is clear. When set, counts down obj_off_y $3748; at zero, reloads it with $4B and joins start_arc_next_substate.

If bit 7 of obj_flags $364C is set, stores $0D in $19. Then calls block_property_at $9400 with A and Y both $0C; when the result ANDed with $43 is zero, returns. Otherwise sets $32CE,x to 1, clears obj_arc_state $3F19, advances obj_off_x $36F4, masks obj_state $3592 to its low nibble, and sets bit 6 of $35EF,x.
Loads $0C into A and Y for the block_property_at $9400 call.
Phase 3: when obj_off_x $36F4 is nonzero, goes to phase3_land_check. When zero, returns unless bit 7 of obj_flags $364C is set, in which case falls into start_arc_next_substate.
Advances obj_off_x $36F4, sets obj_arc_state $3F19 to $C0, and sets obj_arc_counter $3F76 to 1.
Shared RTS.

Stores $0D in $19, then shifts the 16-bit obj_y_hi:obj_y_lo ($3A03:$39A6) right four bits into $E1. When $E1 equals obj_off_y $3748, clears the low four bits of obj_y_lo, clears obj_arc_state $3F19, and masks obj_state $3592 with $81. Returns if the values differ.

Phase 2: saves the top three bits of obj_flags $364C in $E1. With bits 6 and 5 clear, goes to phase2_no_timer_bits. With bit 5 set, goes to phase2_wiggle_y. With only bit 6 set, acts on odd frames of frame_count $08F6 by subtracting 1 from the low nibble of obj_flags; when that borrows, goes to phase2_set_flags_a6.
Shared RTS.
If bit 7 of obj_flags $364C is set, stores $C7 in obj_flags. Otherwise returns.
Stores $A6 in obj_flags $364C.
Shared RTS.

Skips to apply_dir_and_speed when bit 4 of obj_flags $364C is set or frame_count $08F6 is even. Otherwise sets obj_speed $34E1 to 1 and subtracts 1 from the low nibble of obj_flags. On borrow, goes to phase2_wiggle_finish. Else stores the new flags, then bit 0 of the nibble picks decrementing (set) or incrementing (clear) obj_y_lo $39A6, and sets obj_dir $36A0 to $0E or $0D to match.
Sets obj_dir $36A0 to $0E, decrements obj_y_lo $39A6, and jumps to apply_dir_and_speed.
Sets obj_dir $36A0 to $0D, increments obj_y_lo $39A6, and jumps to apply_dir_and_speed.
Stores bit 7 of obj_flags $364C plus $30 back in obj_flags, sets $32CE,x to $FE, obj_arc_state $3F19 to $C0, and obj_arc_counter $3F76 to 0, then falls into apply_dir_and_speed.
When bit 7 of obj_flags $364C is set, copies obj_dir $36A0 to $19 and obj_speed $34E1 to $0295. Otherwise returns without writing.
Phase 1: when bit 7 of obj_flags $364C is set, clears that bit, stores $0D in $19 and 1 in $0295, and adds 2 to obj_y_lo $39A6. When clear, goes to phase1_pull_back_y.
If obj_y_lo $39A6 is below obj_off_x $36F4, returns. Otherwise subtracts 2 from obj_y_lo.
Shared RTS.

Chooses an aim direction (0-9, see aim_dir) for a player standing on a slope. Called with X = slope_kind ($0C) from $9F2B and $AF74, only when slope_kind and stance ($0299) are non-zero; the caller stores A in aim_dir ($0297). Bit 3 of player_facing ($18) set means facing left. Slope kind 2: right gives 3 (down-right), left gives 8 (up-left). Any other kind (1): right gives 1 (up-right), left gives 6 (down-left). So the aim follows the slope's incline (inferred from the codes).

Table handler for index 0 of the table at $B382. Do nothing when bit 7 of f_35EF is set. Otherwise, when player_x ($08B7/$08B8) lies from about $40 pixels left of the object's X ($E7/$E8) to about $18 pixels right of it (the carry is not set explicitly, so the edges may be off by one), jump to $4C9D, which sets bit 7 of f_35EF and swaps the motion byte at $32CE with the one at $3322.

Set the hit box of object X from its new position (E7-EA) and the first four bytes of its current frame's part list (pointer $EB/$EC): left = X + byte 0 into $3BD4/$3C31, top = Y + byte 1 into $3D48/$3DA5, right = X + byte 2 into $3C8E/$3CEB, and bottom = Y + byte 3 into $3E02/$3E5F.

Table handler for index 13. Count down obj_off_y ($3748), used here as a timer. When it reaches zero, reload it with $32 and jump to $4C9D, which sets bit 7 of f_35EF and swaps the motion byte at $32CE with the one at $3322.

Computes the edges of the player's box at the trial position. $EE/$EF is player_try_y ($08BD/$08BE) plus $031C and $031D (vertical offsets, with carry into the high byte). $E5/$E6 is player_try_x ($08BB/$08BC) plus $031A, and $EC/$ED is that plus $031B. It then jumps to $9E17, which starts a loop over the objects counted in $0910 (inferred to be the overlap test against them). Which offset is the box's near edge and which its size is inferred.

Per-frame routine over six slots (X=5 down to 0) whose flag byte $06DD,x has bit 7 set. First, if $08E0 is nonzero and frame_count $08F6 is even, counts $08CD down; at zero this clears $08E0 and copies $B8F8 to $28 and $B8FD to $29 (purpose of $28/$29 unknown). Then masks $40 and $42 to multiples of 8 into $E1 and $E2 (the view position, as used for the on-screen test below).

Active slot: decrements timer $070D,x and deactivates the slot at zero. Otherwise subtracts the view ($E1/$41 for x, $E2/$43 for y) from the slot position ($06E3/$06E9 x, $06EF/$06F5 y); the slot is deactivated unless the result falls inside 40 character columns (x/8 below $28) and 20 rows (y/8 below $14).
Clears the slot flag $06DD,x to 0, then continues with the next slot.

Slot is on screen: Y = row. Builds the screen address in $E3/$E4 from row table $02E8,y/$02FC,y plus the column in $EB and $08C0 (added to the high byte), and the matching colour RAM address in $E5/$E6 (row-table high byte plus $D8). If char_colour_table $0C22 for the character already at that cell has bit 7 set, the slot is deactivated. Otherwise loads the frame list pointer into $E7/$E8 (tables $0398/$039B indexed by $0713,x) and the frame definition pointer into $E9/$EA (list offset $0719,x). Definition byte 0 picks the draw case: 0 is one cell, 1 is two cells, and 2 or more is a 2x2 block.

One-cell case: appends a record to the buffer at $0743 using the index in $0904 (old character, a 0 marker, screen address high/low, colour RAM high), then advances $0904 by 5. Writes definition byte 4 to the screen cell and byte 1 to colour RAM. The code that reads the record buffer back is not in this stretch.

Two-cell case (cells side by side): appends a 6-byte record (two old characters, a 1 marker, screen address high/low, colour RAM high) at $0743 using $0904, then advances $0904 by 6. Writes definition bytes 4 and 5 to the two screen cells and byte 1 to both colour cells.
Common tail after drawing: restores the slot number from $EB. The slot only animates on frames where frame_count $08F6 AND mask $0725,x is zero; otherwise goes to the next slot.
If mask $0725,x is nonzero and $90 is zero, queues sound $18 via queue_sound $0B8C ($90 is sound_queue_count).

Loads the path pointer from $06FB,x/$0701,x into $EB/$EC. Advances the frame offset $0719,x by 2; when it reaches limit $071F,x the offset wraps to 0 if the mask $0725,x is zero, or to $0A if the mask is nonzero. Stores the new offset and reloads the frame definition pointer $E9/$EA from the list at $E7.

Reads a 4-byte step from the path at ($EB) offset $0707,x: adds bytes 0 and 1 to slot x ($06E3/$06E9) and bytes 2 and 3 to slot y ($06EF/$06F5), then stores the new path offset in $0707,x. Step byte value $80 at the start of a step is an end marker: with mask $0725,x nonzero the offset goes back 4 bytes to repeat the previous step, and with mask zero it restarts at offset 0. Finally writes $072B,x/$0731,x (x plus definition byte 2) and $0737,x/$073D,x (y plus definition byte 3); their meaning is unknown, and the adds reuse the carry left by the previous add.

Four-cell (2x2) case: appends an 8-byte record (four old characters, the marker value, screen address high/low, colour RAM high) at $0743 using $0904, then advances $0904 by 8. Writes definition bytes 4, 5, 6, and 7 to the cells at offsets 0, 1, $28, and $29 on the screen, and byte 1 to the same four colour cells.

Pops the saved-background stack and puts the characters back on the screen and their colours into colour RAM. $0904 holds the top of the stack; it does nothing if it is zero. Each record is 5, 6 or 8 bytes ending at offset X in $073B..$0742: a tag in $073F,x (0 = 1 cell, 1 = 2 cells, 2 or more = 2x2 cells), a screen pointer in $0740/$0741 and a colour RAM pointer in $0741/$0742. Each saved character is stored back at the screen address, and its colour is looked up in char_colour_table ($0C22) and stored at the colour RAM address. It loops until the stack is empty, then clears $0904. Pairs with slot_save_draw_1_cell, _2_cells and _4_cells, which push the records; role inferred.

Entry for a one-cell record on the saved-background stack: restores the single character at offset 0 and its colour, then pops 5 bytes from the stack pointer in X (ends the routine if that empties it).

Entry for a two-cell record on the saved-background stack: restores two adjacent characters (offsets 0 and 1) with their colours, then pops 6 bytes; ends via $AF08 when the stack is empty, else loops back to $AE95.

Fire a shot; update_player calls it while fire_flags bit 6 is clear (fire pressed). Nothing while $08FF or player_hit is non-zero. player_mode picks how aim_dir is set. Mode 0 on a slope with stance set uses slope_aim_dir; else on the ground joy_bits up gives 0 (9 when player_facing bit 3 is set), up-right 1, right 2, left 7, up-left 8, and anything else 2 or 7 by the facing ($AFAB-$AFBF, for 3-6, is never reached); in the air only the facing (7 or 2). On the ground it then sets fire_flags and $0903 to $80 and $0902 to $FE. Mode 1 goes to $B16B, mode 2 or more straight on. A shot needs shot_delay bit 7 set: it reloads $08DE/$08DF from weapon record ($28) bytes $14/$15 and fills a free shot slot with bytes $16-$19 (frames left, frame-list end, list type, animation mask), a start at player_third_x/_y + shot_start_offsets (rounded down to 8), a corner 8 further on, and a path from record bytes 2 x aim_dir. weapon_level under 3: one shot, sound $1C (not at 2); 3 up: two ($B088), sound $20.

Jump through a table of handlers indexed by obj_off_x,x: the low bytes are at $B382 and the high bytes at $B3A1 (31 entries). Called from $A2D9 for an object whose obj_flags bit 5 is set and whose obj_state bit 3 is clear. By table index: 0 is $AB8E, 1 is $B3C0, 2 is $B47B, 3 is $B4B3, 6, 10, 20, 21, and 25 share $BD76, 9 is $BDE0, 13 is $AC06, 14 is $B4C4, 18 is $B4C1, and 30 is $BE31. Indexes 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, and 15 point into per-stage RAM ($243A, $23F7, $25E1, $24BA, $2469, and $2705). Indexes 7, 16, 17, 23, 24, and 28 ($BE73, $BF80, $BFCB, $BE91, $BEB3, and $BE8D) lie past the end of the first stage's code at $BE6A and are probably used by the later stages, which load different code from $BD76. Indexes 19 and 27 ($BDBD and $BE34) enter part-way through the routines at $BD76 and $BE31, and indexes 22, 26, and 29 ($BD86, $BD84, and $BE2E) land inside instructions of the first stage's code.

Advance the movement script of object X. The script is found through the stage-block pointers ($36) and ($38) and the position f_379C,x. A byte below $80 is a command: it is looked up in the address tables at $B33C and $B35F and run through $88AF, and a carry means the command has finished, so the script position moves on. A byte with bit 7 set ($B23C) is a move: its low four bits are a direction in the joystick pattern ($0B left, $07 right, $0E up, $0D down, $06, $05, $09, and $0A for the diagonals, where the sideways steps count twice), the next byte is the repeat count (f_37F0,x), and each step adds or subtracts obj_speed ($34E1) on the position in $E7/$E8 and $E9/$EA. Then, when bit 6 of obj_flags is set, it stores the offset from $08DA and $08DC in obj_off_x and obj_off_y. The direction is also kept in obj_dir ($36A0). Called from $A2B4.

Runs one step of an object's movement script. A holds the script byte (low nibble is the direction), X is the object slot. A repeat counter at $37F0,x is loaded from the next script byte when unset and counted down; the direction is stored in obj_dir ($36A0,x) and the object's 16-bit X ($E7/$E8) and Y ($E9/$EA) working position is moved by obj_speed ($34E1,x). Used for enemies and objects on fixed paths.

Stores the direction nibble in obj_dir and dispatches on it: $0B left, $07 right, $06 up-right, $05 down-right, $09 down-left, $0A up-left, $0E up, $0D down; any other value moves up. Diagonals move twice as far horizontally as vertically.
Moves the object left: subtracts obj_speed from its 16-bit X position ($E7/$E8) with borrow.
Moves the object right: adds obj_speed to its 16-bit X position ($E7/$E8) with carry.
Diagonal move up and right: Y ($E9/$EA) decreases by obj_speed, X ($E7/$E8) increases by twice obj_speed.
Diagonal move down and right: Y ($E9/$EA) increases by obj_speed, X ($E7/$E8) increases by twice obj_speed.
Diagonal move down and left: Y ($E9/$EA) increases by obj_speed, X ($E7/$E8) decreases by twice obj_speed.
Diagonal move up and left: Y ($E9/$EA) decreases by obj_speed, X ($E7/$E8) decreases by twice obj_speed.
Moves the object up: subtracts obj_speed from its 16-bit Y position ($E9/$EA). Also the default for unknown direction codes.
Moves the object down: adds obj_speed to its 16-bit Y position ($E9/$EA).

Low bytes of the 35 script command routines that object_script_step runs for a script byte below $80 (index y): 35 bytes $B33C-$B35E. The high bytes are script_cmd_hi. Most targets lie between $B5xx and $B8xx and in $BCxx and $BDxx; command 5 is $0BA0, command $15 is $9150 (path_start_from_record) and command $18 is $4CC7.
High bytes of the 35 script command routines: $B35F-$B381, partner of script_cmd_lo (values $B5 to $B8, $BC and $BD, except command 5 ($0B), command $15 ($91) and command $18 ($4C)).

Low bytes of a second table of 31 routine addresses, $B382-$B3A0, read by object_run_script_handler; the high bytes are in script_cmd2_hi. Indexes 0-3, 13, 14 and 18 are resident code ($AB8E, $B3C0, $B47B, $B4B3, $AC06, $B4C4, $B4C1). The rest are not fixed: $23F7-$2705 (indexes 4, 5, 8, 11, 12, 15) hold data in the saved state, and $BD76 and up are stage code that changes with the stage; some of those targets ($BE73, $BE8D, $BE91, $BEB3, $BF80, $BFCB) lie past the first stage code ($BD76-$BE6A) or inside one of its instructions, so they belong to other stages.
High bytes of the 31 routine addresses of script_cmd2_lo, $B3A1-$B3BF: $AB to $BF, except $23 to $27 for indexes 4, 5, 8, 11, 12 and 15.

Table handler for index 1. While obj_off_y ($3748) is nonzero it counts that down; when it reaches zero it starts a rising arc (obj_arc_counter $30, obj_arc_state $80) and sets obj_anim_num ($33CA) and obj_dir ($36A0) to face the player (0 and $07 when the object is left of player_x + $1F, otherwise 1 and $0B). At other times, with obj_speed ($34E1) nonzero it walks through $B5D5, which moves the object by obj_speed (left when bit 3 of obj_dir is set) and flips bits $0C of obj_dir at a block with property bit 0 beside it or at X 0, and then sets obj_anim_num from that bit. While falling (bit 6 of obj_arc_state) it tests the block under it with block_property_at ($9400), property AND 3: 2 or 3 jumps to $A8FA, 1 lands the object and sets obj_off_y to $0A (the wait before the next hop), and 0 clears bit 0 of obj_state when obj_arc_counter is 7. When bit 6 is clear, bit 0 of obj_state is set while obj_arc_counter is below $10.
Block property 2 or 3: launch the object upward through $A8FA.

Table handler for index 2. Do nothing when bit 7 of obj_kind ($35EF) is set or the animation index ($3EBC) is nonzero, and count obj_off_y ($3748) down when it is nonzero. Otherwise subtract the object's X from player_box_left ($4C/$4D): when bit 3 of $18 is clear, jump to $4C9D if the player is left of the object by 1 to $40, and when it is set, if the player is level with it or right of it by up to $3F (only the low byte of the difference is compared with the limit). Before jumping it sets obj_off_y to $0A. $4C9D sets bit 7 of obj_kind and swaps the motion byte at $32CE with the one at $3322.
Table handler for index 3. Walk sideways through $B5D5, then run object_land_bounce ($B4C4). When that reports a final landing (carry set), set the motion byte ($32CE) to zero.
Table handler for index 18. Walk sideways through $B5D5, then fall into object_land_bounce ($B4C4).

Table handler for index 14, and the second half of indexes 3 and 18. While the object falls (bit 6 of obj_arc_state $3F19), test the block under it with block_property_at ($9400). On a hit, snap the object's Y ($E9/$EA) to a block boundary. If obj_off_y ($3748) is nonzero, it becomes the new obj_arc_counter and is halved, and obj_arc_state is set to $80 so the object bounces up again, with carry clear. Otherwise obj_arc_state is cleared, bit 5 of obj_flags is cleared (so $A2D9 stops calling the table handlers), and carry is set. With no hit, or when the object is not falling, carry is clear.
Bounce: obj_off_y becomes the rise counter and is then halved.
No bounce height left: land for good, and stop the table handler by clearing bit 5 of obj_flags.

Advances one object's animation. X is the object slot. The object's obj_anim_num indexes the pointer tables at ($3A) and ($3C), giving the animation data block in $E5/$E6. If bit 0 of obj_state is set, the per-object delay $3A60,x counts down; when it passes zero it is reloaded from $3535,x and the frame index $3EBC,x goes up by one, wrapping to 0 at the count in the block's first byte.
Alternate entry (no caller found in this range): reloads the data block pointer $E5/$E6 for the object's obj_anim_num without advancing the frame index, then falls into the common code at $B5B2.

Common end: store the frame index, then read that frame's pair of bytes (at offset 5 + 2 x index of the data block) into $3B1A,x and $3B77,x (and copies in $EB/$EC), and set $3ABD,x to $37 minus the block's byte 4 ($38 with sbc and the carry clear). What those fields are drawn from (offsets or sizes) is inferred, not traced.

Count down a timed player effect, once a frame. While player_effect ($08B1) is non-zero, on every second frame it decrements player_effect_timer ($08CE); when that reaches zero it clears player_effect and player_effect_flash ($08B2). While the timer is below $24 it sets bit 7 of player_effect_flash from bit 0 of the timer, so the flag toggles with each tick. player_pose uses the flag (bit 7 of $08B2) to change the third sprite's colour to $0E and its shape number, and the contact code at $A5A7 tests bit 7 of $08B1. The routine at $0BBE starts it: it queues sound 8 and sets $08B1 and $08B2 to $FF and the timer to $E0 (448 frames); init_round_state clears it at $4EF5. It is probably an invulnerability or power-up timer.

Low bytes of the addresses of the five weapon records, indexed by the number in $3322,x of the weapon item: $C9, $E3, $02, $FD and $2B. The pick-up handler at $A83C copies the pair into weapon_ptr ($28/$29) and stores the number in $08E0.
High bytes of the five weapon record addresses ($B9 each), so the records are at $B9C9, $B9E3, $B902, $B9FD and $B92B.
Raster interrupt at line $DE: after a short delay, $D011 = $17 turns the black mode off, so the status panel shows from here (24 rows).

Converts the five score digit tiles ($08D0-$08D4) to plain digit values (tile minus $C1) and stores them at $FFF5-$FFF9. Called from round_start at $8075 when the lives count has run out, just before the jump to title_entry ($4000), and from stage_intro_start at $4057 when the stage number has reached 5, just before the jump to game_start. What reads the stored digits is not established here, so the name is neutral. The zero bytes after the final return at $BD6C onward are padding.

Table handler for indexes 6, 10, 20, 21, and 25. The code at $BD76 and above is stage code loaded from the cartridge, and this description covers the code present in the snapshot, the first stage. When $49 with bit 7 masked off is zero it does nothing. Otherwise that value is the index Y, and $48 counts down; at zero, $49 is decremented and $48 reloaded with 5, and the entries at index Y + $47 of the object arrays are filled in: for example $3F60 is obj_arc_state plus $47, set to $80, with obj_arc_counter $10, obj_state $D0, obj_flags $20, obj_off_y $AC, and y $0016. If bit 7 of $49 is clear, obj_dir is $07, X is $01A8, and the frame is 0. Otherwise obj_dir is $0B, X is $02F0, and the frame is 1. It is started by object type 8 ($A981), which sets $49 to $64.

Table handler for index 9, in the stage code of the first stage. Count down obj_off_y ($3748). At zero, set obj_state to $FF and stop. Otherwise move the object's X ($E7/$E8) by 4, left when bit 3 of obj_dir ($36A0) is set and right when clear. While it falls (bit 6 of obj_arc_state) and (Y + $15) AND $0C is zero, it tests the block under it with block_property_at ($9400) and on a hit starts a new rise (obj_arc_state $80, obj_arc_counter $30). It is probably the handler for the objects that $BD76 creates, which have obj_off_y $AC and a direction of $07 or $0B.

Table handler for index 30, in the stage code of the first stage. Take the object's Y minus $15 ($E9) and, for each of objects 27, 28, and 29 whose obj_state bit 0 is set ($35AD, $35AE, and $35AF), store it in their obj_y_lo ($39C1-$39C3) and store the low byte of the object's X ($E7) plus $18, $08, and $3E in their obj_x_lo ($3907-$3909). There is no clc, so a sum is one more when the carry is set; for the first that is when Y is $15 or more. This places three attached objects relative to this one.

Byte patched to $19 by stage3_patch (with $00 at $BF23, $01 at $BF24 and $00 at $BF25). Zero in the saved stage 0 state; this lies in the part of the stage code area that other stages fill.
